title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
嘉靖甲午廣東復當鄉試維
時巡按監察御史戴璟飭材
考役備物脩禮著令甲焉乃
聘德洪暨教諭張槩為考試
官學正𡩋元伯教諭謝恒紀
穆曾茂卿黃梅余拱北訓導
===
王寵為同考試官提調維左
布政使王俊民參政劉雍監
試維按察使柴經僉事王崇
百執事則知府鄒守愚史立
模而下皆慎選也先試期三
日入院既入凡閈閎階序之
制鐘鼓旗布之設巡者瞭者
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

嘉靖甲午，廣東復當鄉試。維時巡按監察御史戴璟飭材考役，備物脩禮，著令甲焉。乃聘德洪暨教諭張槩為考試官，學正𡩋元伯、教諭謝恒、紀穆、曾茂卿、黃梅、余拱北、訓導王寵為同考試官。提調維左布政使王俊民、參政劉雍，監試維按察使柴經、僉事王崇。百執事則知府鄒守愚、史立模而下，皆慎選也。先試期三日入院。既入，凡閈閎階序之制，鐘鼓旗布之設，巡者、瞭者、
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the jiawu year of Jiajing (1534), Guangdong was again due to hold its Provincial Examination. At that time, Dai Jing, the Investigating Censor on regional inspection, ordered the preparation of materials and reviewed service assignments, supplied the necessary articles, put the ceremonial arrangements in order, and set down regulations. He then invited Dehong and Instructor Zhang Gai to serve as Examiners; School Instructor Ning Yuanbo, Instructors Xie Heng, Ji Mu, Zeng Maoqing, Huang Mei, and Yu Gongbei, and Assistant Instructor Wang Chong to serve as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Junmin and Administration Vice Commissioner Liu Yong; those overseeing the examination were Surveillance Commissioner Chai Jing and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Chong. All personnel, from Prefects Zou Shouyu and Shi Limo downward, were carefully selected.

We entered the examination compound three days before the examination date. Once inside, everything—the arrangement of gates, steps, and halls; the provision of bells, drums, and flags [?]; the patrolmen and lookouts…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詰者衛者具飱餼者監灌燎
者司扃鑰者掌聲節者督禦
嗛者畢備而聽命焉御史遂
率簾內外以矢曰薦士
國之大者其有比于私慝以干
彝典明神殛之德洪亦屬衆
曰凡有二心有如此矢已乃
===
進提學僉事田汝成所簡士
一千八百有奇而三試之掣
書授目杜關節也更番校閱
致詳愼也黜落浮怪正體習
也錄中式者七十有五人以
獻錄成德洪當僭言首簡嘗讀粤
方輿誌及唐人書有曰中州
punctuated:
詰者、衛者、具飱餼者、監灌燎者、司扃鑰者、掌聲節者、督禦嗛者，畢備而聽命焉。御史遂率簾內外以矢曰：「薦士，國之大者。其有比于私慝以干彝典，明神殛之！」德洪亦屬衆曰：「凡有二心，有如此矢！」已乃進提學僉事田汝成所簡士一千八百有奇，而三試之。掣書授目，杜關節也；更番校閱，致詳愼也；黜落浮怪，正體習也。錄中式者七十有五人以獻。
錄成，德洪當僭言首簡。嘗讀《粤方輿誌》及唐人書，有曰：「中州
translation_en:
…those responsible for questioning and guarding, those providing meals and provisions, those supervising watering and burning [?], those keeping the locks and keys, those managing audible signals, and those overseeing provisions [?] were all in place and awaited orders. The censor then led the staff serving inside and outside the examination curtain in an oath, saying: “Recommending men of worth is a great affair of state. Should anyone collude in private wrongdoing and violate the established statutes, may the luminous spirits strike him down!” Dehong likewise enjoined the assembled staff: “Should anyone harbor divided loyalties, may he fare like this arrow!”
They then admitted the more than eighteen hundred candidates selected by Tian Rucheng, the education intendant holding the rank of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and examined them in three sessions. Lots were drawn and topics assigned to prevent clandestine dealings; papers were reviewed in rotation to ensure thoroughness and care; frivolous and eccentric writing was rejected to rectify literary styles and habits. Seventy-five successful candidates were entered on a list for submission.
When the record was completed, it fell to Dehong to presume to offer some words on its opening leaves. I once read in the Geographical Gazetteer of Yue and in writings by men of the Tang a statement that says: “The central provinces …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
清淑之氣至嶺而窮又曰陽
德炳燿獨發於紛葩瑰麗之
物而罕鍾於人愚謂理誠有
之造化精華必有所寓不在
人必在物蓋是時文命未敷
故天地之氣尚有所限際耳
自我
===
皇明以來賢達之出比之中土非
獨盛於科甲而一代文學之
宗傑然為天下倡故至今天
下士樂得師資者未嘗不為
茲土之士慶也今幸盡讀多
士之文師友淵源固知所自
然拘於數不可盡錄則知樂
punctuated:
「清淑之氣至嶺而窮。」又曰：「陽德炳燿，獨發於紛葩瑰麗之物，而罕鍾於人。」愚謂理誠有之，造化精華必有所寓，不在人必在物。蓋是時文命未敷，故天地之氣尚有所限際耳。
自我皇明以來，賢達之出，比之中土，非獨盛於科甲，而一代文學之宗，傑然為天下倡。故至今天下士樂得師資者，未嘗不為茲土之士慶也。今幸盡讀多士之文，師友淵源，固知所自。然拘於數，不可盡錄，則知樂
translation_en:
…“The pure and harmonious vital force reaches the mountains and is exhausted.” It also says: “The radiant power of yang manifests itself only in things of abundant blossoms and extraordinary beauty, and seldom gathers in human beings.” In my humble view, there is indeed such a principle: the essence of creation must find a dwelling; if not in people, then necessarily in things. At that time, the civilizing influence had not yet spread widely, so the vital force of Heaven and Earth still had its limits.
Since the founding of our august Ming dynasty, the emergence of worthy and accomplished men here has rivaled that of the central regions. Their distinction has not been confined to success in the examinations: leading masters of literary learning in our age have stood preeminent as exemplars for all under Heaven. Thus, even today, scholars throughout the realm who rejoice in finding such teachers invariably congratulate the scholars of this land. Now I have had the good fortune to read all these candidates’ writings, and I can clearly discern the sources of their learning in the traditions transmitted by teachers and friends. Yet, constrained by the quota, we cannot admit them all. I thus know that the joy …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
育於時以俟將來者未艾也
是非
國家文教誕敷蟠天極地而精
氣所萃無遠弗屆故魁瓌奇
麗不稱諸物而獨于人也則
夫諸士子生斯時者不大可
自慶耶雖然天地之氣鍾於
===
物則誠物爾矣鍾於人則誠
人爾矣蓋未嘗有所矯飾其
間也丹砂大貝鍾乳石英合
浦之珠博羅之龜可以實包
篚可以薦
宗廟皆誠物也諸士子之生既得
淑氣所鍾矣則其發爲文章
punctuated: 育於時，以俟將來者未艾也。是非國家文教誕敷，蟠天極地，而精氣所萃，無遠弗屆，故魁瓌奇麗不稱諸物而獨于人也？則夫諸士子生斯時者，不大可自慶耶？雖然，天地之氣鍾於物，則誠物爾矣；鍾於人，則誠人爾矣。蓋未嘗有所矯飾其間也。丹砂、大貝、鍾乳、石英、合浦之珠、博羅之龜，可以實包篚，可以薦宗廟，皆誠物也。諸士子之生，既得淑氣所鍾矣，則其發爲文章
translation_en:
…those being nurtured in this age to await their future opportunities are still coming forth without end. Is this not because the state's civilizing instruction spreads abundantly, encompassing heaven and reaching the ends of the earth, so that nowhere is too distant for its concentrated vital essence to reach—and thus grandeur, magnificence, rarity, and beauty are predicated not of things but uniquely of people? Should not the scholars born in this age greatly congratulate themselves?

Nevertheless, when the vital energy of heaven and earth concentrates in things, they are simply genuine things; when it concentrates in people, they are simply genuine people. There has never been any contrivance or embellishment involved. Cinnabar, great cowrie shells, stalactite, quartz, pearls from Hepu, and tortoises from Boluo can fill tribute parcels and baskets and be presented in the ancestral temple: all are genuine things. Since these scholars at birth have received a concentration of auspicious vital energy, then, when it finds expression in their literary compositions…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也果皆陽德之炳燿乎抑未
免有所矯乎孔子曰脩辭立
其誠所以居業也其言如是
其心如是者謂之誠其心未
然其言則然者謂之矯矯則
僞矣天以誠與人以僞喪是
棄天也有志者所必不爲也
===
夫誠與矯惟知道者能察之
而德洪則非其人也然則將
若之何諸士子亦自察之而
已矣夫物不貴華貴適於用
文不貴華貴適於道君子之
道得之於心而樂措之於家
國天下而順傳之於後世而
punctuated:
也，果皆陽德之炳燿乎？抑未免有所矯乎？孔子曰：「脩辭立其誠，所以居業也。」其言如是，其心如是者，謂之誠；其心未然，其言則然者，謂之矯。矯則僞矣。天以誠與，人以僞喪，是棄天也，有志者所必不爲也。
夫誠與矯，惟知道者能察之，而德洪則非其人也。然則將若之何？諸士子亦自察之而已矣。夫物不貴華，貴適於用；文不貴華，貴適於道。君子之道，得之於心而樂，措之於家國天下而順，傳之於後世而
translation_en:
…when expressed in literary composition, is it indeed all a radiant manifestation of yang virtue? Or is it still not free from affectation? Confucius said: “Refining one’s words to establish sincerity is the means of abiding in one’s undertaking.” When one’s words are thus and one’s heart is likewise, this is called sincerity; when one’s heart is not so, yet one’s words claim that it is, this is called affectation. Affectation is falsity. Heaven bestows through sincerity, but people lose its gift through falsity: this is to abandon Heaven, something those with resolve would certainly never do.
Only those who understand the Way can discern sincerity and affectation, and I, Dehong, am not such a person. What, then, is to be done? You examination candidates must simply examine yourselves. Things are valued not for their splendor but for their fitness for use; writing is valued not for its splendor but for its accord with the Way. The Way of the gentleman, when grasped in the heart, brings joy; when put into practice in the family, the state, and all under Heaven, brings harmony; when transmitted to later generations…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
尊其出也有源其流也不息
其凝也不朽誠也誠於物者
以形用誠於人者以神用神
用者不朽形用者敝矯而偽
則天之與我者先自刓敝雖
有此心其神不凝君子所貴
夫誠不敢矯焉以偽為者惡
===
自敝也詩曰靡不有初鮮克
有終諸士子既得於天是有
初矣愼無自敝以克厥終則
國家之文教益弘而所謂為天
下倡者當益光而彌大此又
國家之慶也夫豈徒諸士子之
福司考校者亦與有賴焉諸
punctuated: 尊。其出也有源，其流也不息，其凝也不朽，誠也。誠於物者以形用，誠於人者以神用。神用者不朽，形用者敝。矯而偽，則天之與我者先自刓敝，雖有此心，其神不凝。君子所貴夫誠，不敢矯焉以偽為者，惡自敝也。《詩》曰：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」諸士子既得於天，是有初矣。愼無自敝，以克厥終，則國家之文教益弘，而所謂為天下倡者，當益光而彌大。此又國家之慶也，夫豈徒諸士子之福？司考校者亦與有賴焉。諸
translation_en: …is held in honor. Its emergence has a source; its flow never ceases; what it brings to fruition does not perish: this is sincerity. Sincerity in things operates through physical form; sincerity in human beings operates through spirit. What operates through spirit does not perish; what operates through physical form wears out. If one resorts to contrivance and falsehood, one first wears away what Heaven has bestowed upon oneself. Though one possesses this mind, its spirit does not become firmly established. The gentleman values sincerity and dares not act with contrivance and falsehood because he abhors wearing himself away. The Book of Odes says: “None fails to make a beginning; few can achieve an ending.” You scholars have already received your endowment from Heaven, and thus have made a beginning. Take care not to wear yourselves away, so that you may carry matters through to the end. Then the state's literary and moral instruction will spread still further, and what is called setting an example for all under Heaven will become ever more illustrious and expansive. This, too, will be a blessing for the state. How could it be a benefit only to you scholars? Those charged with examining and evaluating you will likewise have something upon which to rely. All …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
士子其慎圖之是舉也維提
督侍郎兼都御史陶諧都御
史陳察總兵咸寧侯仇鸞皆
懋宣
威靈奠綏南服故士有寧宇得肆
學以待問先任左布政使今
光禄卿王學夔脩廢振敝懋
===
經畧以光重
令典叅政朱珮叅議劉勲洪異
陳端甫副使游璉鄧鋐僉事
黃澄陳大珊吳大本吳玭江
匯叅將程鑒都指揮僉事陳
松武鸞則皆賛襄防範與有
勞也茲不可以不書
punctuated: 士子其慎圖之！是舉也，維提督侍郎兼都御史陶諧、都御史陳察、總兵咸寧侯仇鸞，皆懋宣威靈，奠綏南服，故士有寧宇，得肆學以待問。先任左布政使、今光禄卿王學夔，脩廢振敝，懋經畧以光重令典。叅政朱珮，叅議劉勲、洪異、陳端甫，副使游璉、鄧鋐，僉事黃澄、陳大珊、吳大本、吳玭、江匯，叅將程鑒，都指揮僉事陳松、武鸞，則皆賛襄防範，與有勞也。茲不可以不書。
translation_en: …Let the students consider this carefully! For this examination, Tao Xie, Vice Minister and concurrently Censor-in-Chief charged with overall supervision; Chen Cha, Censor-in-Chief; and Qiu Luan, Regional Commander and Marquis of Xianning, all diligently extended imperial authority and prestige, securing and pacifying the southern domains. Thus the students had peaceful surroundings in which to devote themselves to study and prepare to be questioned. Wang Xuekui, formerly Left Provincial Administration Commissioner and now Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, restored what had fallen into disuse and remedied what had deteriorated, diligently undertaking arrangements to enhance the distinction and dignity of this excellent institution. Zhu Pei, Administration Vice Commissioner; Liu Xun, Hong Yi, and Chen Duanfu, Administration Assistant Commissioners; You Lian and Deng Hong, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Huang Cheng, Chen Dashan, Wu Daben, Wu Pin, and Jiang Hui, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Cheng Jian, Regional Vice Commander; and Chen Song and Wu Luan, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, all assisted with protective and preventive measures and shared in the work. Their contributions cannot go unrecorded.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
直隸蘇州府儒學教授錢德
洪謹序
punctuated: 直隸蘇州府儒學教授錢德洪謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully composed by Qian Dehong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Suzhou Prefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史戴璟〔孟光浙江奉化縣人丙戌進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使王俊民〔用章湖廣石首縣人甲戌進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政劉雍〔堯臣山東昌樂縣人丁丑進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使柴經〔季常浙江鄞縣人丁丑進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事王崇〔仲德浙江永康縣人己丑進士〕
===
考試官
直隸蘇州府儒學教授錢德洪〔洪甫浙江餘姚縣人壬辰進士〕
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學教諭張槩〔孔瞻福建侯官縣人戊子貢士〕
同考試官
河南彰德府磁州儒學學正甯元伯〔仁甫湖廣衡陽縣人戊子貢士〕

punctuated:
嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史戴璟〔孟光，浙江奉化縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使王俊民〔用章，湖廣石首縣人，甲戌進士〕。
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政劉雍〔堯臣，山東昌樂縣人，丁丑進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使柴經〔季常，浙江鄞縣人，丁丑進士〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事王崇〔仲德，浙江永康縣人，己丑進士〕。

考試官：
直隸蘇州府儒學教授錢德洪〔洪甫，浙江餘姚縣人，壬辰進士〕。
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學教諭張槩〔孔瞻，福建侯官縣人，戊子貢士〕。

同考試官：
河南彰德府磁州儒學學正甯元伯〔仁甫，湖廣衡陽縣人，戊子貢士〕。
浙江湖州府烏程縣儒學教諭謝恒〔惟一，江西新淦縣人，壬午貢士〕。
浙江處州府遂昌縣儒學教諭紀穆〔希文，江西永豐縣人，壬午貢士〕。

translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, the thirteenth year of Jiajing (1534)

Supervising Official:
Dai Jing, Regional Inspector of Guangdong serving as Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Mengguang and was a native of Fenghua County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.

Proctors:
Wang Junmin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Yongzhang and was a native of Shishou County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.
Liu Yong, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Yaochen and was a native of Changle County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Examination Monitors:
Chai Jing, Surveillance Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Jichang and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Wang Chong, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Zhongde and was a native of Yongkang County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫仁者己欲立而立人己欲達而達人能
近取譬可謂仁之方也已
誠者自成也而道自道也
存其心養其性所以事天也
易
觀乎天文以察時變觀乎人文以化成天
下
===
當位以節中正以通
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
精義入神以致用也
書
慎厥身脩思永惇叙九族庶明勵翼邇可
遠在茲禹拜昌言曰俞
惟天聰明惟聖時憲
凡厥庶民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

夫仁者，己欲立而立人，己欲達而達人。能近取譬，可謂仁之方也已。

誠者，自成也；而道，自道也。

存其心，養其性，所以事天也。

易

觀乎天文，以察時變；觀乎人文，以化成天下。

當位以節，中正以通。

夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

精義入神，以致用也。

書

慎厥身，脩思永，惇叙九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠在茲。禹拜昌言，曰：「俞！」

惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。

凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The benevolent person, wishing to establish himself, establishes others; wishing to attain success himself, enables others to attain success. To draw analogies from what is close at hand may be called the method of benevolence.

Sincerity is that by which one completes oneself; the Way is that by which one guides oneself.

Preserving one's heart and nourishing one's nature are the means of serving Heaven.

Book of Changes

Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern the changes of the seasons; observe the patterns of human culture to transform and bring the world to completion.

Occupying the proper position, one exercises restraint; through centrality and correctness, one achieves free passage.

The Changes is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and broaden their undertakings. Knowledge is lofty; ritual propriety is lowly. The lofty emulates Heaven; the lowly models itself on Earth.

Refining one's understanding of what is right until one enters the realm of the numinous serves to bring it into practical use.

Book of Documents

Be watchful over your person; cultivate yourself with thought for the long term. Maintain affectionate and orderly relations among the nine degrees of kinship. Let the many enlightened men exert themselves in assisting you. The possibility of extending your influence from near to far lies in this. Yu bowed in acknowledgment of these excellent words and said, “Yes!”

Heaven hears and sees clearly; the sage takes this as his model.

As for all the common people, they are to take the promulgated words of the Supreme Standard as their instruction and put them into practice, so as to draw near to the Son of Heaven's …

春秋
春鄭人來輸平隱公六年
冬鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳襄公二十有五年
叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋
向戍衛齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭
罕虎許人曹人于虢昭公元年
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
戚襄公五年
punctuated:
之光。我咸成文王功于不怠，丕冒海隅出日，罔不率俾。

詩
彼茁者葭，壹發五豝，于嗟乎騶虞！彼茁者蓬，壹發五豵，于嗟乎騶虞！樂只君子，邦家之基；樂只君子，萬壽無期。昭明有融，高朗令終。赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈。

春秋
春，鄭人來輸平。隱公六年。
冬，鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳。襄公二十有五年。
叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戍、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。昭公元年。
公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚。襄公五年。
translation_en:
…the radiance [of the Son of Heaven]. Let us all complete King Wen’s work without flagging, extending its protection far over the coastal regions where the sun rises, so that none fail to follow and obey.

Book of Odes
Those luxuriant reeds! One discharge of the bow, five sows! Ah, the zouyu! Those luxuriant clumps of mugwort! One discharge of the bow, five young boars! Ah, the zouyu!
Joyful is the noble man, the foundation of the state and its ruling house. Joyful is the noble man; may his life last ten thousand years without end.
His brilliant virtue shines far; lofty and radiant, he brings matters to a good conclusion.
Illustrious is his renown; resplendent is his spiritual power.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In spring, men of Zheng came to offer peace. Sixth year of Duke Yin.
In winter, Gongsun Xia of Zheng led an army against Chen. Twenty-fifth year of Duke Xiang.
Shusun Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Shu [?] of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao. First year of Duke Zhao.
The duke met at Qi with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, and representatives of Wu and Zeng. Fifth year of Duke Xiang.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
冬楚子蔡侯陳侯許男頓子沈子徐人越
人伐吳昭公五年
禮記
朝諸侯分職授政任功曰予一人
天子以德爲車以樂爲御
天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣流而不
息合同而化而樂興焉
樂而毋荒有禮而親威莊而安孝慈而敬
使民有父之尊有母之親如此而后可
===
以爲民父母矣非至德其孰能如此乎
第貳塲
論
上下與天地同流
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢以諸儒講五經同異詔甘露三年
擬唐以同州刺史姚元之爲兵部尚書同
中書門下三品誥開元元年
擬宋曾鞏謝賜唐六典表元豐五年
punctuated:
冬，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、沈子、徐人、越人伐吳。昭公五年。

禮記
朝諸侯，分職授政任功，曰予一人。
天子以德爲車，以樂爲御。
天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣；流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。
樂而毋荒，有禮而親，威莊而安，孝慈而敬，使民有父之尊，有母之親，如此而后可以爲民父母矣。非至德，其孰能如此乎？

第貳塲
論
上下與天地同流。

詔誥表內科一道
擬漢以諸儒講五經同異詔。甘露三年。
擬唐以同州刺史姚元之爲兵部尚書、同中書門下三品誥。開元元年。
擬宋曾鞏謝賜唐六典表。元豐五年。
translation_en:
In winter, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Baron of Xu 許, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Shen, and men of Xu 徐 and Yue attacked Wu. Fifth year of Duke Zhao.

Book of Rites
When receiving the regional lords at court, distributing offices, conferring administrative responsibilities, and entrusting undertakings, he calls himself “I, the One Man.”
The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his carriage and music as his charioteer.
Heaven is high and earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct, and the ordering of ritual operates. They flow without ceasing, unite in harmony and undergo transformation, and music arises.
Be joyful without excess, observe ritual while remaining affectionate, be dignified and stately yet at ease, and be filial and loving yet reverent. Enable the people to feel the respect due to a father and the affection due to a mother. Only then can one become father and mother to the people. Without consummate virtue, who could accomplish this?

Second Session
Discourse
Above and below, sharing in the same flow as Heaven and Earth.

One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor directing the Confucian scholars to discuss agreements and differences in the Five Classics. Third year of Ganlu.
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Yao Yuanzhi, Prefect of Tongzhou, as Minister of War and Participant in the Administration (tong Zhongshu Menxia sanpin). First year of Kaiyuan.
Compose a memorial in the voice of Zeng Gong of the Song, expressing thanks for the gift of the Six Statutes of the Tang (Tang liudian). Fifth year of Yuanfeng.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
判語五條
擅離職役
別籍異財
服舍違式
私賣戰馬
偽造寶鈔
第參場
策五道
問帝王之學以正心為要唐虞三代所同
===
也故盛德大業垂範無窮焉自漢而降
此學不明雖或石渠詔講弘文引士清
心貯籍奎章置員要皆彌文無益于用
此治之所以不古若也洪惟我
祖宗天啓
聖神纘千載不傳之緒蓋嘗莊誦
觀心亭記擬問心道衡說題暮雪雙禽圖曁
明鏡止水之喻製筆自怠之規金獅安危之
戒眞有以上契帝王心學精蘊而超出
punctuated:
判語五條：擅離職役；別籍異財；服舍違式；私賣戰馬；偽造寶鈔。

第參場
策五道
問：帝王之學，以正心為要，唐虞三代所同也，故盛德大業，垂範無窮焉。自漢而降，此學不明，雖或石渠詔講、弘文引士、清心貯籍、奎章置員，要皆彌文，無益于用，此治之所以不古若也。洪惟我祖宗，天啓聖神，纘千載不傳之緒。蓋嘗莊誦《觀心亭記》《擬問心》《道衡說》《題暮雪雙禽圖》，曁明鏡止水之喻、製筆自怠之規、金獅安危之戒，眞有以上契帝王心學精蘊，而超出
translation_en:
Five topics for legal judgments: leaving one’s official post or assigned service without authorization; establishing a separate household registration and dividing family property; clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed regulations; privately selling warhorses; counterfeiting paper currency.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The learning of emperors and kings takes rectifying the mind as its essential concern. This was common to the rulers of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties; hence their flourishing virtue and great achievements provided models for all time. From the Han onward, this learning ceased to be clearly understood. Although there were imperially ordered discussions at the Shiqu Pavilion, scholars recruited to the Hongwen Academy, books stored in the Qingxin Hall, and personnel appointed to the Kuizhang Pavilion, these were ultimately mere elaborations of ceremony, without practical benefit. This is why government failed to equal that of antiquity.

We reverently reflect that our imperial ancestors, whose sagely wisdom Heaven inspired, continued a tradition that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years. We have reverently recited the Record of the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind, An Imagined Questioning of the Mind, A Discourse on the Balance of the Way, and Inscription on a Painting of Two Birds in Evening Snow, together with the analogy of a bright mirror and still water, the admonition concerning making a writing brush and one’s own indolence [?], and the warning concerning the golden lion and security and peril. These truly accord with the profound essence of the ancient emperors’ and kings’ learning of the mind, and surpass…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
歷代諸君萬萬矣
聖謨具在可得而敬述耶
皇上法
祖憲聖日躋盛隆心學之傳仰見追美
先德凌駕百王久矣其見於
聖製如
祖德詩
穀祗蠶壇賦
平臺召見集固皆
===
睿藻宸章秘之
天府非草茅疏遠者所可盡見然
敬一箴五箴則已
昭啓維則頒四方矣諸士子有能覽悟其
玄微者耶抑或有芹曝之
獻以賛揚
休烈於萬一耶願悉著之以觀子格心之學
問六經之道同歸而禮樂之用為急班孟
堅有是言也不知若何急於六經耶歐
punctuated:
歷代諸君萬萬矣！聖謨具在，可得而敬述耶？皇上法祖憲聖，日躋盛隆，心學之傳，仰見追美先德，凌駕百王久矣。其見於聖製，如《祖德詩》《穀祗蠶壇賦》《平臺召見集》，固皆睿藻宸章，秘之天府，非草茅疏遠者所可盡見。然《敬一箴》《五箴》，則已昭啓維則，頒四方矣。諸士子有能覽悟其玄微者耶？抑或有芹曝之獻，以賛揚休烈於萬一耶？願悉著之，以觀子格心之學。
問：六經之道同歸，而禮樂之用為急，班孟堅有是言也。不知若何急於六經耶？歐
translation_en:
…surpassing the rulers of successive ages ten thousand times over! These sagely counsels are all preserved: might you reverently expound them? His Majesty models himself on his ancestors and follows the sages, daily ascending to greater flourishing. In the transmission of the learning of the mind, we have long looked up to him as matching the excellence of his forebears’ virtue and surpassing the hundred kings. Its manifestations in his imperial writings, such as Poems on Ancestral Virtue, Rhapsody on the Grain Deity and Sericulture Altars [?], and Collection of Audiences at the Platform, are indeed works of imperial literary brilliance, kept in the imperial repositories. Those of humble station, remote from court, cannot see them all. Yet the Admonition on Reverent Oneness and the Five Admonitions have already clearly disclosed the guiding standards and been promulgated throughout the realm. Are there any among you candidates who have read them and grasped their subtle profundities? Or might you offer some humble contribution—as one offering celery or the warmth of the sun—to help extol even a ten-thousandth part of his glorious achievements? Set it all down, so that we may observe your learning in rectifying the ruler’s mind.
Question: The Way of the Six Classics converges upon the same end, but the practical application of rites and music is most urgent. Ban Mengjian made this statement. In what sense, then, does this take precedence within the Six Classics? Ou…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
陽氏謂三代而上治出於一而禮樂達
於天下三代而下治出於二而禮樂爲
虚名亦古今不易之論矣而又何所指
耶及考董仲舒劉向皆以庠序爲禮樂
之原而太史公以刑措爲禮樂所由起
然則出於一者何道耶夫周官一書禮
之綱領固然矣而又謂儀禮爲本經禮
記爲義説可得而歷數歟世之疑周禮
者不止一何休也皆不知周公致太平
===
之書也而王荆公諸人崇信之又何以
取敗歟漢之禮製於叔孫通及曹褒唐
有顯慶開元等禮宋有開寶政和禮至
於漢有制氏李延年京房之所較定唐
有祖孝孫顏師古之所奏議宋有和胡
阮李范馬諸人之建白其儀文音節亦
備矣而率不免爲虚名何歟後之論禮
樂者類曰文公家禮庶幾古人脩身齊
家之道而以何者爲之本歟蔡氏新書
punctuated: 陽氏謂三代而上，治出於一，而禮樂達於天下；三代而下，治出於二，而禮樂爲虚名。亦古今不易之論矣，而又何所指耶？及考董仲舒、劉向，皆以庠序爲禮樂之原，而太史公以刑措爲禮樂所由起。然則出於一者，何道耶？夫《周官》一書，禮之綱領固然矣，而又謂《儀禮》爲本經，《禮記》爲義説，可得而歷數歟？世之疑《周禮》者，不止一何休也，皆不知周公致太平之書也。而王荆公諸人崇信之，又何以取敗歟？漢之禮製於叔孫通及曹褒，唐有顯慶、開元等禮，宋有開寶、政和禮。至於漢有制氏、李延年、京房之所較定，唐有祖孝孫、顏師古之所奏議，宋有和、胡、阮、李、范、馬諸人之建白，其儀文音節亦備矣，而率不免爲虚名，何歟？後之論禮樂者類曰：《文公家禮》，庶幾古人脩身齊家之道。而以何者爲之本歟？蔡氏《新書》
translation_en:
…Master Ouyang maintained that in the Three Dynasties and earlier, government issued from a single source, and rites and music extended throughout the realm; after the Three Dynasties, government issued from two sources, and rites and music became empty names. This, too, is a judgment valid for all time; but what precisely does it refer to? On examining Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang, we find that both regarded schools as the source of rites and music, whereas the Grand Historian regarded the setting aside of punishments as the circumstance from which rites and music arose. By what Way, then, did government issue from a single source? The Offices of Zhou certainly provides the guiding framework for ritual. Yet it is also said that the Ceremonies and Rites is the foundational classic, and the Record of Rites an exposition of its meaning. Can these matters be enumerated in detail? He Xiu was by no means the only person to doubt the Rites of Zhou: all such critics failed to recognize it as the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about great peace. Yet when Wang, Duke of Jing, and others revered and trusted it, why did they meet with failure?

The Han ritual system was fashioned by Shusun Tong and Cao Bao. The Tang had the ritual codes of the Xianqing and Kaiyuan eras, among others; the Song had those of the Kaibao and Zhenghe eras. As for music, under the Han there were the collation and determination undertaken by Master Zhi, Li Yannian, and Jing Fang; under the Tang, the proposals submitted by Zu Xiaosun and Yan Shigu; and under the Song, the recommendations of He, Hu, Ruan, Li, Fan, Ma, and others. Their ceremonial forms and musical measures were indeed comprehensive, yet they generally could not escape becoming empty names. Why was this? Later writers on rites and music commonly say that Master Wengong’s Family Rituals comes close to the ancients’ Way of cultivating oneself and regulating one’s family. But what serves as its foundation? Master Cai’s New Book…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
黃鐘圍徑之數變律半聲之例五聲二
變之則亦精矣而所謂聲氣之元果求
之黍尺葭莩之間歟抑别有說歟禮樂
之難言久矣不知朱蔡二書可與周禮
若是班歟諸士子悉心以對毋曰夫我
則不暇
問文者治之精華道之枝葉也聖賢何意
於為文哉其所以明道紀事宣上達下
如菽粟水火之在人世不可一日缺焉
===
者議者乃謂三代無文人六經無文法
何耶後世以文章為事業汲汲乎弊精
神以求見於世亦已勞矣卒未聞有追
古作抑又何耶或者曰學文之道急於
明理明理果謂學文而急乎或者曰文
章以體製為先則大誥繫辭諸書又何
所法程乎或者又曰文章與時高下三
代之文至戰國而病涉秦漢復起漢之
文至三國而病唐興復起夫戰國秦漢
punctuated:
黃鐘圍徑之數、變律半聲之例、五聲二變之則，亦精矣，而所謂聲氣之元，果求之黍尺葭莩之間歟？抑别有說歟？禮樂之難言久矣，不知朱蔡二書可與周禮若是班歟？諸士子悉心以對，毋曰夫我則不暇。
問：文者，治之精華，道之枝葉也。聖賢何意於為文哉？其所以明道紀事、宣上達下，如菽粟水火之在人世，不可一日缺焉者，議者乃謂三代無文人、六經無文法，何耶？後世以文章為事業，汲汲乎弊精神以求見於世，亦已勞矣，卒未聞有追古作，抑又何耶？或者曰：「學文之道，急於明理。」明理果謂學文而急乎？或者曰：「文章以體製為先。」則《大誥》《繫辭》諸書又何所法程乎？或者又曰：「文章與時高下，三代之文至戰國而病，涉秦漢復起；漢之文至三國而病，唐興復起。」夫戰國秦漢
translation_en:
…the calculations of the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe, the rules for altered pitches and half-tones [?], and the principles governing the five notes and two altered notes are also exact. But is what is called the origin of sound and vital breath truly to be sought in millet-based measurements and reed-membrane ash? Or is there another explanation? Rites and music have long been difficult to discuss. Might these two books by Zhu and Cai be ranked alongside the Rites of Zhou in this way? You candidates should devote your full attention to answering; do not say, “I, for my part, have no time.”
Question: Writing is the finest expression of governance, the branches and leaves of the Way. What intention did the sages and worthies have in composing writings? Writing illuminates the Way and records events, proclaims the intentions of those above and conveys the concerns of those below. Like beans and grain, water and fire in human life, it cannot be dispensed with for a single day. Why, then, do commentators claim that the Three Dynasties had no literary men and the Six Classics no principles of composition? In later ages, people made literary composition their vocation, anxiously exhausting their mental energies to gain recognition in the world. Their toil was indeed great, yet in the end we hear of none whose works rivaled those of antiquity. Why is this, too? Some say, “In learning to write, understanding principle is the most urgent task.” Is understanding principle truly urgent for the sake of learning to write? Some say, “Form and structure come first in literary composition.” What, then, did such texts as the Great Announcement and the Appended Statements take as their models and standards? Others say, “Literature rises and falls with the times. The literature of the Three Dynasties declined in the Warring States period, then revived through the Qin and Han. Han literature declined in the Three Kingdoms period, then revived with the rise of the Tang.” Now, in the Warring States, Qin, and Han…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之時若列禦寇莊周荀況之辨與夫賈
傅董相史遷相如揚雄皆以文章鳴世
其或邪或正或純或駁可得而品評歟
唐之稱文者莫過韓愈氏當時學者誦
其功並孟子固也但觀其讀墨篇與孟
簡書何以為異說所惑歟原道原性等
篇又何以見大用而昧大體歟宋之稱
文者莫過歐陽氏當時學者皆曰歐陽
子今之韓愈似也但自稱乃曰我所為
===
文必與道俱文與道果二事歟或謂其
說詩賦似李白記事如馬遷論治如陸
贄然歟否歟或謂二子之文千變萬化
韓無心而歐有心韓文高而歐可學又
何所據也或謂有化工剪裁繪畫之文
有治世衰世亂世之文不知二子何所
造耶夫成癖類俳固不可為文而文之
所以為文不可不講也其悉言之毋畧
問道之大原出於天而傳於聖賢實士君
punctuated:
之時，若列禦寇、莊周、荀況之辨，與夫賈傅、董相、史遷、相如、揚雄，皆以文章鳴世。其或邪或正，或純或駁，可得而品評歟？唐之稱文者，莫過韓愈氏。當時學者誦其功並孟子，固也。但觀其《讀墨》篇、《與孟簡書》，何以為異說所惑歟？《原道》《原性》等篇，又何以見大用而昧大體歟？宋之稱文者，莫過歐陽氏。當時學者皆曰：「歐陽子，今之韓愈。」似也。但自稱乃曰：「我所為文，必與道俱。」文與道果二事歟？或謂其說詩賦似李白，記事如馬遷，論治如陸贄，然歟否歟？或謂二子之文千變萬化，韓無心而歐有心，韓文高而歐可學，又何所據也？或謂有化工、剪裁、繪畫之文，有治世、衰世、亂世之文，不知二子何所造耶？夫成癖類俳，固不可為文，而文之所以為文，不可不講也。其悉言之，毋畧。

問：道之大原出於天，而傳於聖賢，實士君
translation_en:
…in those times, the disputations of Lie Yukou, Zhuang Zhou, and Xun Kuang, together with the writings of Grand Tutor Jia Yi, Chancellor Dong Zhongshu, the historian Sima Qian, Sima Xiangru, and Yang Xiong, all won renown in the world through literary composition. Can their heterodoxy or orthodoxy, their purity or admixture, be assessed and ranked?

Among those celebrated for writing in the Tang, none surpassed Han Yu. Scholars of his time praised his achievement as equal to that of Mengzi; rightly so. Yet, examining his Reading Mozi and Letter to Meng Jian, why was he misled by heterodox doctrines? In such essays as An Inquiry into the Way and An Inquiry into Human Nature, why did he perceive the Way’s great operation yet remain unclear about its fundamental substance?

Among those celebrated for writing in the Song, none surpassed Ouyang Xiu. Scholars of his time all said, “Master Ouyang is the Han Yu of our day.” The comparison seems apt. Yet he himself declared, “The writing I produce must always accompany the Way.” Are writing and the Way really two separate things? Some say that his poetry and rhapsodies resemble Li Bai’s [?], his recording of events resembles Sima Qian’s, and his discussion of government resembles Lu Zhi’s. Is this so or not? Some say that the writing of these two masters undergoes innumerable transformations: Han writes without deliberate intent, whereas Ouyang writes with deliberate intent; Han’s writing is lofty, whereas Ouyang’s can be learned. On what grounds do they say this? Some speak of writing fashioned by nature, writing cut and tailored, and writing painted and embellished; they also speak of writing belonging to an age of good government, an age of decline, or an age of disorder. To which of these realms did the two masters attain? Certainly, writing that becomes an obsession and resembles a jester’s performance is unacceptable; yet what makes writing truly writing must be examined. Explain it all fully, omitting nothing.

Question: The great source of the Way issues from Heaven and is transmitted through sages and worthies. It is truly, for scholars and gentlemen …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
子進脩之標的也大哉羲易爲萬世文
字之鼻祖是矣而帝堯又何以開千萬
世心學之源耶列聖相承傳授一統至
吾夫子集大成以詔萬世至矣夫復何
言姑以孔門傳授之始終論之孟子得
夫子之道者也而何謂傳統於子思歟
顏孟皆隱未見行未成也而何謂優湯
武並禹稷歟或謂軻死無傳而又謂濂
溪得千聖不傳之秘則傳孟子之統者
===
濂溪也而何受學於希夷歟二程之統
實得之濂溪議者乃以龍德正中比顏
子而不及文理密察比孟子而過之抑
又何所見歟夫聖賢一道也兄弟一氣
也條例青苗西監之所處定夫中立之
所愛至於論性論心間有不同何歟或
謂明道孟子以後一人又曰朱子之功
不在孟子下然則孟氏之統程朱皆得
而傳歟當時若橫渠堯夫延平東萊敬
punctuated: 子進脩之標的也。大哉！羲易爲萬世文字之鼻祖，是矣；而帝堯又何以開千萬世心學之源耶？列聖相承，傳授一統，至吾夫子集大成，以詔萬世，至矣夫！復何言？姑以孔門傳授之始終論之。孟子得夫子之道者也，而何謂傳統於子思歟？顏孟皆隱，未見行，未成也，而何謂優湯武、並禹稷歟？或謂軻死無傳，而又謂濂溪得千聖不傳之秘，則傳孟子之統者濂溪也，而何受學於希夷歟？二程之統，實得之濂溪，議者乃以龍德正中，比顏子而不及；文理密察，比孟子而過之，抑又何所見歟？夫聖賢一道也，兄弟一氣也。條例、青苗、西監之所處，定夫、中立之所愛，至於論性論心，間有不同，何歟？或謂明道孟子以後一人，又曰朱子之功不在孟子下，然則孟氏之統，程朱皆得而傳歟？當時若橫渠、堯夫、延平、東萊、敬
translation_en:
…the standard for gentlemen’s advancement in learning and self-cultivation. How great it is! That Fuxi’s Changes is the progenitor of writing for all ages is indeed so; but how did Emperor Yao also open the wellspring of learning concerning the mind for countless generations? Successive sages inherited and transmitted a single lineage, until our Master, Confucius, brought it to its fullest culmination and thereby instructed all ages. This was perfection indeed! What more could be said? Let us nevertheless discuss the transmission within the school of Confucius from beginning to end. Mengzi attained the Master’s Way; why, then, is he said to have received the lineage from Zisi? Yan Hui and Mengzi both lived in obscurity, their Way neither put into practice nor brought to accomplishment; why, then, are they said to surpass Tang and Wu and equal Yu and Ji? Some say that after Meng Ke died, the transmission ceased; yet they also say that Lianxi (Zhou Dunyi) obtained the secret that a thousand sages had not transmitted. If, then, Lianxi transmitted Mengzi’s lineage, why did he receive instruction from Xiyi (Chen Tuan)?

The two Cheng brothers indeed received their lineage from Lianxi. Yet commentators, judging by the dragon’s virtue of uprightness and centrality, compare them with Master Yan and find them inferior; judging by their close discernment of patterned principles, they compare them with Mengzi and find them superior. What insight underlies these judgments? The sages and worthies share one Way, and brothers share one vital energy. Why, then, did the brothers sometimes differ in their positions concerning the Regulations Office, the Green Sprouts policy, and the ‘Western Directorate’ [?], in their affection for Dingfu (You Zuo) and Zhongli (Yang Shi), and even in their discussions of human nature and the mind? Some say that Mingdao (Cheng Hao) was the one outstanding figure since Mengzi; they also say that Master Zhu’s contribution was no less than Mengzi’s. Does this mean, then, that both Cheng and Zhu received and transmitted Mengzi’s lineage? Among the men of those times were Hengqu (Zhang Zai), Yaofu (Shao Yong), Yanping (Li Tong), Donglai (Lü Zuqian), and Jing…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫之賢皆不得與而龜山勉齋反繼程
朱之統抑又何歟今之學聖人者曰學
顏子爲近又曰立志以明道自期待何
論顏子而不及孟子至於范希文儕之
明道何歟就顏孟所至而造聖人微何
以使之全麤何以使之粹歟厥後又有
元亨利貞論統者又何謂也不幾於牽
合而誇張歟諸子讀聖賢之書其必想
像而旁通之矣願明以告我
===
問爲政如張琴瑟論事若持權衡士君子
淹貫經史何爲也凡廟堂江湖之所當
憂吾分內事也而可孤桑弧之志哉他
不暇舉姑以東廣事宜與諸生商之瓊
州以黎峒盤於內即皇甫所擬虺蛇入
室者也其將搗穴窮巢驅除之乎抑如
韓管帥之勞來也高廉以𤟤獞環於外
即伏波所爲銅柱表界者也其將鑿山
刊道殄滅之乎抑如倉知州之撫諭也
punctuated:
夫之賢，皆不得與，而龜山、勉齋反繼程朱之統，抑又何歟？今之學聖人者曰：「學顏子爲近。」又曰：「立志以明道自期待。」何論顏子而不及孟子，至於范希文儕之明道，何歟？就顏孟所至而造聖人，微何以使之全，麤何以使之粹歟？厥後又有元亨利貞論統者，又何謂也？不幾於牽合而誇張歟？諸子讀聖賢之書，其必想像而旁通之矣，願明以告我。

問：爲政如張琴瑟，論事若持權衡。士君子淹貫經史，何爲也？凡廟堂江湖之所當憂，吾分內事也，而可孤桑弧之志哉？他不暇舉，姑以東廣事宜與諸生商之。瓊州以黎峒盤於內，即皇甫所擬虺蛇入室者也。其將搗穴窮巢驅除之乎？抑如韓管帥之勞來也？高廉以𤟤獞環於外，即伏波所爲銅柱表界者也。其將鑿山刊道殄滅之乎？抑如倉知州之撫諭也？
translation_en:
…[Jing]fu, despite their worthiness, were all excluded, while Guishan and Mianzhai instead succeeded to the orthodox transmission of Cheng and Zhu: why was this? Those who now study the way of the sages say, “Learning from Master Yan offers the closest approach.” They also say, “In setting your aspirations, take Mingdao as the standard you expect to attain.” Why do they discuss Master Yan without mentioning Master Meng? And why do they place Fan Xiwen on a level with Mingdao? Starting from what Yan and Meng attained and advancing toward sagehood, how can what is subtle be made complete, and what is coarse be made pure? Later, there were also those who discussed the orthodox transmission in terms of origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy: what did they mean? Does this not verge on forced connections and exaggeration? You gentlemen have read the books of the sages and worthies; surely you have reflected upon them and grasped their wider connections. I ask you to explain these matters clearly to me.

Question: Governing is like stringing a qin or se zither; deliberating on affairs is like wielding a weighing beam and weights. For what purpose do gentlemen acquire comprehensive mastery of the classics and histories? Everything that ought to concern us, whether at court or away from office, falls within our own responsibilities. Can we betray the aspirations symbolized by the mulberry bow? There is no time to enumerate other matters; let me discuss with you students the practical affairs of Guangdong. In Qiongzhou, the Li settlements are entrenched in the interior—precisely the situation Huangfu likened to venomous snakes entering a house. Should we attack their lairs, pursue them to their remotest nests, and drive them out? Or should we comfort and win them over, as Commander Han did? Gaozhou and Lianzhou are surrounded on their outer borders by the [𤟤?] and Zhuang peoples—the very situation for which the General Who Subdues the Waves erected bronze pillars to mark the boundary. Should we cut through mountains, clear roads, and exterminate them? Or should we reassure and admonish them, as Prefect Cang did?

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
海賊之雙桅出沒皆曰漳民糴穀麥之
害也今前船雖盡毀矣而巡哨未必無
私通之弊也不知昔人之立寨主與負
海舟踈耶密耶番舶之連年往來皆曰
竒貨資軍餉之利也今諸夷雖效順矣
而將來恐未必無開邊之釁也不知昔
人之貸緡錢與招舶商是耶非耶今之
屯政未嘗不嚴也或謂武弁恃世襲而
侵欺者愈衆何以化之昔在欽州而課
===
農業與范仲淹之行屯政有相合乎今
之軍伍未嘗不補也或謂軍士苦輪班
而逃亡者相望何以實之昔在端州而
括隱丁與張說之變彍騎有相同乎積
穀所以備賑也今永豐際留等倉皆不
堪於乆積不知李悝耿壽昌之舊規可
潤色之乎均徭所以平施也而弓兵水
夫等役皆不樂於親當不知君實介甫
之爭辨可決擇之乎凡此皆關地方之
punctuated: 海賊之雙桅出沒，皆曰漳民糴穀麥之害也。今前船雖盡毀矣，而巡哨未必無私通之弊也。不知昔人之立寨主與負海舟，踈耶？密耶？番舶之連年往來，皆曰竒貨資軍餉之利也。今諸夷雖效順矣，而將來恐未必無開邊之釁也。不知昔人之貸緡錢與招舶商，是耶？非耶？今之屯政未嘗不嚴也，或謂武弁恃世襲而侵欺者愈衆，何以化之？昔在欽州而課農業，與范仲淹之行屯政有相合乎？今之軍伍未嘗不補也，或謂軍士苦輪班而逃亡者相望，何以實之？昔在端州而括隱丁，與張說之變彍騎有相同乎？積穀所以備賑也，今永豐、際留等倉皆不堪於乆積，不知李悝、耿壽昌之舊規可潤色之乎？均徭所以平施也，而弓兵、水夫等役皆不樂於親當，不知君實、介甫之爭辨可決擇之乎？凡此皆關地方之
translation_en:
The pirates’ two-masted vessels come and go, and everyone calls this a harmful consequence of the people of Zhangzhou purchasing grain and wheat. Although the vessels just mentioned have now all been destroyed, the patrols may still be guilty of secret collusion. Were the earlier arrangements for appointing stockade chiefs and assigning responsibility for coastal vessels [?] lax or thorough?

Foreign merchant ships arrive year after year, and everyone speaks of the benefit of using their exotic merchandise to finance military provisions. Although the foreign peoples now profess obedience, I fear that this may yet provoke trouble on the frontier. Were the earlier practices of lending strings of cash and recruiting maritime merchants right or wrong?

The administration of military agricultural colonies today is certainly strict. Yet some say that military officers rely on their hereditary positions, and that ever more of them encroach upon others and commit fraud. How can they be reformed? Did the earlier encouragement of agriculture in Qinzhou accord with Fan Zhongyan’s administration of military agricultural colonies?

The ranks of the army today are certainly replenished. Yet some say that soldiers suffer from rotating duty, and that deserters follow one another in an unending stream. How can the ranks be filled? Was the earlier registration of concealed adult males in Duanzhou comparable to Zhang Yue’s reorganization of the guoqi cavalry?

Grain is stored to provide for famine relief. Yet the Yongfeng, Jiliu [?], and other granaries today are all unsuitable for prolonged storage. Could the old regulations of Li Kui and Geng Shouchang be adapted and improved?

The equalization of labor service is intended to distribute obligations equitably. Yet no one willingly performs in person such duties as those of archers and water-service laborers. Can we adjudicate between the positions debated by Junshi (Sima Guang) and Jiefu (Wang Anshi)? All these matters concern the locality’s…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
利害休戚不可不先庚後甲以為之所
也其條陳之吾將觀子之胷襟且以為
當宁獻
punctuated: 利害休戚，不可不先庚後甲，以為之所也。其條陳之，吾將觀子之胷襟，且以為當宁獻。
translation_en: …benefits and harms, well-being and distress. These matters require careful deliberation beforehand and attention afterward, so that suitable arrangements may be made. Set out your proposals point by point. I shall examine the breadth of your understanding and aspirations, and also present your proposals to the reigning sovereign.

中式舉人七十五名。

第一名梁津，廣州府學生，詩。第二名潘庭楠，肇慶府學生，易。第三名梁以蘧，廣州府學生，書。第四名饒相，潮州府學生，禮記。第五名林時雨，饒平縣學生，春秋。第六名黎民表，從化縣學生，詩。第七名姚學古，潮陽縣學生，書。第八名周文明，南海縣學附學生，易。第九名葉成章，瓊山縣學附學生，禮記。第十名李景元，崖州學生，春秋。第十一名楊紹震，番禺縣學增廣生，書。第十二名李兆龍，南海縣學生，詩。第十三名龐嵩，廣州府學生，詩。第十四名麥英，從化縣學生，易。第十五名倫學智，南海縣學附學生，易。第十六名何派行，香山縣學生，易。
translation_en:
Seventy-five successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Liang Jin, a student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Second: Pan Tingnan, a student of the Zhaoqing Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Third: Liang Yiqu, a student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Fourth: Rao Xiang, a student of the Chaozhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

Fifth: Lin Shiyu, a student of the Raoping County School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Sixth: Li Minbiao, a student of the Conghua County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Seventh: Yao Xuegu, a student of the Chaoyang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Eighth: Zhou Wenming, an attached student of the Nanhai County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Ninth: Ye Chengzhang, an attached student of the Qiongshan County School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

Tenth: Li Jingyuan, a student of the Yazhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Eleventh: Yang Shaozhen, an added student of the Panyu County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Twelfth: Li Zhaolong, a student of the Nanhai County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Thirteenth: Pang Song, a student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Fourteenth: Mai Ying, a student of the Conghua County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Fifteenth: Lun Xuezhi, an attached student of the Nanhai County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Sixteenth: He Paixing, a student of the Xiangshan County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

〔庚戌〕第十七名趙時舉饒平縣學附學生書

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫仁者己欲立而立人己欲達而達人能
近取譬可謂仁之方也已
潘庭楠
同考試官教諭謝批論仁在孔門爲難此作辭理充
暢而與物同體之意藹然言外豈甞求仁而有得者耶
同考試官學正甯批欲立欲達處正仁人不待於推
而自然及物之心此作善能發揮錄之
===
考試官教諭張批疏暢
考試官教授錢批辭達
聖人狀仁者之心而因示求仁之術也夫仁者
以公物爲心也恕以行之則近之矣而又何以
過求爲哉昔夫子因子貢以博施濟衆爲仁故
告之以此若曰道在天下與其索之高遠而難
爲功孰若求之切近而易爲力哉試以仁之體
爲汝言之夫仁者其心公而溥其量恢以弘是
故開吾之麗以植其生吾之心欲如此其立也
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

夫仁者，己欲立而立人，己欲達而達人。能近取譬，可謂仁之方也已。

潘庭楠

同考試官教諭謝批：論仁在孔門爲難，此作辭理充暢，而與物同體之意藹然言外，豈甞求仁而有得者耶？

同考試官學正甯批：欲立欲達處，正仁人不待於推而自然及物之心，此作善能發揮，錄之。

考試官教諭張批：疏暢。

考試官教授錢批：辭達。

聖人狀仁者之心，而因示求仁之術也。夫仁者，以公物爲心也，恕以行之則近之矣，而又何以過求爲哉？昔夫子因子貢以博施濟衆爲仁，故告之以此，若曰：「道在天下，與其索之高遠而難爲功，孰若求之切近而易爲力哉？試以仁之體爲汝言之。夫仁者，其心公而溥，其量恢以弘。是故開吾之麗以植其生，吾之心欲如此其立也，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The benevolent person, wishing to establish himself, establishes others; wishing to advance himself, advances others. To be able to draw an analogy from what is near at hand may be called the method of benevolence.”

Pan Tingnan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: “Even in Confucius’s school, discussing benevolence was difficult. This composition is ample and fluent in both expression and reasoning; a sense of forming one body with all things suffuses what lies beyond its words. Might its author have sought benevolence and gained some understanding of it?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Ning, Instructor: “In the desire to establish oneself and to advance oneself lies precisely the benevolent person’s heart, which naturally reaches others without awaiting a deliberate extension. This composition develops that meaning well. Select it.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Clear and fluent.”

Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: “The wording conveys the meaning.”

The Sage describes the heart of the benevolent person and thereby shows the method of seeking benevolence. The benevolent person takes impartial concern for others as his guiding intent. By practicing reciprocity, one comes close to this; why, then, seek excessively beyond it? Formerly, because Zigong regarded bestowing benefits widely and bringing relief to the multitude as benevolence, the Master instructed him with these words. It was as though he said: “As for the Way in the world, rather than seeking it in what is lofty and remote, where accomplishment is difficult, would it not be better to seek it in what is immediate and near, where exerting oneself is easy? Let me explain to you the substance of benevolence. The benevolent person’s heart is impartial and all-embracing, and his capacity broad and generous. Thus, in opening opportunities for those associated with me so as to sustain their lives [?], my heart desires that I should establish myself in this way …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
即欲夫人之同立也而凡水火金木土穀惟脩
以躋諸富壽者森然其莫禦棐吾之彞以明其
德吾之心欲如此其達也即欲夫人之同達也
而凡黨庠術序國學是敎以開其聰明者油然
其自萌所施雖未能盡如吾願也隨吾身之所
接而加吾固有之心何天理之流通乎所行雖
未能悉副吾欲也隨物之自來而應以物所同
然之願何至誠之惻怛乎仁之本體如此然非
一蹴可至也而求之顧豈無其術哉蓋已之心
===
欲立也譬夫人之喜康共猶夫我也則推所欲
而與之聚之稱物得平施之宜已之心欲達也
譬夫人之樂綏猷猶夫吾也則推所欲而爲之
及之同人無于宗之吝是雖未能大道爲公也
然涵養之漸充則將私欲消而真性湛求仁之
方豈外於是耶雖未能與物爲體也然真積之
既久則將査滓化而實理融求仁之術不有在
於斯耶是則語之以仁立其的也示之以方啓
其扃也夫子之敎子貢至矣哉嗟夫仁之難成
punctuated: 即欲夫人之同立也。而凡水火金木土穀惟脩，以躋諸富壽者，森然其莫禦；棐吾之彞以明其德，吾之心欲如此其達也，即欲夫人之同達也。而凡黨庠術序國學是敎，以開其聰明者，油然其自萌。所施雖未能盡如吾願也，隨吾身之所接而加吾固有之心，何天理之流通乎！所行雖未能悉副吾欲也，隨物之自來而應以物所同然之願，何至誠之惻怛乎！仁之本體如此，然非一蹴可至也，而求之顧豈無其術哉？蓋已之心欲立也，譬夫人之喜康共猶夫我也，則推所欲而與之聚之，稱物得平施之宜；已之心欲達也，譬夫人之樂綏猷猶夫吾也，則推所欲而爲之及之，同人無于宗之吝。是雖未能大道爲公也，然涵養之漸充，則將私欲消而真性湛，求仁之方豈外於是耶？雖未能與物爲體也，然真積之既久，則將査滓化而實理融，求仁之術不有在於斯耶？是則語之以仁，立其的也；示之以方，啓其扃也。夫子之敎子貢至矣哉！嗟夫！仁之難成
translation_en:
…one immediately wishes others likewise to establish themselves. Thus all efforts to put water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain in good order, thereby bringing people wealth and longevity, arise in profusion, irresistibly. In supporting our constant moral norms so as to illuminate virtue, when my heart wishes thus to attain fulfillment, it immediately wishes others likewise to attain fulfillment. Thus instruction in district schools, township schools [?], and the schools of the capital, through which people’s intelligence and understanding are developed, springs forth spontaneously. Although what one bestows cannot wholly accord with one’s wishes, one extends one’s inherent heart to all whom one encounters: how freely Heaven’s principle flows! Although one’s actions cannot fully satisfy one’s desires, one responds to beings as they come, according to the wishes they share: how tender is the solicitude of utmost sincerity!

Such is the fundamental substance of benevolence. Yet it cannot be attained in a single stride. Can there nevertheless be no method for seeking it? When one’s own heart wishes to establish itself, one recognizes by analogy that others delight in well-being [?] just as oneself does. One then extends what one desires to others, gathering it for them, weighing circumstances and achieving an appropriately equitable bestowal. When one’s own heart wishes to attain fulfillment, one recognizes by analogy that others delight in peaceful guidance [?] just as oneself does. One then extends what one desires to others, acting for them and bringing it within their reach; in fellowship with others, one avoids the narrowness of confining it to one’s own clan.

Although this may not yet amount to making the Great Way common to all, as moral nurturing gradually reaches fullness, selfish desires will dissolve and one’s true nature become clear. Could the means of seeking benevolence lie outside this? Although one may not yet form a single body with all beings, once genuine effort has accumulated over a long time, the dross will be transformed and true principle will become thoroughly integrated. Does not the method of seeking benevolence lie here? Thus, in speaking to him of benevolence, the Master established his target; in showing him the means, he opened the gate for him. How consummate was the Master’s instruction of Zigong! Alas, the difficulty of achieving benevolence …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也久矣而夫子之敎子貢不止於此他日又曰
賜也非爾所及又曰一言終身行之亦深切而
著明矣此子貢之晩年進德蓋亦以强恕爲入
門乎厥後曾子絜矩孟子强恕之論實相表裏
此亦可見聖賢傳授同一道也學者宜合而觀
之

異名而一理也中庸發自成自道之訓其責望
斯人之意何深切乎想其意謂夫君子之道具

punctuated:

…has long been difficult to achieve. Yet the Master's instruction of Zigong did not stop here. On another occasion he said, “Ci, this is beyond your reach,” and again, “A single word to practice throughout one's life.” These teachings, too, were penetrating and clear. Thus Zigong's advancement in virtue in his later years probably also began with diligent practice of reciprocity. Subsequently, Zengzi's teaching of the measuring square and Mengzi's discussion of striving to practice reciprocity complemented one another. Here, too, we can see that the sages and worthies transmitted the same Way. Students should consider these teachings together.
“Sincerity is self-completion, and the Way is that by which one directs oneself.”
Li Minbiao
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: “Self-completion and self-direction precisely reveal the learning that unites the inner and outer. Writers who discuss things in general terms when treating ‘self-sincerity’ [?] miss the original purport. This essay displays an exceptionally firm understanding and merits inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: “Considering the following passage, ‘not merely completing oneself,’ and the explanation in Questions and Answers of becoming a son and becoming a minister, the exposition should focus on human beings. This essay excels in its reasoning and has a distinctive organizing approach. Its author is someone with whom one can discuss sincerity.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Refined and precise.”
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: “Grasps the purport.”

How profound and earnest are the expectations it places upon human beings when the Doctrine of the Mean sets forth its teaching of self-completion and self-direction! title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
豈有道外之誠哉是故眞實無僞之心完具於
繼善之初誠也誠何以切於物耶蓋有體必有
性以為之帥斯良知不匱而衆善可承乎權輿
有物必有則以為之彞斯眞精不散而萬化可
發於機括於德而舉輶毛固宜厥脩之罔覺有
孚而至盈缶是謂所履之其旋如實心事父實
心事君乃臣子之所自成也否則非所以為物
矣推之萬物莫不然者物之於誠豈可遺哉若
夫眞實無妄之理發見於日用之常道也道何
===
以切於人耶蓋無為者在有覺者為之運吾擇
吾善而無資於人形而上者在形而下者為之
弘吾固吾執而無待於外克念有作聖之階當
棄蹠之徒而由舜務學有緝熈之路必舍桀之
行以從堯如孝於父忠於君乃臣子之所以自
行也否則非所以為人矣推之萬事莫不然者
人之於道豈可離哉是則誠為天命道外無誠
也道為率性誠外無道也思誠者於己取之而
已矣抑誠也道也體用一原也自成自道物我
punctuated: 豈有道外之誠哉？是故眞實無僞之心，完具於繼善之初，誠也。誠何以切於物耶？蓋有體必有性以為之帥，斯良知不匱，而衆善可承乎權輿；有物必有則以為之彞，斯眞精不散，而萬化可發於機括。於德而舉輶毛，固宜厥脩之罔覺；有孚而至盈缶，是謂所履之其旋。如實心事父、實心事君，乃臣子之所自成也，否則非所以為物矣。推之萬物，莫不然者，物之於誠豈可遺哉？若夫眞實無妄之理，發見於日用之常，道也。道何以切於人耶？蓋無為者在，有覺者為之運，吾擇吾善而無資於人；形而上者在，形而下者為之弘，吾固吾執而無待於外。克念有作聖之階，當棄蹠之徒而由舜；務學有緝熈之路，必舍桀之行以從堯。如孝於父、忠於君，乃臣子之所以自行也，否則非所以為人矣。推之萬事，莫不然者，人之於道豈可離哉？是則誠為天命，道外無誠也；道為率性，誠外無道也。思誠者於己取之而已矣。抑誠也，道也，體用一原也；自成自道，物我
translation_en:
…could there be sincerity outside the Way? Thus, the true and unfeigned heart, fully endowed at the inception of the continuing goodness of creation, is sincerity. Why is sincerity essential to things? Whatever has a substantial form must have a nature to govern it: thus innate moral knowledge is inexhaustible, and the many forms of goodness can be received from their very beginning. Whatever exists must have a principle as its constant norm: thus its true essence does not disperse, and the myriad transformations can issue from their activating pivot. In speaking of virtue, a light feather is invoked; fittingly, its cultivation proceeds without conscious awareness. Trustworthiness reaches the point of filling an earthen vessel: this is what is meant by returning to the course one treads [?]. Serving one's father with a sincere heart and serving one's ruler with a sincere heart are how subjects and sons bring themselves to completion. Otherwise, they would lack what makes them the beings they are. Extend this to the myriad things, and none is otherwise. How, then, could things dispense with sincerity?
As for true and unfailing principle manifesting itself in ordinary daily life, this is the Way. Why is the Way essential to human beings? That which acts without deliberate effort exists, but conscious beings put it into operation: I choose what is good for me without relying on others. That which is above physical form exists, but what is within physical form gives it fuller expression: I hold firmly to what I embrace without depending on anything external. The capacity for mindful reflection provides steps toward sagehood: one should abandon the company of Zhi and follow Shun. Devotion to learning offers a path toward continuing illumination: one must forsake the conduct of Jie and follow Yao. Being filial toward one's father and loyal toward one's ruler are how subjects and sons themselves put the Way into practice. Otherwise, they would lack what makes them human. Extend this to the myriad affairs, and none is otherwise. How, then, could human beings be separated from the Way?
Thus sincerity is what Heaven mandates: outside the Way there is no sincerity. The Way is following one's nature: outside sincerity there is no Way. Those who seek sincerity need only obtain it within themselves. Moreover, sincerity and the Way have substance and function issuing from a single source. Bringing oneself to completion and guiding oneself along the Way, things and oneself…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一致也此所謂致用崇德而儒者內外合一之
學不外是也彼語寂滅者不知道徇生執有者
不識誠此子思以世之功於是乎大也人苟能
反求而自得之則成已成物之道思過半矣然
求之何先其要在於慎獨
存其心養其性所以事天也
梁以斅
同考試官教諭紀批心性天一理塲中能發明此意
者絕少辭理精到不費雕𣃔僅見此篇
===
考試官教諭張批密緻
考試官教授錢批明順
能全其天之與我者所以為奉若天者也夫心
也性也皆天之所以與我者也善事天者安可
廢存養之功哉孟子之意若曰君子之學固先
之致知而啓其端矣若非繼之以力行何以致
其實哉是故虛靈湛一心之本體也物知相誘
心斯蕩矣猶夫其弗盡也故必守之以惺惺之
法渾然神明之退藏持之以乾乾之功昭然本
punctuated:
一致也。此所謂致用崇德，而儒者內外合一之學不外是也。彼語寂滅者不知道，徇生執有者不識誠，此子思以世之功於是乎大也。人苟能反求而自得之，則成已成物之道思過半矣。然求之何先？其要在於慎獨。
「存其心，養其性，所以事天也。」
梁以斅
同考試官教諭紀批：心性天一理，塲中能發明此意者絕少。辭理精到，不費雕𣃔，僅見此篇。
考試官教諭張批：密緻。
考試官教授錢批：明順。
能全其天之與我者，所以為奉若天者也。夫心也，性也，皆天之所以與我者也。善事天者安可廢存養之功哉？孟子之意若曰：君子之學固先之致知而啓其端矣，若非繼之以力行，何以致其實哉？是故虛靈湛一，心之本體也；物知相誘，心斯蕩矣，猶夫其弗盡也。故必守之以惺惺之法，渾然神明之退藏；持之以乾乾之功，昭然本
translation_en:
…are one and the same. This is what is meant by putting learning into practice and exalting virtue; the Confucian learning that unites the inner and outer extends no further than this. Those who speak of quiescence and extinction do not understand the Way; those who pursue life and cling to existence do not understand sincerity. Herein lies the greatness of Zisi’s service to the world [?]. If people can turn inward to seek it and attain it for themselves, they will have understood more than half of the Way of perfecting themselves and other things. Yet what comes first in seeking it? The essential point is vigilance when alone.
“Preserving one’s mind and nourishing one’s nature are the means of serving Heaven.”
Liang Yixiao
Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: Mind, nature, and Heaven share a single principle. Among the candidates in the examination hall, exceedingly few can elucidate this meaning. The language and reasoning are refined and exact, without laborious embellishment [?]. This essay alone achieves it.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Closely reasoned and meticulous.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Director of Studies: Clear and fluent.
To preserve intact what Heaven has bestowed upon us is the means of reverently obeying Heaven. Mind and nature are both what Heaven has bestowed upon us. How could one who serves Heaven well dispense with the work of preserving and nourishing them? Mencius’s meaning is as if he said: The learning of the noble man certainly begins with extending knowledge, thereby making a start. But unless this is followed by earnest practice, how can he bring it to fulfillment? Thus, emptiness and spiritual awareness, clarity and unity, constitute the original substance of the mind. When external things and knowing entice one another [?], the mind becomes unsettled, as though its capacities had not been fully realized. Therefore one must guard it through constant wakefulness, with its spiritual intelligence withdrawn into undivided repose; one must sustain it through unremitting effort, making luminously clear its fundamental…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
體之澄徹是寂亦存也感亦存也寧有旦晝之
梏亡乎純粹至善性之淵源也客感相攻性斯
害矣猶夫其弗知也故必復吾固有之眞從容
以待其自化順吾擴充之量優游以俟其自成
是動亦養也靜亦養也寧有人爲之助長乎夫
心也者天之神而吾得之以爲心也存心夫何
爲也以爲天之不可褻而惟欽惟寅以繼其志
性也者天之理而吾得之以爲性也養性夫何
爲也以爲天之不可忽而其難其愼以述其事
===
上天之載固爾於穆而所以對越之誠若相爲
游衍也豈心外別有天爲之奉承哉維天之命
亦維顯思而所以欽崇之理若相爲陟降也豈
性外別有天爲之祗若哉是則天人一原也微
顯一機也事天之道不出於心性之外矣君子
其可重於視天而輕於待己乎大抵心也性也
天也其名三其實一也是故虞廷止於言心中
庸首於論性而說天莫辨乎易孟子此章兼而
論之其實有得於一貫之道也厥後西銘論事
punctuated: 體之澄徹，是寂亦存也，感亦存也，寧有旦晝之梏亡乎？純粹至善，性之淵源也。客感相攻，性斯害矣，猶夫其弗知也。故必復吾固有之眞，從容以待其自化；順吾擴充之量，優游以俟其自成。是動亦養也，靜亦養也，寧有人爲之助長乎？夫心也者，天之神而吾得之以爲心也。存心夫何爲也？以爲天之不可褻，而惟欽惟寅以繼其志。性也者，天之理而吾得之以爲性也。養性夫何爲也？以爲天之不可忽，而其難其愼以述其事。上天之載，固爾於穆，而所以對越之誠，若相爲游衍也，豈心外別有天爲之奉承哉？維天之命，亦維顯思，而所以欽崇之理，若相爲陟降也，豈性外別有天爲之祗若哉？是則天人一原也，微顯一機也，事天之道不出於心性之外矣。君子其可重於視天而輕於待己乎？大抵心也，性也，天也，其名三，其實一也。是故虞廷止於言心，《中庸》首於論性，而說天莫辨乎《易》。孟子此章兼而論之，其實有得於一貫之道也。厥後《西銘》論事
translation_en: …the clarity of its original substance. Thus the mind is preserved both in stillness and in responding to things: how could the fetters of daily activity cause its loss? Purity and utmost goodness are the wellspring of human nature. When external stimuli assail one another, our nature is harmed, as though we had never understood it. We must therefore recover the authenticity inherently ours, calmly awaiting its spontaneous transformation; we must follow our capacity for expansion and fulfillment, unhurriedly awaiting its spontaneous completion. Thus our nature is nourished both in activity and in stillness: how could there be any artificial forcing of its growth? The mind is Heaven’s spiritual potency, which we receive as our own mind. What is the purpose of preserving the mind? Recognizing that Heaven must not be profaned, we maintain reverence and respect so as to carry forward its intent. Human nature is Heaven’s principle, which we receive as our own nature. What is the purpose of nourishing our nature? Recognizing that Heaven must not be slighted, we take care and exercise caution so as to carry on its work. The workings of Heaven above are indeed profound and silent; the sincerity with which we stand before it seems to flow and unfold together with them. Could there be a separate Heaven outside the mind for us to serve? Heaven’s mandate is also truly manifest; the principle through which we revere it seems to ascend and descend together with it. Could there be a separate Heaven outside our nature for us reverently to obey? Thus Heaven and humanity share one source, and the hidden and the manifest share one activating impulse. The way of serving Heaven does not extend beyond the mind and human nature. How could the gentleman regard Heaven seriously yet treat himself lightly? In general, mind, nature, and Heaven are three names for a single reality. Thus the court of Yu confined its teaching to the mind; the Doctrine of the Mean begins by discussing human nature; and no account of Heaven is more discerning than the Book of Changes. In this chapter, Mengzi discusses all three together, truly grasping the Way that unites them through a single thread. Later, the Western Inscription discussed serving …

天之道，蓋原於此。故曰：「子厚養浩然之氣。」其以是夫！

translation_en:
…the way of serving Heaven surely derives from this. Hence the saying, “Zihou nurtured his vast, flowing vital energy.” Was this not the reason?

Book of Changes
“Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern changes in the seasons; observe human patterns to transform and perfect all under Heaven.”
By Zhou Wenming.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: The topic fundamentally elucidates the sage’s learning, which orders the affairs of Heaven and humanity, and is quite difficult to write on. This composition expounds the principles fully without wasting words. It merits inclusion as a model for the many candidates.
Comment by Associate Examiner Ning, School Director: Reading this composition, I wonder: are you one whose understanding encompasses Heaven and humanity? Admirable, admirable!
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: He understands the principles of Heaven and humanity.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: Clear and fluent.

The Great Commentary fully expounds the way of Adornment: it provides the means to order Heaven’s seasons and improve the people’s customs. For nothing in the way of Adornment is greater than Heaven and humanity. How profound is the Judgment Commentary’s exhaustive exposition of it! Its meaning is that the way of Adornment is embodied in the Book of Changes but did not originate with that book. Should we not observe the relationship between Heaven and humanity? Thus, as the firm and yielding interweave, people recognize that Heaven’s patterns appear in Adornment; yet do they understand that applying these patterns enables one to discern seasonal changes? Indeed, the waxing and waning, decline and growth of the two vital energies follow an unending cycle. I seek the solstices to explain their regularity …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
