人文賁道之大信矣抑古聖賢之有得於賁道
者於帝吾得堯舜焉命羲和而齊七政是也於
punctuated: 七政之往來進退，實變遷不定，吾推其歲差以稽其變。春夏秋冬之所以錯行，固有以考其星鳥、星火之各為其度；晦朔弦望之所以迭謝，又有以究其天根、月窟之互為其宫。是不必觀渾天之儀，在璿衡之政，而凡星宿之所以垂象、月朔之所以頒令，一剛柔之文也，何有於弗經者耶？文明以止，人知人之文見於賁也，而豈知用之可以化天下哉？誠以庸天秩之分，而觀會通以有行，則可以納斯民於軌物之中；惇天叙之典，而辨等威於有别，則可以錫斯人於皇極之内。在家而父子、兄弟、夫婦之三綱以明，群黎有畜牝牛之化；在國而吉凶軍賓嘉之五禮以叙，百僚有變文豹之風。是不必布象魏之法、徇木鐸之教，而凡群后之所以承德、蒸民之所以陳常，一明止之文也，何有於弗成者耶？是則時變難察也，而察之於天文；道化難成也，而成之於人文。賁道之大，信矣！抑古聖賢之有得於賁道者，於帝吾得堯舜焉，命羲和而齊七政是也。於
translation_en:
…The movements back and forth, advances and retreats, of the seven luminaries are indeed ever shifting and uncertain; I calculate their annual precession to examine these changes. As spring, summer, autumn, and winter proceed in succession, there are means to ascertain the respective positions of the Bird and Fire stars; as the last and first days of the lunar month, the quarter moons, and the full moon replace one another, there are likewise means to investigate how the “root of Heaven” and the “cavern of the moon” alternately serve as their lodgings. Thus, without necessarily inspecting the armillary instrument or attending to the regulation of the jade astronomical apparatus [?], all the means by which the constellations display their signs and ordinances are promulgated at each new moon belong to the single pattern of the firm and the yielding. What, then, could remain unregulated?

Brightness and refinement governed by restraint: people know that human cultural pattern manifests itself in Bi, Adornment, but how could they know that its application can transform all under Heaven? Indeed, by putting into practice the distinctions of Heaven’s ordained ranks, and by observing how things converge and interconnect so as to act accordingly, one can bring the people within the bounds of proper norms. By giving substance to the established institutions of Heaven’s ordering, and distinguishing grades of dignity according to their differences, one can grant the people a place within the August Ultimate, the supreme standard. Within the family, the three cardinal bonds [?] of father and son, elder and younger brothers, and husband and wife are thereby clarified, and the common people undergo the transformation signified by rearing a cow. Within the state, the five rites—auspicious, mourning, military, guest, and celebratory—are thereby ordered, and the officials acquire the disposition signified by the leopard’s transformation into a patterned coat. Thus, without necessarily posting laws at the palace gate towers or making the rounds to proclaim instruction with a wooden-clapper bell, all the means by which the lords uphold virtue and the multitude set forth constant norms belong to the single pattern of brightness and restraint. What, then, could remain unaccomplished?

Thus, changes in the seasons are difficult to discern, yet they are discerned through Heaven’s patterns; transformation through the Way is difficult to accomplish, yet it is accomplished through human cultural patterns. Great indeed is the Way of Adornment! As for ancient sages and worthies who grasped the Way of Adornment, among the emperors I find Yao and Shun: their commanding Xi and He and bringing the seven luminaries into order exemplify this. Among…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王吾得湯武焉脩人紀而叙彝倫是也後世有
以太玄而準易數以慚德而輩商周多見其不
知量也易之道其大如此其孰以卜筮小吾易
哉
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
麥英
同考試官教諭謝批場中作者於知禮處類多窘滯
是作以大中敦化發明聖學之資殆盡可式
===
同考試官學正甯批場中易義不拘則泛予能會意
融暢深得潔凈之旨
考試官教諭張批深得易道
考試官教授錢批精潔
大傳論易為聖學之資而必推其功之極也夫
聖人自有心易之妙也然德業必資於易焉易
之至也一至此哉大傳之意謂夫人知易書之
作也肇於聖人而不知易書之既作也有功於
聖人今夫高明極無窮之休此聖人之德若是
punctuated:
王，吾得湯武焉，脩人紀而叙彝倫是也。後世有以太玄而準易數，以慚德而輩商周，多見其不知量也。易之道，其大如此，其孰以卜筮小吾易哉！
夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。
麥英
同考試官教諭謝批：場中作者於知禮處類多窘滯，是作以大中敦化發明聖學之資殆盡，可式。
同考試官學正甯批：場中易義不拘則泛，予能會意融暢，深得潔凈之旨。
考試官教諭張批：深得易道。
考試官教授錢批：精潔。
大傳論易為聖學之資，而必推其功之極也。夫聖人自有心易之妙也，然德業必資於易焉。易之至也，一至此哉！大傳之意謂夫人知易書之作也肇於聖人，而不知易書之既作也有功於聖人。今夫高明極無窮之休，此聖人之德，若是
translation_en:
…among kings, I find Tang and Wu: their cultivation of human relationships and ordering of the constant moral relations exemplify this. In later ages, some used the Supreme Mystery (Taixuan) to match the numerical principles of the Changes, or, despite virtue that gave cause for shame, ranked themselves alongside the Shang and Zhou. Such cases mostly reveal their failure to know their own limits. So great is the Way of the Changes! Who would belittle our Changes by treating it as merely divination?
“The Changes is that by which the sage exalts his virtue and broadens his achievements. Knowledge is lofty; ritual propriety is lowly. Loftiness emulates Heaven; lowliness takes Earth as its model.”
Mai Ying
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: Most writers in the examination hall became constrained and halting when addressing knowledge and ritual propriety. This essay uses the ideas of supreme centrality and generous transformation to elucidate almost exhaustively how the Changes supports the learning of sages. It may serve as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner Ning, Assistant Instructor: The examination essays on the meaning of the Changes are either constrained or diffuse. “I” [?] can grasp its meaning and express it fluently and coherently, profoundly apprehending its purport of purity and refinement.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Profoundly grasps the Way of the Changes.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: Precise and pure.
The Great Commentary discusses the Changes as a resource for the learning of sages and necessarily traces its efficacy to the utmost. The sage himself possesses the wondrous workings of the Changes within his mind; nevertheless, his virtue and achievements must draw upon the Changes. Can the supreme excellence of the Changes really extend so far? The Great Commentary means that people know the writing of the Changes originated with the sages, but do not know that, once written, the Changes in turn benefited the sages. Now, lofty and luminous, reaching the utmost of inexhaustible excellence—such is the sage’s virtue, so…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其崇不特賢人之可久而已富有極無疆之盛
此聖人之業若是其廣不但賢人之可大而已
然崇非自崇也駸駸上達之機必於卦爻法象
得之而易其爲聖人崇德之書矣乎廣不自廣
也而蕩蕩難名之勢必於奇偶變通得之而易
其爲聖人廣業之書矣乎是果何以見之蓋聖
人以易而窮理則以大中爲極而廓虛靈之盡
其知無弗崇也以易而循理則以敦化爲深而
致踐履之實其禮無弗卑也夫其崇何所似也
===
===
聖人非有心於效天也自與穹窿上覆同一體
若所謂聰明憲天是已而德有不崇耶夫其卑
何所似也聖人非有心於法地也自與靜深不
測同一機若所謂安貞應地者矣而業有不廣
耶夫聖人德以易而崇業以易而廣則易道之
有益於人如此而可遠乎雖然聖人性之也而
何資於易蓋聖人先天而天不違而易理適與
之相契也但聖人之心不自滿足而有假我數
年之嘆也聖人尚然然則學者之居安樂玩尤
punctuated: 其崇，不特賢人之可久而已；富有極無疆之盛，此聖人之業，若是其廣，不但賢人之可大而已。然崇非自崇也，駸駸上達之機，必於卦爻法象得之，而易其爲聖人崇德之書矣乎！廣不自廣也，而蕩蕩難名之勢，必於奇偶變通得之，而易其爲聖人廣業之書矣乎！是果何以見之？蓋聖人以易而窮理，則以大中爲極，而廓虛靈之盡，其知無弗崇也；以易而循理，則以敦化爲深，而致踐履之實，其禮無弗卑也。夫其崇何所似也？聖人非有心於效天也，自與穹窿上覆同一體，若所謂聰明憲天是已，而德有不崇耶？夫其卑何所似也？聖人非有心於法地也，自與靜深不測同一機，若所謂安貞應地者矣，而業有不廣耶？夫聖人德以易而崇，業以易而廣，則易道之有益於人如此，而可遠乎？雖然，聖人性之也，而何資於易？蓋聖人先天而天不違，而易理適與之相契也。但聖人之心不自滿足，而有假我數年之嘆也。聖人尚然，然則學者之居安樂玩尤
translation_en:
…such is its loftiness, exceeding even the enduring virtue of the worthy. Abundant in possession and boundless in flourishing: such is the breadth of the sage’s accomplishments, exceeding even the greatness attainable by the worthy. Yet this loftiness does not arise of itself. The impetus for steadily ascending to higher understanding must be gained from the patterns and images of the hexagrams and their lines. Is not the Book of Changes, then, the book through which the sage elevates his virtue? Nor does this breadth arise of itself. Its vast and indescribable scope must be gained from the transformations and interrelations of odd and even lines. Is not the Book of Changes, then, the book through which the sage broadens his accomplishments?

How, indeed, can this be demonstrated? When the sage uses the Changes to fathom principle, he takes the great mean as his ultimate standard and fully extends the mind’s open and luminous capacity: his knowledge is lofty in every respect. When he uses the Changes to follow principle, he grounds himself deeply in generous transforming influence and brings actual practice to fruition: his ritual conduct is lowly in every respect. What does this loftiness resemble? The sage does not deliberately seek to emulate Heaven; he naturally forms one body with the vault that covers all above. This is what is meant by taking Heaven as the model for his perceptiveness and understanding. How could his virtue fail to be lofty? What does this lowliness resemble? The sage does not deliberately seek to model himself upon Earth; he naturally shares the same workings as its still and unfathomable depths. This is what is meant by responding to Earth through tranquil steadfastness. How could his accomplishments fail to be broad?

The sage’s virtue is thus elevated through the Changes, and his accomplishments broadened through the Changes. Since the Way of the Changes benefits people in this manner, may it be kept at a distance? Even so, the sage possesses this by nature: why should he need assistance from the Changes? When the sage acts before Heaven, Heaven does not depart from him; the principles of the Changes accord precisely with him. Yet the sage’s mind is never self-satisfied, and so he sighs, “Grant me a few more years.” If even the sage is like this, then for learners, dwelling contentedly and delighting in contemplation is all the more…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不可缺也以此勉焉而得意忘言則易不在聖
人而在我矣
書
惟天聰明惟聖時憲
姚學古
同考試官教諭紀批天聰明作者類皆浮泛此篇以
聲氣法象根於理者模寫得其旨矣錄之以破群疑
考試官教諭張批文有思致
考試官教授錢批有見之言
===
大臣之望君欲其與天而爲一焉蓋天之道出
於公也聖人法天以爲治寧有外於此哉傅說
以之告高宗謂夫惟天佑民也惟辟奉天也與
其自任私智而無益於治孰若自天稽謀乎夫
天聰而已矣人知其馨香則聞穢德則聞赫臨
之下無遁情焉以爲天如是其聰也不知天非
有耳力以爲聽也而聰止於此耶夫天明而已
矣人知其游衍則見出王則見監觀之間無遺
物焉以爲天如是其明也不知天非有目力以
punctuated:
不可缺也。以此勉焉，而得意忘言，則易不在聖人而在我矣。

書
惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。
姚學古

同考試官教諭紀批：天聰明，作者類皆浮泛。此篇以聲氣法象根於理者模寫，得其旨矣。錄之以破群疑。
考試官教諭張批：文有思致。
考試官教授錢批：有見之言。

大臣之望君，欲其與天而爲一焉。蓋天之道出於公也，聖人法天以爲治，寧有外於此哉？傅說以之告高宗，謂夫惟天佑民也，惟辟奉天也。與其自任私智而無益於治，孰若自天稽謀乎？夫天聰而已矣。人知其馨香則聞，穢德則聞，赫臨之下無遁情焉，以爲天如是其聰也。不知天非有耳力以爲聽也，而聰止於此耶？夫天明而已矣。人知其游衍則見，出王則見，監觀之間無遺物焉，以爲天如是其明也。不知天非有目力以
translation_en:
…cannot be dispensed with either. By striving at this, and grasping the meaning while forgetting the words, the Changes will reside not in the sage but in me.

Book of Documents
“Heaven hears and sees clearly; the sage takes this as his model.”
Yao Xuegu

Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: Those writing on Heaven’s clear hearing and sight are generally superficial and vague. This essay portrays sound and vital force, patterns and images, as rooted in principle, and thus captures the purport. It is selected to dispel the many doubts.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The composition shows thoughtful refinement.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: These are words of insight.

What a great minister hopes for from his ruler is that he become one with Heaven. For Heaven’s Way proceeds from impartiality. When the sage models himself on Heaven in governing, how could he depart from this? Fu Yue used this principle to admonish Gaozong, saying that Heaven protects the people and the sovereign serves Heaven. Rather than relying on one’s own private wisdom without benefiting government, would it not be better to consult Heaven for counsel?

Heaven, indeed, hears clearly. People know that it hears fragrant offerings and hears of foul virtue: beneath its august presence, no circumstances can be concealed. They therefore suppose that this is what Heaven’s clear hearing consists in. They do not understand that Heaven does not hear through the power of ears. Could its clear hearing be confined to this?

Heaven, indeed, sees clearly. People know that it sees them when they wander at leisure and sees them when they go forth: nothing escapes its watchful gaze. They therefore suppose that this is what Heaven’s clear sight consists in. They do not understand that Heaven does not possess the power of eyes with which to…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爲視也而明止於此耶自其公之道見於凡物
有聲者言之凡化機之所以自鼓而得於聲氣
之元者孰非此理之流通蓋微而顯虛而靈無
聞而無所不聞也夫是之謂聰乎自其公之道
見於凡物有形者言之凡太虛之所以融結而
至於法象之彰者孰非此理之敷布蓋一而神
兩而化無見而無所不見也夫是之謂明乎天
之道一出於公如此聖人若何而憲天乎蓋法
天之聰則詛呪知之怨汝詈汝亦知之必將爲
===
之宣鬱通滯以平天下之情可謂聽無所壅矣
而聖人猶曰吾尚弗肖於天也法天之明則驩
兜知之令色孔壬亦知之必將爲之除奸剔蠹
以清天下之政可謂視無所蔽矣而聖人猶曰
吾尚有忝於天也天之道於穆不已一息不公
非天也故夫幽獨之所以幾康不異乎大庭之
所以兢業几緝煕敬止咸正無缺也天其有心
之聖人乎天之道純粹至善一念不公非天也
故夫小民之所以顧畏不異於大祭之所以祗
punctuated: 爲視也，而明止於此耶？自其公之道見於凡物有聲者言之，凡化機之所以自鼓而得於聲氣之元者，孰非此理之流通？蓋微而顯，虛而靈，無聞而無所不聞也。夫是之謂聰乎？自其公之道見於凡物有形者言之，凡太虛之所以融結而至於法象之彰者，孰非此理之敷布？蓋一而神，兩而化，無見而無所不見也。夫是之謂明乎？天之道一出於公如此，聖人若何而憲天乎？蓋法天之聰，則詛呪知之，怨汝詈汝亦知之，必將爲之宣鬱通滯，以平天下之情，可謂聽無所壅矣。而聖人猶曰：「吾尚弗肖於天也。」法天之明，則驩兜知之，令色孔壬亦知之，必將爲之除奸剔蠹，以清天下之政，可謂視無所蔽矣。而聖人猶曰：「吾尚有忝於天也。」天之道於穆不已，一息不公，非天也。故夫幽獨之所以幾康，不異乎大庭之所以兢業，几緝煕敬止，咸正無缺也。天其有心之聖人乎？天之道純粹至善，一念不公，非天也。故夫小民之所以顧畏，不異於大祭之所以祗
translation_en:
…to see; could its clear sight be limited to this? Consider the manifestation of Heaven’s impartial Way in all things that have sound: wherever the workings of transformation stir of themselves and draw upon the source of sound and vital energy, what is not the circulation of this principle? Subtle yet manifest, empty yet numinous, it hears nothing and yet leaves nothing unheard. Is this not what is called keen hearing? Consider the manifestation of its impartial Way in all things that have form: wherever the Great Void coalesces, culminating in manifest patterns and images, what is not the unfolding of this principle? One, it is numinous; divided into two, it transforms. It sees nothing and yet leaves nothing unseen. Is this not what is called clear sight?

Since Heaven’s Way proceeds entirely from impartiality in this manner, how should the sage take Heaven as his model? In emulating Heaven’s keen hearing, he knows of curses, and also knows when people resent and revile him. He will surely release their pent-up grievances and clear obstructions, bringing the feelings of all under Heaven into balance. His hearing may thus be called unobstructed. Yet the sage still says: “I do not yet resemble Heaven.” In emulating Heaven’s clear sight, he recognizes Huan Dou, and also recognizes those whose pleasing expressions conceal great treachery. He will surely eliminate the wicked and root out those who prey upon others, purifying the government of all under Heaven. His sight may thus be called unclouded. Yet the sage still says: “I still fall short of Heaven.”

Heaven’s Way is profound and unceasing: were it partial for even a single breath, it would not be Heaven. Thus the care he takes to maintain tranquillity [?] in solitude does not differ from his vigilance in the great court. Through continuing illumination and abiding reverence [?], all is correct and nothing deficient. Might Heaven be a sage possessed of a mind? Heaven’s Way is utterly pure and supremely good: were it partial for even a single thought, it would not be Heaven. Thus the wary respect with which he regards the common people does not differ from the reverence with which he conducts the great sacrifices…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
肅凡篤實光輝自周有終也聖人其無為之天
道乎必如此而後謂之聰明必如是而後謂之
憲天大臣責難之恭於此亦可見矣抑臣之告
君責之以難而不詳以告之則何以感悟君心
也傅說憲天聰明之訓固足為君人出治之綱
要矣而下文以慎言時動任賢事神不矜有備
之說懇懇言之是則所以告嘉猷示同行者詳
且至矣厥後高宗為商哲王何莫不本於傅說
啓沃之功也夫
===
凡厥庶民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子
之光
楊紹震
同考試官教諭紀 批箕子述敷言之化見人君不可
不建極之意此作論感發之機在於君辭約意盡矣佳士佳士
考試官教諭張 批典則
考試官教授錢 批麗而雅
教行於民而德協於君皇極敷言之化也夫敷
言之訓所以一天下之趨者也今歸化於君而
punctuated:
肅，凡篤實光輝，自周有終也。聖人其無為之天道乎？必如此而後謂之聰明，必如是而後謂之憲天。大臣責難之恭，於此亦可見矣。抑臣之告君，責之以難而不詳以告之，則何以感悟君心也？傅說憲天聰明之訓，固足為君人出治之綱要矣。而下文以慎言、時動、任賢、事神、不矜、有備之說，懇懇言之，是則所以告嘉猷、示同行者，詳且至矣。厥後高宗為商哲王，何莫不本於傅說啓沃之功也夫！

凡厥庶民，極之敷言是訓是行，以近天子之光。

楊紹震

同考試官教諭紀批：「箕子述敷言之化，見人君不可不建極之意。此作論感發之機在於君，辭約意盡矣。佳士！佳士！」
考試官教諭張批：「典則。」
考試官教授錢批：「麗而雅。」

教行於民，而德協於君，皇極敷言之化也。夫敷言之訓，所以一天下之趨者也。今歸化於君而
translation_en:
…solemn reverence. All that is substantial and radiant is complete in itself and carried through to the end. Is the sage not Heaven’s Way acting without deliberate effort? Only thus may he be called discerning; only thus may he be said to model himself on Heaven. Here, too, we can see the reverence with which a great minister demands difficult achievements of his ruler. Yet if a minister, in advising his ruler, demands what is difficult without explaining it fully, how can he move and awaken the ruler’s heart? Fu Yue’s instruction to model oneself on Heaven’s discernment certainly suffices as an outline for a ruler’s conduct of government. In the text that follows, however, he speaks earnestly of caution in speech, timely action, employing the worthy, serving the spirits, avoiding self-conceit, and maintaining preparedness. Thus his presentation of good counsels and demonstration of the course they should follow together are detailed and thorough indeed. That Gaozong subsequently became a wise king of Shang—how could this not have rested entirely on Fu Yue’s achievement in enlightening and enriching his mind!

“All the common people take the widely proclaimed words of the supreme standard as their instruction and put them into practice, thereby drawing near to the Son of Heaven’s radiance.”

Yang Shaozhen

Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: “Jizi describes the transforming influence of the proclaimed words, revealing why the ruler must establish the supreme standard. This composition argues that the impetus that moves and awakens people lies with the ruler. Its language is concise and its meaning fully expressed. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Classical and exemplary.”
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: “Elegant and refined.”

Instruction takes effect among the people, and their virtue accords with that of the ruler: such is the transforming influence of the proclaimed words of the August Standard. Instruction through these proclaimed words serves to unify the aspirations of all under Heaven. Now they submit to the ruler’s transforming influence and…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有以近其光焉感應之機固至此哉箕子演皇
極之疇以告武王謂夫天子之於庶民不同者
分而所同者理也皇極敷言之理既發於君而
有不孚乎人耶是故既見聖亦不由聖庶民之
常態也今則漸濡久而善念興曰遵義遵道遵路
諷誦以求其旨凡念茲釋茲所勿忘不懽咎亦
不協極中人之故習也今則觀感深而真機動
曰蕩蕩平平正直吟咏以味其真自一話一言猶
不廢匪徒時而颺之也而且祗遹以紹其聞凡
===
有咎則畢棄者自於是乎乾乾也豈有民彝之
弗褒者耶非特勸而歌之也而且觀省以稽其
德凡非幾則勿貢者將於此乎孜孜也豈有天
道之實悖者耶若是者何以為近天子之光哉
吾知惟皇作極而覃被四表之文煌煌乎不可
尚矣然在上有以慎其麗而在下有以勸其刑
實一理之相為感格惟王造哲而誕敷四海之
光炳炳乎不可掩矣然在上有以爽厥師而在
下有以從厥乂實一心之自為流通全體昭晰
punctuated: 有以近其光焉，感應之機固至此哉！箕子演皇極之疇以告武王，謂夫天子之於庶民，不同者分，而所同者理也。皇極敷言之理既發於君，而有不孚乎人耶？是故既見聖亦不由聖，庶民之常態也。今則漸濡久而善念興，曰遵義、遵道、遵路，諷誦以求其旨，凡念茲釋茲所勿忘。不懽咎亦不協極，中人之故習也。今則觀感深而真機動，曰蕩蕩、平平、正直，吟咏以味其真，自一話一言猶不廢。匪徒時而颺之也，而且祗遹以紹其聞，凡有咎則畢棄者，自於是乎乾乾也，豈有民彝之弗褒者耶？非特勸而歌之也，而且觀省以稽其德，凡非幾則勿貢者，將於此乎孜孜也，豈有天道之實悖者耶？若是者，何以為近天子之光哉？吾知惟皇作極，而覃被四表之文煌煌乎不可尚矣。然在上有以慎其麗，而在下有以勸其刑，實一理之相為感格。惟王造哲，而誕敷四海之光炳炳乎不可掩矣。然在上有以爽厥師，而在下有以從厥乂，實一心之自為流通。全體昭晰，
translation_en:
…and thereby draw near to his radiance. Can the workings of stimulus and response indeed reach such a point! Jizi expounded the section on the Imperial Ultimate to King Wu, explaining that what distinguishes the Son of Heaven from the common people is their station, while what they share is principle. Once the principle expressed in the Imperial Ultimate’s proclaimed teachings has issued from the ruler, could it fail to win the people’s trust?

To encounter a sage yet not follow him is the common people’s usual disposition. Now, however, after long immersion in his influence, good thoughts arise. They recite, “Follow righteousness, follow the Way, follow the path,” seeking the meaning through repeated recitation. In thinking upon these words and expounding them, they do not forget them. Neither delighting in wrongdoing nor conforming to the Ultimate is the habitual condition of people of middling character. Now, however, their deep response to what they observe stirs their true moral impulse. They chant, “Broad and open, level and even, upright and straight,” savoring the truth through recitation, neglecting not even a single phrase or word.

They do not merely proclaim these teachings at the proper times; they also reverently follow them, carrying forward what they have heard. In wholly casting away whatever is blameworthy, they henceforth exert themselves unceasingly. How could the people’s constant moral norms fail to be exalted? They do not merely encourage one another and sing these teachings; they also observe and examine themselves, scrutinizing their virtue. In presenting nothing that does not accord with the subtle workings of goodness [?], they will apply themselves diligently. How could they truly depart from the Way of Heaven?

Why does conduct such as this constitute drawing near to the Son of Heaven’s radiance? I know that it is the sovereign who establishes the Ultimate, and that the civilizing influence extending to the four bounds shines with unsurpassable brilliance. Yet those above attend carefully to what they adhere to, while those below strive to emulate their example: this is truly the mutual stirring and penetration of a single principle. It is the king who brings forth wisdom, and the radiance spread widely throughout the Four Seas shines too brightly to be concealed. Yet those above enlighten their multitudes, while those below submit to their governance: this is truly the free circulation of a single heart. The whole is luminously clear…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雖未能盡如君道之備也而丕變之餘日異而
月不同矣豈不庶幾焉爾乎大用顯行固未能
遽擬天德之純也而維新之下月異而歲不同
矣又何遠之有乎用是觀之則知上下一心也
而孚格之機由於上君臣一體也而倡率之道
在於君有天下者其亦知所懋哉抑論之民從
所好違所令也久矣而箕子何取夫言敎也蓋
敷言之敎以君德爲之本而非在言語文字之
間後世此義不明而徒以法把持天下故說愈
===
詳而無益於治若蘇威介甫之類可鑒也然則
爲王道謀者如之何曰當求箕子所以敷言之
意
詩
彼茁者葭壹發五豝于嗟乎騶虞彼茁者
蓬壹發五豵于嗟乎騶虞
龐嵩
同考試官敎諭余 批是作不事華藻而仁恩仁心剖
析明白可與言詩矣
punctuated:
雖未能盡如君道之備也，而丕變之餘，日異而月不同矣，豈不庶幾焉爾乎？大用顯行，固未能遽擬天德之純也，而維新之下，月異而歲不同矣，又何遠之有乎？用是觀之，則知上下一心也，而孚格之機由於上；君臣一體也，而倡率之道在於君。有天下者，其亦知所懋哉！抑論之，民從所好，違所令也久矣，而箕子何取夫言敎也？蓋敷言之敎，以君德爲之本，而非在言語文字之間。後世此義不明，而徒以法把持天下，故說愈詳，而無益於治，若蘇威、介甫之類可鑒也。然則爲王道謀者如之何？曰：當求箕子所以敷言之意。
詩
彼茁者葭，壹發五豝，于嗟乎騶虞！彼茁者蓬，壹發五豵，于嗟乎騶虞！
龐嵩
同考試官敎諭余批：是作不事華藻，而仁恩仁心剖析明白，可與言詩矣。
translation_en:
…Although they cannot yet fully attain the completeness of the ruler’s Way, following the great transformation they change from day to day and from month to month. Are they not approaching it? In their great undertakings and manifest conduct, they certainly cannot immediately rival the purity of Heaven’s virtue; yet under this renewal they change from month to month and from year to year. How far away, then, can that attainment be? Viewed in this light, those above and below are of one mind, but the impulse that moves others through sincerity originates above; ruler and ministers form one body, but the responsibility for taking the lead rests with the ruler. Should not he who possesses all under Heaven know where to direct his efforts?
To consider the matter further: the people have long followed what their rulers favor while disregarding what they command. Why, then, did Jizi value instruction through words? Because instruction through the promulgation of words is rooted in the ruler’s virtue, rather than residing in spoken or written language itself. Later generations failed to understand this principle and sought merely to control all under Heaven through laws. Thus their pronouncements grew ever more detailed without benefiting government. Men such as Su Wei and Jiefu [Wang Anshi] offer cautionary examples. What, then, should those who seek the Kingly Way do? The answer is: they should seek to understand Jizi’s intention in promulgating words.
Book of Odes
Those luxuriant reeds!
One shot, five sows!
Ah, the Zouyu!
Those luxuriant wormwood plants!
One shot, five young boars!
Ah, the Zouyu!
Pang Song
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: This composition does not strive for ornate embellishment, but clearly analyzes humane beneficence and the humane heart. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss the Odes.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭曾批題意本易冗雜是作獨潔淨可觀錄之
考試官教諭張批温厚和平
考試官教授錢批諷咏有不盡意
詩人美諸侯必兩叙其仁恩之及物而嘆其仁
心之自然也夫恩及庶類惟天下之至仁能之
也是宜詩人重嘆而深美之歟南國諸侯承文
王之化能脩身齊家以治其國而詩人美之意
謂言治者以仁民愛物為全功言仁者以萬物
===
得所為極至孰不知我侯及物之仁者耶盖自
春田之際而觀之是故植吾知其為葭也則茁
然而壯盛動吾知其為豝也則一發而中五以
此徵之則凡南國之中將無一人不得其所可
見矣是盖至仁之無恩皆自然而然之機而萬
物之並生有不疾而速之化于嗟乎騶虞之仁
得於天性而我侯實同之也其形體之異吾何
知焉載觀茁然者不惟葭也而蓬亦如其盛一
發而五者不惟豝也而縱亦如其番以此推之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭曾批：題意本易冗雜，是作獨潔淨可觀，錄之。
考試官教諭張批：温厚和平。
考試官教授錢批：諷咏有不盡意。
詩人美諸侯，必兩叙其仁恩之及物，而嘆其仁心之自然也。夫恩及庶類，惟天下之至仁能之也，是宜詩人重嘆而深美之歟！南國諸侯承文王之化，能脩身齊家以治其國，而詩人美之。意謂言治者，以仁民愛物為全功；言仁者，以萬物得所為極至。孰不知我侯及物之仁者耶？盖自春田之際而觀之，是故植，吾知其為葭也，則茁然而壯盛；動，吾知其為豝也，則一發而中五。以此徵之，則凡南國之中，將無一人不得其所，可見矣。是盖至仁之無恩，皆自然而然之機，而萬物之並生，有不疾而速之化。于嗟乎！騶虞之仁得於天性，而我侯實同之也，其形體之異，吾何知焉？載觀茁然者，不惟葭也，而蓬亦如其盛；一發而五者，不惟豝也，而縱亦如其番。以此推之，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: “The theme readily lends itself to prolixity and clutter, but this composition alone is clean and clear, and merits attention. Include it.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Gentle and generous, harmonious and balanced.”
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “Reciting it brings out inexhaustible meaning.”
When the poet praises the feudal lords, he twice recounts how their benevolent favor reaches other creatures, and marvels at the spontaneity of their benevolent hearts. Only those of the utmost benevolence under Heaven can extend favor to all kinds of beings. Surely it is fitting that the poet should repeatedly marvel at this and praise it so deeply! Receiving King Wen’s transforming influence, the feudal lords of the southern lands cultivated themselves and regulated their households in order to govern their states, and the poet praised them. His meaning is that, in discussing government, its complete achievement consists in benevolence toward the people and care for other creatures; in discussing benevolence, its highest attainment consists in all things finding their proper place. Who does not know our lord’s benevolence, which reaches even other creatures?
Consider the spring hunt. Among growing things, we recognize the reeds, sprouting vigorously and flourishing; among moving creatures, we recognize the sows, five of which are struck with a single discharge. From this evidence we can see that throughout the southern lands there will be no person who fails to find a proper place. This is surely the utmost benevolence bestowing no deliberate favor [?]: all proceeds through spontaneous workings, while the myriad things grow together under a transforming influence that is swift without haste. Ah! The benevolence of the zouyu comes from its Heaven-given nature, and our lord truly shares it. What do I care about the difference in their bodily forms?
Looking again, it is not only the reeds that sprout vigorously: the mugwort flourishes just as abundantly. Nor is it only sows that number five at a single discharge: the young boars [?] likewise appear in matching numbers [?]. Extending this reasoning …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則凡蓬豵之外將無一物不盡其性又可知矣
是蓋至和之欝積既有以流通乎兩間而大化
之宣昭自有以發舒乎品彙于嗟乎騶虞之仁
本於天賦而我侯寔類之也其形迹之殊又何
知焉是則政以昭德德以顯仁仁以及物諸侯
之可美若此文王之化於是詩不有可稽哉抑
論之文王之化不特及於南國也桃夭之化及
女子兔罝之化及武夫遠而江漢汝墳莫不然
非特南國諸侯之賢而文王過化存神之妙有
===
不可誣者不然當紂之時王室如燬非文王之
怙冒西土人且弗獲自盡而况庶類之蕃殖耶
嗚呼此騶虞為鵲巢之應而季札之歌二南深
美之也歟
樂只君子邦家之基樂只君子萬壽無期
陳道
同考試官教諭余 批美德祝壽乃古人尊賓實意予
善模寫之宜錄以式
同考試官教諭曾 批辭意溫醇寫出當時美祝氣象
punctuated:
則凡蓬豵之外，將無一物不盡其性，又可知矣。是蓋至和之欝積，既有以流通乎兩間，而大化之宣昭，自有以發舒乎品彙。于嗟乎！騶虞之仁，本於天賦，而我侯寔類之也，其形迹之殊，又何知焉？是則政以昭德，德以顯仁，仁以及物，諸侯之可美若此，文王之化於是詩不有可稽哉？抑論之，文王之化不特及於南國也。《桃夭》之化及女子，《兔罝》之化及武夫，遠而江漢、汝墳，莫不然。非特南國諸侯之賢，而文王過化存神之妙，有不可誣者。不然，當紂之時，王室如燬，非文王之怙冒西土，人且弗獲自盡，而况庶類之蕃殖耶？嗚呼！此《騶虞》為《鵲巢》之應，而季札之歌《二南》深美之也歟？

樂只君子，邦家之基；樂只君子，萬壽無期。
陳道

同考試官教諭余批：美德祝壽，乃古人尊賓實意。予善模寫之，宜錄以式。

同考試官教諭曾批：辭意溫醇，寫出當時美祝氣象
translation_en:
…then we may also know that, beyond the luxuriant plants and young boars, there will be no creature that does not fully realize its nature. The accumulated abundance of perfect harmony thus circulates between Heaven and Earth, while the manifest workings of the great transforming power unfold among all kinds of beings. Ah! The benevolence of the zouwu is endowed by Heaven, and our lord truly resembles it. What account need I take of their differences in outward form and conduct? Thus government manifests virtue, virtue reveals benevolence, and benevolence extends to all creatures. If the feudal lords deserve such praise, can we not find evidence of King Wen’s transforming influence in this poem?

Moreover, King Wen’s transforming influence did not reach only the southern states. The influence celebrated in “Peach Tree, Tender and Young” (Tao yao) reached women; that in “Rabbit Nets” (Tu ju) reached warriors. Even as far away as the Jiang and Han rivers and the banks of the Ru, it was everywhere so. This was not merely the worthiness of the southern lords: the marvel of King Wen’s transforming influence wherever he passed, and his spiritual efficacy wherever he dwelt, cannot be denied. Otherwise, in the time of Zhou, when the royal house was like a raging fire, had King Wen not sheltered and protected the western lands, even human beings could not have fully realized their capacities. How much less could the many kinds of creatures have multiplied and flourished? Ah! Is this not why “The Zouwu” (Zou yu) answers “The Magpie’s Nest” (Que chao), and why Ji Zha so deeply praised the songs of the Two Southern Sections (Er nan) when they were performed?

“Joyful is the noble gentleman, the foundation of the state and ruling house; joyful is the noble gentleman, may his ten thousand years of life have no end.”
Chen Dao

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, School Instructor: Praising virtue and wishing long life express the ancients’ sincere intention in honoring their guests. I commend the depiction of this; it should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, School Instructor: The language and meaning are gentle and pure, conveying the spirit of praise and benediction of that time…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可式多士
考試官教諭張批婉曲有味
考試官教授錢批誠愛之情溢於言外
詩人於所燕之賓美其德而祝其壽焉夫德福
相因自然之符也觀詩人燕賓而必以是祝美
焉其尊之之隆何如哉此燕饗通用之樂蓋謂
君之燕臣也非優禮無以通堂陛之情臣之與
燕也非齒德無以為國家之望吾觀在燕君子
人品之高明足以消人慢易之態器度之渾厚
===
足以動人親愛之誠信如是其可樂也是故我
觀其德焉德底於老成而浚明亮采之不器望
隆於篤棐而左宜右有之皆能上而輔君可為
麴蘖塩梅而天子是毗也下而脩政可為蕃宣
藩屏而王國是楨也蓋信乎為邦家之基矣然
是樂只君子吾何以願之哉蓋其德望之隆既
負重大之寄必壽考之永可樹高遠之勳吾將
願其貞固以為體申離祉於靈長平格以為徵
獲純嘏於保合身其用康而胡考之休蓋首五
punctuated:
可式多士。
考試官教諭張批：婉曲有味。
考試官教授錢批：誠愛之情溢於言外。
詩人於所燕之賓，美其德而祝其壽焉。夫德福相因，自然之符也。觀詩人燕賓而必以是祝美焉，其尊之之隆何如哉！此燕饗通用之樂，蓋謂君之燕臣也。非優禮，無以通堂陛之情；臣之與燕也，非齒德，無以為國家之望。吾觀在燕君子，人品之高明，足以消人慢易之態；器度之渾厚，足以動人親愛之誠。信如是其可樂也！是故我觀其德焉：德底於老成，而浚明亮采之不器；望隆於篤棐，而左宜右有之皆能。上而輔君，可為麴蘖塩梅，而天子是毗也；下而脩政，可為蕃宣藩屏，而王國是楨也。蓋信乎為邦家之基矣！然是樂只君子，吾何以願之哉？蓋其德望之隆，既負重大之寄，必壽考之永，可樹高遠之勳。吾將願其貞固以為體，申離祉於靈長；平格以為徵，獲純嘏於保合。身其用康，而胡考之休，蓋首五
translation_en:
… may serve as a model for the many candidates.
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Subtle and graceful, with lasting savor.”
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “Feelings of sincere affection overflow beyond the words.”
The poet praises the virtue of the guests entertained at the feast and wishes them longevity. Virtue and blessings give rise to one another: this is a correspondence inherent in nature. When we see that the poet invariably offers these wishes and praises when entertaining guests, how profound is the honor he accords them! This music, used generally at banquets, refers here to a ruler entertaining his ministers. Without generous ceremonial treatment, the feelings of those above and below the throne cannot be brought into communion. Nor can ministers who attend the banquet command the esteem of the realm without seniority and virtue. I observe that the gentlemen at the banquet possess a loftiness and clarity of character sufficient to dispel others’ contemptuous attitudes, and a breadth and generosity of bearing sufficient to awaken sincere affection. Truly, such men deserve to be rejoiced in!
Thus I consider their virtue. Their virtue has reached seasoned maturity; deeply discerning and accomplished in their duties, they are not confined to a single function. Their prestige rests upon their devoted assistance; suited to service on either hand, they are capable in every task. Above, in assisting their ruler, they can act as ferment and malt, salt and plums, sustaining the Son of Heaven. Below, in putting government in order, they can serve as bulwarks and screens, upholding royal authority and acting as pillars of the kingdom. Truly they are the foundation of the state!
Yet what wishes should I offer this gentleman in whom we rejoice? Since his eminent virtue and reputation have already brought him weighty responsibilities, he must enjoy a long life if he is to establish lofty and far-reaching achievements. I would wish that steadfastness form the substance of his being, and that blessings repeatedly attend him throughout his enduring years; that peace and rectitude be their manifest sign [?], and that he receive abundant blessings through preserving harmony. May his person enjoy health; and the blessing of great old age surely ranks first among the five…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
福而與國無疆者矣惟性惟爾彌而萬年之祿矣
作三朋而與天無極者矣夫燕所以昭德也德
所以徵壽也主人之尊賓孰有大於是哉抑舜
之戒禹曰不矜不伐言持滿之難也而何周王
燕臣乃美德祝壽得無驕其志歟蓋德不可僞
爲壽不可幸致美之所以規之祝之所以勉之
也後世之燕臣者至有拔劒擊柱之風後庭玉
樹之曲君臣規戒之意安在哉噫南山之賦眞
可以爲訓矣
===
春秋
冬鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳襄公二十有五年
叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋
向戌衛齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭
罕虎許人曹人于虢昭公元年
李景元
同考試官教諭黃批子產以禮相鄭處發揮殆盡是
蓋深于春秋者
考試官教諭張批有斷制
punctuated:
福而與國無疆者矣。惟性惟爾彌而萬年之祿矣，作三朋而與天無極者矣。夫燕所以昭德也，德所以徵壽也。主人之尊賓，孰有大於是哉？抑舜之戒禹曰：「不矜不伐。」言持滿之難也。而何周王燕臣，乃美德祝壽，得無驕其志歟？蓋德不可僞爲，壽不可幸致；美之所以規之，祝之所以勉之也。後世之燕臣者，至有拔劒擊柱之風、後庭玉樹之曲，君臣規戒之意安在哉？噫！南山之賦，眞可以爲訓矣。

春秋

冬，鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳。襄公二十有五年。
叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。昭公元年。

李景元

同考試官教諭黃批：「子產以禮相鄭處，發揮殆盡，是蓋深于春秋者。」
考試官教諭張批：「有斷制。」
translation_en:
… blessings, and endure without limit alongside the state. Only your nature, only you [?]—blessings for ten thousand years; forming three companies [?], enduring without limit alongside Heaven.

A banquet serves to make virtue manifest, and virtue serves as a sign of longevity. How could a host honor his guests more greatly than this? Yet Shun admonished Yu, saying, “Neither be conceited nor boast,” speaking of the difficulty of maintaining prosperity at its height. Why, then, did the king of Zhou, when feasting his ministers, praise their virtue and wish them longevity? Might this not make them proud? Virtue cannot be counterfeited, and longevity cannot be attained by mere good fortune. Praising them is thus a means of admonishing them; blessing them is a means of encouraging them. In later ages, rulers’ banquets for ministers even featured such conduct as drawing swords and striking pillars, and songs such as Jade Trees of the Rear Courtyard. Where was the intention that ruler and ministers should admonish and caution one another? Ah! The poem Southern Mountain truly can serve as an instructive example.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In winter, Gongsun Xia of Zheng led an army to attack Chen.” Twenty-fifth year of Duke Xiang.

“Shusun Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and men of Xu and Cao.” First year of Duke Zhao.

Li Jingyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The passage on Zichan’s use of ritual propriety in assisting the government of Zheng develops the subject almost exhaustively. This is surely someone with a deep understanding of the Spring and Autumn Annals.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Shows decisive judgment.”

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授錢批〔得傳意〕
春秋紀賢臣有所以抑内霸者有所以抑外夷
者蓋禮國之幹也子產於晉楚而能以禮抑之
春秋安得不書其事以彰其賢哉且魯襄末年
中國之大勢在晉蓋其席屢世主盟之威所臨
莫之敢抗也惟時公孫夏以師伐陳而獻捷于
晉當時侵小之問晉之所以易鄭者何如使無
人爲之干城則鄭以削弱之國而當表裏山河
之勢土崩瓦解之時也可危也哉惟子產也氣
===
正而理明忠激而詞勁論莊宣賴以入國既有
以鳴陳人刊木之横援城濮命以輔王又有以
服莊伯戎服之詰卒使晉人遂納其俘載禮其
使焉夫以北方之國莫强於晉而能折之以成
命是晉之勢不足懾而在我之禮有足恃者噫
僑之相鄭允矣社稷之衞乎魯昭初年天下之
大勢在楚蓋其恃蠻夷積强之勢所至莫之敢
撄也維時公子圍因于虢之會僞逆女於鄭當
時衷甲之謀楚之所以窺鄭者何如使無人焉
punctuated:
考試官教授錢批〔得傳意〕

春秋紀賢臣，有所以抑内霸者，有所以抑外夷者。蓋禮，國之幹也。子產於晉楚而能以禮抑之，春秋安得不書其事以彰其賢哉？且魯襄末年，中國之大勢在晉，蓋其席屢世主盟之威，所臨莫之敢抗也。惟時公孫夏以師伐陳，而獻捷于晉。當時侵小之問，晉之所以易鄭者何如？使無人爲之干城，則鄭以削弱之國，而當表裏山河之勢，土崩瓦解之時也，可危也哉！惟子產也，氣正而理明，忠激而詞勁。論莊宣賴以入國，既有以鳴陳人刊木之横；援城濮命以輔王，又有以服莊伯戎服之詰。卒使晉人遂納其俘載，禮其使焉。夫以北方之國莫强於晉，而能折之以成命，是晉之勢不足懾，而在我之禮有足恃者。噫！僑之相鄭，允矣社稷之衞乎！魯昭初年，天下之大勢在楚，蓋其恃蠻夷積强之勢，所至莫之敢撄也。維時公子圍因于虢之會，僞逆女於鄭。當時衷甲之謀，楚之所以窺鄭者何如？使無人焉
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: 〔Captures the purport of the Commentary.〕

In recording worthy ministers, the Spring and Autumn Annals records some who checked the hegemonic powers within the Chinese states and others who checked the non-Chinese peoples beyond them. Ritual propriety is the mainstay of a state. Since Zichan could use ritual propriety to restrain Jin and Chu, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to record his deeds and make manifest his worthiness?

Now, in the final years of Duke Xiang of Lu, the preponderance of power among the central states lay with Jin. Drawing upon the authority accumulated through successive generations of leadership over the covenant assemblies, it encountered none who dared resist it. At that time, Gongsun Xia led an army against Chen and presented the spoils of victory to Jin. In its questioning of this attack upon a smaller state, how contemptuously Jin treated Zheng! Had there been no one to serve as its shield and rampart, Zheng, a weakened state, would have faced a power protected by mountains and rivers. It would have been a moment of utter collapse. How perilous!

Zichan alone was upright in spirit and clear in reasoning, impassioned in loyalty and forceful in speech. By discussing how Zhuang and Xuan had relied upon assistance to enter their states [?], he exposed the outrageous conduct of the men of Chen in cutting down trees. By invoking the charge at Chengpu to assist the king, he also rebutted Zhuangbo’s questioning about military dress. In the end, he induced the men of Jin to accept the captives and booty and to treat Zheng’s envoy with due ceremony. Although no northern state was stronger than Jin, he could check it by invoking an established command. Thus Jin’s power was insufficient to intimidate him, while the ritual principles on his own side provided sufficient grounds for confidence. Ah! In assisting Zheng, Qiao truly was a defender of its altars of soil and grain!

In the early years of Duke Zhao of Lu, the preponderance of power under Heaven lay with Chu. Relying upon the accumulated strength of a non-Chinese power, it encountered none who dared challenge it. At that time, Prince Wei took advantage of the meeting at Guo and made a pretext of fetching a bride from Zheng. In its plot to conceal armor beneath clothing, what designs Chu had upon Zheng! Had there been no one there …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之砥柱則鄭以挫困之邦而當帶甲百萬之雄
河决魚爛之秋也可懼也哉幸僑也幾審而慮
熟氣昌而備周爰築在外之館既有以陰折其
奸而不愛豐氏之桃又有以飽塞其欲卒之楚
人垂橐而入會虢以還焉夫南方之國莫强於
楚而能拒之以弭患是楚之勢不足畏而吾人
之禮有足憑者吁僑之在鄭展哉邦家之基乎
夫以子産在鄭而强國終莫能屈其賢可知矣
宜春秋備書而樂道之也歟抑鄭一也鄭忽以
===
無故而失守子産以多難而興邦何也大要在
志不在力而亦由簡公推轂之功也不然魯之
有叔孫豹猶鄭之有子産也何鄭國以振而昭
不免其身哉以是知人才係國之重輕而人君
以用賢爲急
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
戚〔襄公五年〕
林時雨
punctuated:
之砥柱，則鄭以挫困之邦而當帶甲百萬之雄，河决魚爛之秋也，可懼也哉！幸僑也幾審而慮熟，氣昌而備周，爰築在外之館，既有以陰折其奸；而不愛豐氏之桃，又有以飽塞其欲。卒之楚人垂橐而入，會虢以還焉。夫南方之國莫强於楚，而能拒之以弭患，是楚之勢不足畏，而吾人之禮有足憑者。吁！僑之在鄭，展哉，邦家之基乎！夫以子産在鄭，而强國終莫能屈，其賢可知矣。宜《春秋》備書而樂道之也歟！抑鄭一也，鄭忽以無故而失守，子産以多難而興邦，何也？大要在志不在力，而亦由簡公推轂之功也。不然，魯之有叔孫豹，猶鄭之有子産也，何鄭國以振而昭不免其身哉？以是知人才係國之重輕，而人君以用賢爲急。
公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚〔襄公五年〕。
林時雨
translation_en:
…to serve as a bulwark, then Zheng, a battered and beleaguered state confronting a mighty power with a million armored soldiers, would have faced a time of bursting rivers and utter decay. How fearful that would have been! Fortunately, Qiao discerned the first signs of danger and deliberated thoroughly; his spirit was vigorous and his preparations comprehensive. He therefore built lodgings outside the city, thereby quietly frustrating their treacherous design. By not begrudging the Feng clan’s peach tree [?], he also fully satisfied their desires. In the end, the men of Chu entered with their bags hanging down [?], attended the meeting at Guo, and returned. No southern state was stronger than Chu, yet he could resist it and avert disaster. Thus Chu’s power was insufficient to inspire fear, while the ritual propriety on our side provided sufficient support. Ah! With Qiao in Zheng, he was indeed the foundation of the state!
With Zichan in Zheng, the powerful states ultimately proved unable to subdue it: his worth is evident. Surely it was fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded these matters fully and delighted in recounting them! Yet it was the same Zheng: Hu of Zheng lost his hold on the state when there was no crisis, whereas Zichan revived it amid many troubles. Why? The essential consideration lay in resolve rather than strength; it also owed something to Duke Jian’s merit in advancing and supporting him. Otherwise, Lu’s possession of Shusun Bao was like Zheng’s possession of Zichan: why did Zheng flourish while Duke Zhao could not even secure his own person? From this we know that men of talent determine a state’s standing, and that a ruler must make employing the worthy his urgent concern.
“The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, and men of Wu and Zeng at Qi.” 〔Fifth year of Duke Xiang〕
Lin Shiyu

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭黃批深得聖人與人爲善之意不徒
曰文
考試官敎諭張批辭約而義章
考試官敎授錢批嚴整
遠人慕義而守禮春秋所以進之也夫中國禮
義之大宗也遠人旣能慕而守之春秋安得不
取其善而進之哉且夫春秋嚴華夷之大防故
吳自郯之伐以號舉矣今戚之會遂進之以人
何耶夫邦交人道之大倫也使其不知慕義而
===
坐致乎諸侯亦不足取今則慕我中國之聲敎
遣壽越以請後會之期惟以不得與樽俎之間
爲辱此其心誠其志切視諸侯往與之會大不
侔矣會盟中國之盛典也使其不知守禮而爲
主於諸侯則尤可惡今則受吾中國之號令甘
後名以締歸好之懽惟以不得廁衣裳之後爲
愧此其禮恭其事順其視屈服諸侯偃然爲主
大不同矣夫前此鷄澤之役會吳子而不至是
其憑陵之威已著晉人方懼其蠶食也而况親
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭黃批：深得聖人與人爲善之意，不徒曰文。
考試官敎諭張批：辭約而義章。
考試官敎授錢批：嚴整。
遠人慕義而守禮，春秋所以進之也。夫中國，禮義之大宗也。遠人旣能慕而守之，春秋安得不取其善而進之哉？且夫春秋嚴華夷之大防，故吳自郯之伐以號舉矣。今戚之會，遂進之以人，何耶？夫邦交，人道之大倫也。使其不知慕義而坐致乎諸侯，亦不足取。今則慕我中國之聲敎，遣壽越以請後會之期，惟以不得與樽俎之間爲辱。此其心誠，其志切，視諸侯往與之會，大不侔矣。會盟，中國之盛典也。使其不知守禮而爲主於諸侯，則尤可惡。今則受吾中國之號令，甘後名以締歸好之懽，惟以不得廁衣裳之後爲愧。此其禮恭，其事順，其視屈服諸侯、偃然爲主，大不同矣。夫前此鷄澤之役，會吳子而不至，是其憑陵之威已著，晉人方懼其蠶食也，而况親
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “This deeply grasps the Sage’s intention of helping others to do good; it is more than mere literary composition.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The wording is concise and the meaning clear.”
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “Rigorous and orderly.”
When people from afar admire righteousness and observe ritual propriety, the Spring and Autumn Annals accords them higher standing. The Central States are the great fountainhead of ritual propriety and righteousness. Once people from afar can admire and observe these, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to acknowledge their goodness and accord them higher standing? Moreover, the Spring and Autumn Annals strictly maintains the great boundary between the civilized and the outsiders. Thus, from the attack on Tan onward, Wu was recorded by its state designation alone. Yet at the meeting at Qi, it was raised to the designation “men of Wu.” Why?
Relations between states constitute one of the great bonds of human society. If Wu did not know to admire righteousness, but merely induced the feudal lords to come to it without stirring itself, there would be nothing worthy of approval. Now, however, it admired the renown and civilizing instruction of our Central States and dispatched Shou Yue to request the date of a subsequent meeting. It regarded exclusion from the sacrificial vessels and banquet tables as a disgrace. Its heart was sincere and its resolve earnest: this was very different from the feudal lords going to meet with it.
Meetings and covenants are grand institutions of the Central States. If Wu did not know to observe ritual propriety but presided over the feudal lords, that would be especially reprehensible. Now, however, it accepted the commands of our Central States and willingly let its name be placed after the others, securing the joy of friendly relations. It regarded being unable to take a place behind those in ceremonial robes as a source of shame. Its ritual conduct was reverent and its actions compliant: this was very different from subjugating the feudal lords and arrogantly presiding over them.
Previously, at the gathering at Jize, the Viscount of Wu was invited to the meeting but did not come. His overbearing might was already evident, and the people of Jin were then afraid of his gradual encroachments; how much less could they have expected him to draw close …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於中國乎詩曰出自幽谷遷于喬木若吴亦可
謂能遷善矣何意棄義之國而能慕義如此耶
後此黃池之會與晉人而爭長是其倔强之勢
以萌中國方憂其虎視也而况主於晉伯乎易
曰困于臲卼動悔有悔若吴可謂悔過矣何意
棄禮之國而能守禮如此耶是故聞其名則非
較其行則是取其今則是追其往則非此春秋
進吴而稱人樂與人爲善之心一至此哉抑吴
之與楚與徐越皆聖賢之裔夏之變於夷也犯
===
順則狄之悔過則進之此聖人無絕人與天地
相似也若純於夷者豈可通哉故潜之會唐之
盟以號外之觀此而知聖人之書法本之以謹
嚴行之以忠恕
禮記
朝諸侯分職授政任功曰予一人
葉成章
同考試官訓導王 批本題曰予一人處包括大正見
人君有任重之意此作獨能闡之誠爲可錄
punctuated:
於中國乎？《詩》曰：「出自幽谷，遷于喬木。」若吴亦可謂能遷善矣，何意棄義之國而能慕義如此耶？後此黃池之會，與晉人而爭長，是其倔强之勢以萌，中國方憂其虎視也，而况主於晉伯乎？《易》曰：「困于臲卼，動悔，有悔。」若吴可謂悔過矣，何意棄禮之國而能守禮如此耶？是故聞其名則非，較其行則是；取其今則是，追其往則非。此《春秋》進吴而稱人，樂與人爲善之心一至此哉！抑吴之與楚、與徐、越，皆聖賢之裔，夏之變於夷也。犯順則狄之，悔過則進之，此聖人無絕人，與天地相似也。若純於夷者，豈可通哉？故潜之會、唐之盟，以號外之。觀此而知聖人之書法，本之以謹嚴，行之以忠恕。

禮記
朝諸侯，分職授政，任功，曰「予一人」。
葉成章
同考試官訓導王批：本題「曰予一人」處，包括大，正見人君有任重之意。此作獨能闡之，誠爲可錄。
translation_en:
…toward the Central States? The Book of Odes says: “Leaving the secluded valley, they ascend to lofty trees.” Wu, too, may be said to have turned toward goodness. Who would have expected a state that had abandoned righteousness to admire righteousness so deeply? Later, at the meeting at Huangchi, Wu contended with the men of Jin for precedence. Its defiant ambition had already begun to emerge, and the Central States were apprehensive of its predatory gaze; how much more so at its claiming precedence over Jin, the hegemon? The Book of Changes says: “Beset by instability; movement brings regret. There is repentance.” Wu may be said to have repented of its faults. Who would have expected a state that had abandoned ritual propriety to observe it so faithfully?

Thus, judging by its designation, one condemns it; examining its conduct, one approves it. Considering its present actions, one approves it; tracing its past, one condemns it. This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals advances Wu by calling its representatives “men.” How far this willingness to help others do good extends! Moreover, Wu, Chu, Xu, and Yue all descend from sages and worthies: they represent peoples of the Xia tradition who became barbarians. When they violate the proper order, the sage treats them as barbarians; when they repent, he advances them. In refusing to reject anyone utterly, the sage resembles Heaven and Earth. But how could those wholly barbarian be admitted? Thus, in recording the meeting at Qian and the covenant at Tang, he uses their rulers’ titles to mark them as outsiders. From this we know that the sage’s manner of writing rests on scrupulous rigor and is carried out with conscientiousness and sympathetic understanding.

Book of Rites
“When receiving the feudal lords at court, distributing offices and entrusting governmental duties, and assigning undertakings, he calls himself ‘I, the One Man.’”
Ye Chengzhang
Associate Examiner Wang, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “The words ‘he calls himself “I, the One Man”’ in this topic embrace a broad meaning, precisely revealing the ruler’s sense of bearing a weighty responsibility. This composition is singularly able to elucidate that meaning and truly deserves inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張批精粹
考試官教授錢批筆勢雄逹
記者論大君聽治而及自稱之辭所以寓責望
之意也蓋天子以天下爲己任也即其辭則所
以求踐其實者將不敢不用其力矣且夫天降
下民而作之君何以奉若天道以寵綏四方哉
此其責任誠爲重且大矣是故諸侯國之衛也
職民之麗也貴有以貞憲也于是乎五服各朝
於方岳考制同度而黜陟惟明六卿各倡乎屬
===
牧簡脩進良而貴賤式序分焉有所統也位焉
有所維也非以貞其憲耶政國之紀也功德之
樹也貴有以昭度也于是乎欽乃攸司列其宅
事宅牧宅準以觀其能嘉乃底績量其三德六
德九德以大其受政惟于其凝也功惟于其勸
也非以昭其度耶然天子於此必自稱曰予一
人者何也蓋天下之責望於君者固甚周而人
君之自任以天下者亦甚重以德威則欲其懷
也以知人則欲其哲也而所以聯屬成身者必
punctuated:
考試官教諭張批：精粹。
考試官教授錢批：筆勢雄逹。
記者論大君聽治而及自稱之辭，所以寓責望之意也。蓋天子以天下爲己任也，即其辭，則所以求踐其實者，將不敢不用其力矣。且夫天降下民而作之君，何以奉若天道，以寵綏四方哉？此其責任誠爲重且大矣。是故諸侯，國之衛也；職，民之麗也，貴有以貞憲也。于是乎五服各朝於方岳，考制同度，而黜陟惟明；六卿各倡乎屬牧，簡脩進良，而貴賤式序。分焉有所統也，位焉有所維也，非以貞其憲耶？政，國之紀也；功，德之樹也，貴有以昭度也。于是乎欽乃攸司，列其宅事、宅牧、宅準，以觀其能；嘉乃底績，量其三德、六德、九德，以大其受。政惟于其凝也，功惟于其勸也，非以昭其度耶？然天子於此必自稱曰「予一人」者，何也？蓋天下之責望於君者固甚周，而人君之自任以天下者亦甚重。以德威則欲其懷也，以知人則欲其哲也，而所以聯屬成身者，必
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Refined and substantial.”
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “The writing has a vigorous, expansive flow.”
The compiler of the Record of Rites discusses the great ruler’s conduct of government and also addresses the words by which he refers to himself, thereby conveying the responsibilities and expectations placed upon him. For the Son of Heaven takes responsibility for all under Heaven. Considering his words, he surely will not dare spare his strength in seeking to fulfill their substance. Heaven brought forth the people below and established a ruler for them: how is he to follow Heaven’s Way reverently and cherish and bring peace to the four quarters? His responsibility is indeed weighty and great.
Thus, the regional lords are the realm’s defenses, and offices are that to which the people attach themselves. What matters is having the means to set the governing statutes firmly in place. Accordingly, those of the five service zones each attend court at the sacred mountain of their quarter; institutions are examined and measures standardized, while demotions and promotions are clearly determined. The six ministers each lead their subordinate governors, selecting the cultivated and advancing the worthy, so that higher and lower ranks are duly ordered. Divisions of responsibility have a unifying authority, and official positions have a sustaining framework. Is this not how the governing statutes are firmly established?
Government is the ordering framework of the realm; achievement is the establishment of virtue. What matters is having the means to make the governing standards manifest. Accordingly, reverence is required in the duties entrusted to officials: those appointed to administrative affairs, to govern the people, and to administer justice are set out in their respective posts so that their abilities may be observed. Their accomplishments are commended, and their possession of three virtues, six virtues, or nine virtues is assessed so that what they receive may be enlarged. Government is to be consolidated, and achievement encouraged. Is this not how the governing standards are made manifest?
Yet why must the Son of Heaven here refer to himself as “I, the one man”? It is because the responsibilities and expectations that all under Heaven place upon the ruler are indeed comprehensive, while the ruler’s own undertaking of responsibility for all under Heaven is also exceedingly weighty. In exercising virtue and awe-inspiring authority, he seeks to win their allegiance; in knowing men, he seeks discerning wisdom. But to link them together into a single body, he must…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
獨運乾綱以操張弛闔闢之權以庶績則欲其
熈也以明試則欲其當也而所以宅中圖治者
必皇建有極以攬予奪廢置之柄不特小民之
祁寒暑雨怨乎我而山川鬼神亦以爲主誠遺
之以艱大而不可逸欲焉者不曰予一人而何
稱哉不特造化之雨暘燠寒風之徵於我而凡
鳥獸魚鱉亦以爲天誠投之以毖闕而不可狎
侮焉者不曰予一人而何謂哉是則欲爲四方
之主當顧一人之名記者斯言其責望之意可
===
謂詞約而義該矣抑能盡予一人之道者惟二
帝三王可以當之後世大綱正者近於霸萬目
舉者雜於夷若議論多而成功少亦不足以爲
至治而要之大學之道皆未之聞也是故聖人
作則必以天地爲本然後可南面治天下而謂
之予一人
天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣流而不
息合同而化而樂興焉
punctuated:
獨運乾綱，以操張弛闔闢之權。以庶績則欲其熈也，以明試則欲其當也，而所以宅中圖治者，必皇建有極，以攬予奪廢置之柄。不特小民之祁寒暑雨怨乎我，而山川鬼神亦以爲主，誠遺之以艱大而不可逸欲焉者，不曰予一人而何稱哉？不特造化之雨暘燠寒風之徵於我，而凡鳥獸魚鱉亦以爲天，誠投之以毖闕而不可狎侮焉者，不曰予一人而何謂哉？是則欲爲四方之主，當顧一人之名。記者斯言，其責望之意，可謂詞約而義該矣。抑能盡予一人之道者，惟二帝三王可以當之。後世大綱正者近於霸，萬目舉者雜於夷，若議論多而成功少，亦不足以爲至治，而要之大學之道皆未之聞也。是故聖人作則，必以天地爲本，然後可南面治天下而謂之予一人。

天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣；流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。
translation_en:
…must alone wield the sovereign authority of Heaven, controlling the power to tighten and relax, to close and open. In the many affairs of government, he wishes accomplishments to flourish; in clearly testing officials, he wishes assessments to be fitting. To occupy the center and plan good government, he must establish the supreme standard as sovereign and retain the authority to grant and take away, dismiss and appoint. It is not merely that the common people complain against me during bitter cold or summer rains: the spirits of mountains and rivers also regard me as their lord. Truly, one entrusted with such great and difficult responsibilities cannot indulge in ease and desire. If he does not call himself “I, the one man,” what should he call himself? It is not merely that nature’s rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind manifest signs corresponding to my conduct: all birds, beasts, fish, and turtles also regard me as their Heaven. Truly, one charged with guarding against failings must not treat these responsibilities with careless contempt. If he does not say “I, the one man,” what should he say? Thus, whoever wishes to be lord of the four quarters must attend to the designation “the one man.” These words of the author of the Record express the responsibilities and expectations placed upon the ruler; they may indeed be called concise in wording yet comprehensive in meaning.

Yet only the Two Emperors and Three Kings can be counted as having fully realized the Way of “I, the one man.” In later ages, those who set the principal framework right approached hegemonic rule, while those who attended to every detail mingled their practices with those of the barbarians. Those who offered much discussion but achieved little were likewise incapable of bringing about the highest order of government. In sum, none had heard the Way of the Great Learning. Therefore, when the sage establishes standards, he must take Heaven and Earth as his foundation. Only then can he face south, govern all under Heaven, and call himself “I, the one man.”

Heaven is high and Earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct, and the institutions of ritual operate. They flow without cease, unite and transform, and music arises.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導王批〔此作能於造化上體認禮樂之〕
〔妙是亦文之粹者用錄以式〕
考試官敎諭張批〔深得禮樂之本〕
考試官敎授錢批〔辭氣充〕
記者論造化具禮樂之妙所以原聖人制作之
本也蓋禮樂不外序與和焉爾矣而造化具有
此妙焉禮樂之時義大矣哉記者之意以為禮
樂之道人知其制出於聖人而不知其端肇於
造化自夫以禮言之夫天輕清以浮象塊然居
===
高不可升地重濁以凝形隤然在下不可極至
於親上而各為聚散大大小小分其群親下而
自為榮枯形形色色殊其態蓋分而言之萬物
各具一太極也若是而謂禮制之行者蓋天地
之道貞觀即截然等威儀則之不可移萬物之
化川流即燦然品節文章之不可亂於凡直而
行也經而等也推而進也放而文也凡所以為
序之至者皆流行於高下散殊之間矣故即造
化以名禮不亦可耶以樂言之天道本陽而陰
punctuated:
同考試官訓導王批〔此作能於造化上體認禮樂之〕〔妙，是亦文之粹者，用錄以式。〕
考試官敎諭張批〔深得禮樂之本。〕
考試官敎授錢批〔辭氣充。〕
記者論造化具禮樂之妙，所以原聖人制作之本也。蓋禮樂不外序與和焉爾矣，而造化具有此妙焉。禮樂之時義大矣哉！記者之意，以為禮樂之道人知其制出於聖人，而不知其端肇於造化。自夫以禮言之，夫天輕清以浮象，塊然居高不可升；地重濁以凝形，隤然在下不可極。至於親上而各為聚散，大大小小分其群；親下而自為榮枯，形形色色殊其態。蓋分而言之，萬物各具一太極也。若是而謂禮制之行者，蓋天地之道貞觀，即截然等威儀則之不可移；萬物之化川流，即燦然品節文章之不可亂。於凡直而行也，經而等也，推而進也，放而文也，凡所以為序之至者，皆流行於高下散殊之間矣。故即造化以名禮，不亦可耶？以樂言之，天道本陽而陰
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: 〔This composition apprehends, within the processes of creation and transformation, the〕〔subtle workings of ritual and music. It is also a refined piece of writing; it is recorded here to serve as a model.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔It profoundly grasps the foundations of ritual and music.〕
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: 〔Its language and expressive force are ample.〕
The author of the Record discusses how creation and transformation embody the subtle workings of ritual and music, thereby tracing the foundations of the sages’ institutions. Ritual and music amount simply to order and harmony, and creation and transformation possess these very subtleties. Great indeed is the significance of ritual and music in their relation to the times! The author’s meaning is that people know the institutions of ritual and music came from the sages, but do not know that their beginnings originated in creation and transformation.
Speaking first of ritual: Heaven, light and clear, floats forth as celestial images, standing solidly [?] on high, beyond ascent; Earth, heavy and turbid, congeals into form, lying broadly below, beyond fathoming. As for things drawn to what is above, they gather and disperse, great and small separating into their respective groups; things drawn to what is below flourish and wither of themselves, their varied forms and colors distinguishing their appearances. Considered separately, each of the myriad things possesses a Supreme Ultimate.
To describe this as the operation of ritual institutions means that the constant manifestation of the Way of Heaven and Earth is itself the clear and immutable ordering of ranks, dignities, deportment, and standards; the riverlike flow of the transformations of the myriad things is itself the brilliant and inviolable arrangement of gradations, distinctions, and patterned adornment. In everything that proceeds uprightly, establishes regular ranks, advances through extension, or takes models to produce refinement, all that brings order to its fullest realization flows among these differences of height and depth, dispersal and distinction. Is it not therefore fitting to identify ritual in creation and transformation itself? Speaking of music: the Way of Heaven is fundamentally yang, while yin…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爲之盪絪縕初無停機地道本柔而剛爲之交
互藏亦無定宅至於親上者皆本於天相見於
亨嘉之會親下者皆本於地均獲夫保合之休
蓋總而言之萬物同囿一太極也若是而謂之
樂與者蓋二氣之無動無靜即律呂變而旋爲
宫萬彙之並育並生即金石諧而從其律於凡
清明也廣大也周旋也終始也凡所以爲和之
至者皆具於流行合同之間矣故即造化而謂
之樂亦何不可耶是則禮樂之道天地不能隱
===
其藏人物不能秘其蘊聖人不過法其自然之
妙而制作之耳而豈有違於造化者哉雖然天
地設位聖人成能是必與天地合德而後禮樂
可興也姑舉舜觀之重華協帝德已至矣故命
官制禮作樂以致天下風動鳳凰來儀噫必如
此無愧於造化也後世禮成於綿蕞曲士樂成
於唐山夫人如此類者相望也又何禮樂之足
云
第貳場
punctuated:
爲之盪，絪縕初無停機；地道本柔，而剛爲之交，互藏亦無定宅。至於親上者，皆本於天，相見於亨嘉之會；親下者，皆本於地，均獲夫保合之休。蓋總而言之，萬物同囿一太極也。若是而謂之樂與者，蓋二氣之無動無靜，即律呂變而旋爲宫；萬彙之並育並生，即金石諧而從其律。於凡清明也，廣大也，周旋也，終始也，凡所以爲和之至者，皆具於流行合同之間矣。故即造化而謂之樂，亦何不可耶？是則禮樂之道，天地不能隱其藏，人物不能秘其蘊，聖人不過法其自然之妙而制作之耳，而豈有違於造化者哉？雖然，天地設位，聖人成能，是必與天地合德，而後禮樂可興也。姑舉舜觀之，重華協帝，德已至矣，故命官制禮作樂，以致天下風動，鳳凰來儀。噫！必如此，無愧於造化也。後世禮成於綿蕞曲士，樂成於唐山夫人，如此類者相望也，又何禮樂之足云？

第貳場
translation_en:
…stirs it into activity, and their intermingling never pauses. The Way of earth is fundamentally yielding, yet the firm joins with it; as they conceal themselves within one another, neither has a fixed abode. Those that have affinity with what is above all take their origin from heaven and encounter one another in a convergence of flourishing and auspiciousness. Those that have affinity with what is below all take their origin from earth and equally enjoy the blessing of preservation and union. Taken together, the myriad things all dwell within a single Supreme Ultimate. To speak of music in this connection is to say that the two vital forces, beyond motion and stillness, correspond to the changing pitch standards, which take turns serving as the fundamental note, gong; and that the myriad kinds, growing and living together, correspond to the harmony of bells and chime stones, each following its pitch standard. Clarity and brightness, breadth and greatness, cyclical movement, endings and beginnings—all that constitutes the utmost harmony is present within this flowing movement and union. Why, then, should we not speak of the workings of creation themselves as music?

Thus, as regards the Way of ritual and music, heaven and earth cannot hide what they contain, nor can people and things conceal what lies within them. The sages merely model themselves upon the subtle workings of their natural spontaneity and give them institutional form. How could this run counter to creation? Nevertheless, heaven and earth establish their positions, and the sages bring their capacities to fulfillment. Only after one's virtue accords with that of heaven and earth can ritual and music flourish. Consider Shun as an example: Chonghua, as Shun was called, accorded with the emperor, and his virtue had already reached perfection. He therefore appointed officials to establish ritual and compose music, causing all under heaven to respond as if moved by the wind, and the phoenixes to come and display their stately bearing. Ah! Only in this way can one be worthy of creation. In later ages, ritual was fashioned by narrow scholars marking ceremonial positions with bundles of reeds, and music by Lady Tangshan. Such figures appeared one after another. What ritual or music worthy of the name could there be to speak of?

Second Session

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
論
上下與天地同流
梁津
同考試官教諭謝批此題王道本於天德當在有心
無爲處見之是作筆老意新而步驟縱逸通微之思鎮俗之體
眞妙於文哉
同考試官學正甯批聖人制法以民故曰有心無爲
非無爲也惟無爲故化與天地無爲一矣此作發聖人有爲之
迹以妙無爲之化其無爲之文矣乎錄之
===
考試官教諭張批明暢
考試官教授錢批理勝
聖人之道與天地參當自其純王之心之政而
觀之也神也者言乎純王之心也化也者言乎
純王之政也而所以謂之純王則廓然大公而
物來順應之妙也非心之外別有神而政之外
別有化也然聖人此心之神非謂寂然一無所
事而謂之神也夫以一身爲天下民物之主凡
有一夫之失所一物之不若其性吾之責也而
punctuated:
論
上下與天地同流
梁津

同考試官教諭謝批：此題王道本於天德，當在有心無爲處見之。是作筆老意新，而步驟縱逸，通微之思，鎮俗之體，眞妙於文哉！

同考試官學正甯批：聖人制法以民，故曰有心無爲，非無爲也。惟無爲，故化與天地無爲一矣。此作發聖人有爲之迹，以妙無爲之化，其無爲之文矣乎！錄之。

考試官教諭張批：明暢。

考試官教授錢批：理勝。

聖人之道與天地參，當自其純王之心之政而觀之也。神也者，言乎純王之心也；化也者，言乎純王之政也。而所以謂之純王，則廓然大公而物來順應之妙也。非心之外別有神，而政之外別有化也。然聖人此心之神，非謂寂然一無所事而謂之神也。夫以一身爲天下民物之主，凡有一夫之失所，一物之不若其性，吾之責也，而
translation_en:
Discourse
“Above and below, flowing together with Heaven and Earth”
Liang Jin 梁津

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: This topic concerns the kingly Way’s foundation in Heaven’s virtue. Its meaning should be discerned in having intention while acting without deliberate intervention. This composition displays a seasoned brush and fresh ideas, while its progression is free and unrestrained. Its thought penetrates subtleties, and its manner steadies vulgar tastes. Truly a marvel of writing!

Comment by Associate Examiner Ning, Instructor: The sage establishes institutions for the people; thus he is said to have intention while acting without deliberate intervention. This does not mean doing nothing. It is precisely through nonaction that his transforming influence becomes one with the nonaction of Heaven and Earth. This composition reveals the traces of the sage’s purposeful action, thereby bringing out the subtlety of his transformation through nonaction. Might it itself be writing achieved through nonaction? Include it in the record.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Clear and fluent.

Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: Outstanding in its reasoning.

The sage’s Way forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. We should consider it through his purely kingly mind and government. “Spiritual efficacy” refers to the purely kingly mind; “transformation” refers to purely kingly government. What makes these purely kingly is the subtle capacity to be expansively impartial and to respond fittingly as things present themselves. There is no separate spiritual efficacy outside the mind, nor any separate transformation outside government. Yet to speak of the spiritual efficacy of this mind of the sage is not to call it spiritually efficacious because it rests in stillness, attending to nothing whatsoever. For, as the single person who is lord of all the people and things under Heaven, he regards any one man’s failure to find his proper place, or any one thing’s failure to accord with its nature, as his own responsibility; and …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可不用其心哉是故無心而成化者天地也有
心而無為者聖人也其迹若不同矣而德業之
盛則一而二二而一者也嗚呼此孟軻氏未發
之意而君子擴之以盡王道也歟請昌其說夫
古聖賢之論治而必舉天地以為配者天地妙
太極之真精道之至者也中庸曰大德敦化小
德川流此天地之所以為大也是以聖人配天
地也易曰顯諸仁藏諸用鼓萬物而不與聖人
同憂是言聖人不如天地之無憂也夫天地能
===
盡物聖人能盡民是聖人與天地同一道也而
曰不與聖人同憂何哉甚矣天地可以無心成
化而口代天言身代天工者不可不以心存天
下也以心存天下而猶謂之存神者雖有心也
而實無為也非實無為也而以有為為應迹以
明覺為自然也是之謂神妙不測而普於無心
也則與天地何害其為同哉今夫聖人之於天
下也無為而民自朴不動而民自變若可以優
游拱手而求觀厥成矣聖人之心猶欿然曰天
punctuated:
可不用其心哉？是故無心而成化者，天地也；有心而無為者，聖人也。其迹若不同矣，而德業之盛，則一而二、二而一者也。嗚呼！此孟軻氏未發之意，而君子擴之以盡王道也歟？請昌其說。
夫古聖賢之論治，而必舉天地以為配者，天地妙太極之真，精道之至者也。《中庸》曰：「大德敦化，小德川流。」此天地之所以為大也，是以聖人配天地也。《易》曰：「顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。」是言聖人不如天地之無憂也。夫天地能盡物，聖人能盡民，是聖人與天地同一道也。而曰「不與聖人同憂」，何哉？甚矣！天地可以無心成化，而口代天言、身代天工者，不可不以心存天下也。以心存天下，而猶謂之存神者，雖有心也，而實無為也。非實無為也，而以有為為應迹，以明覺為自然也。是之謂神妙不測，而普於無心也，則與天地何害其為同哉？
今夫聖人之於天下也，無為而民自朴，不動而民自變，若可以優游拱手而求觀厥成矣。聖人之心猶欿然曰：「天
translation_en:
…could he refrain from applying his mind? Thus, Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without conscious intent; the sage has conscious intent yet acts without contrivance. Their outward manifestations may seem different, but in the fullness of their virtue and achievements, they are one yet two, and two yet one. Ah! Is this an implication that Meng Ke left unexpressed, which the gentleman expands to bring the Way of the true king to its fullest extent? Allow me to amplify this explanation.
When the ancient sages and worthies discussed government, they invariably invoked Heaven and Earth as its counterpart because Heaven and Earth wondrously embody the reality of the Supreme Ultimate and bring the Way to its utmost refinement. The Doctrine of the Mean says: “Great virtue brings generous transformation; lesser virtues flow like streams.” This is what makes Heaven and Earth great, and it is through this that the sage matches Heaven and Earth. The Book of Changes says: “It manifests itself in benevolence and conceals itself in its workings, stirring the myriad things without sharing the sage’s anxieties.” This means that the sage is unlike Heaven and Earth in their freedom from anxiety. Heaven and Earth can bring things to fulfillment, and the sage can bring the people to fulfillment: the sage and Heaven and Earth thus share a single Way. Why, then, does it say that they do not share the sage’s anxieties? How profound this is! Heaven and Earth can accomplish transformation without conscious intent, but one whose mouth speaks for Heaven and whose person performs Heaven’s work cannot fail to keep the realm in his thoughts. Why is keeping the realm in his thoughts nevertheless called preserving spiritual efficacy? Although he has conscious intent, he truly acts without contrivance. It is not that he actually does nothing; rather, he regards deliberate action as the outward manifestation of his responses, and lucid awareness as what is natural. This is what is called being spiritually wondrous and unfathomable, and all-pervading without conscious intent. What, then, prevents him from being at one with Heaven and Earth?
Now, in the sage’s relation to the realm, he acts without contrivance and the people become simple of themselves; he remains unmoved and the people change of themselves. It would seem that he could remain at ease with folded hands and watch the accomplishment unfold. Yet the sage remains dissatisfied in his heart, saying: “All under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
下之民吾同胞也而吾不爲之正德利用厚生
何以代天理物哉於是乎以三農生九穀以百
工飭八材以商賈通貨賄以嬪婦治絲枲以慈
幼以養老以振窮以恤貧以寛疾以安富至於
瘖者實土聾者司火刖者守囿墨者守門侏者
扶廬各以器食之而孤者獨者矜者寡者皆有
常餼盈天地間似無棄人矣猶未已也而達之
以三德擾之以五典命之以九儀開之以六物
稽之以九法糾之以五刑申之以五禁凡正其
===
行而强之道者聖人無不用心以爲之所以聯
師儒以篤父子以睦兄弟以和賓客以正軍旅
以嚴諸侯必使比相保閭相受族相葬黨相救
州相賙鄉相賓聖人純王之政可謂具舉而畢
張矣其究也以於變以丕應以風動以允懐以
攸同以咸若以率俾問之在朝在野而皆不知
此之謂所過者化所存者神也是故清和象元
氣變通象陰陽昭明象日月文華象星辰潤澤
象風雨威靈象雷霆高大象山岳靜深象江漢
punctuated: 下之民，吾同胞也，而吾不爲之正德、利用、厚生，何以代天理物哉？」於是乎，以三農生九穀，以百工飭八材，以商賈通貨賄，以嬪婦治絲枲，以慈幼，以養老，以振窮，以恤貧，以寛疾，以安富。至於瘖者實土，聾者司火，刖者守囿，墨者守門，侏者扶廬，各以器食之，而孤者、獨者、矜者、寡者皆有常餼。盈天地間，似無棄人矣。猶未已也，而達之以三德，擾之以五典，命之以九儀，開之以六物，稽之以九法，糾之以五刑，申之以五禁。凡正其行而强之道者，聖人無不用心以爲之。所以聯師儒，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以和賓客，以正軍旅，以嚴諸侯，必使比相保，閭相受，族相葬，黨相救，州相賙，鄉相賓。聖人純王之政，可謂具舉而畢張矣。其究也，以於變，以丕應，以風動，以允懐，以攸同，以咸若，以率俾，問之在朝在野，而皆不知。此之謂所過者化，所存者神也。是故清和象元氣，變通象陰陽，昭明象日月，文華象星辰，潤澤象風雨，威靈象雷霆，高大象山岳，靜深象江漢。
translation_en:
…the people under Heaven are my siblings. If I do not rectify their virtue, facilitate their use of resources, and enrich their livelihood, how can I govern things on Heaven’s behalf?” Accordingly, the sage employs farmers of the three kinds of land to grow the nine grains, the various artisans to work the eight materials, merchants to circulate goods and wealth, and women to process silk and hemp. He cherishes the young, supports the aged, relieves the destitute, assists the poor, eases the burdens of the sick, and secures the wealthy. Even the mute are employed to work the soil, the deaf to tend fires, those punished by amputation of a foot to guard parks, those punished by tattooing to guard gates, and dwarfs to support the lodges [?]. Each is provided a livelihood according to his capacities, while orphans, the elderly without children, widowers, and widows all receive regular provisions. Throughout Heaven and Earth, it seems that no one is cast aside.
Yet the sage does not stop there. He brings them to fulfillment through the three virtues, guides them through the five teachings, gives them their charges through the nine ceremonial distinctions, enlightens them through the six subjects of instruction, examines them through the nine regulations, corrects them through the five punishments, and admonishes them through the five prohibitions. In everything that rectifies their conduct and urges them toward the Way, the sage devotes his full attention to the task. Thus he brings teachers and scholars into association, strengthens the bonds between fathers and sons, fosters affection between brothers, brings harmony among guests, orders the armies, and instills reverence among the feudal lords. He ensures that households in each bi guarantee one another’s conduct, those in each lü accommodate one another, those in each zu assist with one another’s burials, those in each dang aid one another in emergencies, those in each zhou relieve one another’s needs, and those in each xiang receive one another as honored guests. The sage’s government of pure kingly rule may be said to have been fully instituted and completely put into effect.
Its ultimate results are transformation, a great response, movement as though stirred by the wind, sincere allegiance, unity, universal compliance, and obedience. Yet if one questions those at court and those outside it, none knows how this has come about. This is what is meant by: “Where he passes, transformation takes place; where he abides, his influence is spirit-like.” Thus his purity and harmony resemble the primal vital force; his adaptability resembles yin and yang; his radiance resembles the sun and moon; his patterned splendor resembles the stars; his nourishing beneficence resembles wind and rain; his awe-inspiring power resembles thunder; his loftiness resembles the mountains; and his stillness and depth resemble the Yangzi and Han rivers…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而天之所覆地之所載凡有血氣莫不尊親至
此則不知孰為天地孰為聖人孰為天地聖人
之神化矣謂非與天地同流而何哉抑聖人非
特有同於天地也書五雲掌十煇齊七政宣八
風開九州濬九河以至殺妖鳥攻猛獸蜡昆虫
伐陽木高黍下稻服牛乘馬是又此心之神輔
相天地之所不及而足以參乎天地矣其誰曰
聖人之有心不如天地之無心哉至是而知聖
人惟有純心而後有純政此王道之高出伯道
===
而此心之時義為尤大也抑孟子之論所以辨
伯者驩虞之民不若王者皥皥之民也君子不
論其民而論其心者心者萬事之根本也夫王
者之所以純王之心曰欽明曰允塞曰祗台曰
懋昭曰建極要在以誠意為之本故其功效與
天地參彼伯者久假不歸與王道如碔砆美玉
之相反也又何怪功烈之如彼其卑哉是故有
天德然後可語王道有誠意然後可語天德
表
punctuated:
而天之所覆，地之所載，凡有血氣，莫不尊親。至此，則不知孰為天地，孰為聖人，孰為天地聖人之神化矣。謂非與天地同流而何哉？抑聖人非特有同於天地也：書五雲，掌十煇，齊七政，宣八風，開九州，濬九河，以至殺妖鳥，攻猛獸，蜡昆虫，伐陽木，高黍下稻，服牛乘馬，是又此心之神輔相天地之所不及，而足以參乎天地矣。其誰曰聖人之有心不如天地之無心哉？至是而知聖人惟有純心，而後有純政，此王道之高出伯道，而此心之時義為尤大也。
抑孟子之論，所以辨伯者驩虞之民不若王者皥皥之民也。君子不論其民而論其心者，心者萬事之根本也。夫王者之所以純王之心，曰欽明，曰允塞，曰祗台，曰懋昭，曰建極，要在以誠意為之本，故其功效與天地參。彼伯者久假不歸，與王道如碔砆美玉之相反也，又何怪功烈之如彼其卑哉？是故有天德，然後可語王道；有誠意，然後可語天德。
表
translation_en:
…and among all living beings beneath heaven’s covering and borne upon the earth, none fails to revere and cherish him. At this point, one can no longer distinguish heaven and earth from the sage, or distinguish their wondrous transforming powers. What could this be called, if not sharing in the same flow as heaven and earth? Yet the sage does more than merely resemble heaven and earth. He records the five kinds of clouds, oversees the ten kinds of luminous atmospheric phenomena, regulates the seven celestial governors—the sun, moon, and five planets—and gives free course to the winds of the eight directions. He opens up the Nine Provinces and dredges the nine rivers. He even kills portentous birds, attacks fierce beasts, performs the zha sacrifice concerning insects [?], fells trees on sunny slopes, plants millet on high ground and rice on low ground, harnesses oxen, and rides horses. In these things, the wondrous power of his heart assists heaven and earth where their workings fall short, enabling him to stand alongside them as a third power. Who, then, would say that the sage’s conscious purpose is inferior to heaven and earth’s absence of conscious purpose? From this we understand that only after the sage possesses a pure heart can he establish pure government. This is why the Kingly Way rises above the Way of the Hegemon, and why the timely exercise of this heart has especially great significance.
Moreover, Mencius’s discussion distinguishes the joyfully contented people under a hegemon from the people under a true king, whose broad and untroubled ease surpasses theirs. Why does the gentleman discuss the ruler’s heart rather than his people? Because the heart is the root of all affairs. What enables a true king to make his kingly heart pure is expressed in such phrases as “reverent and discerning,” “truly sincere,” “reverently fulfill my charge,” “strive to make virtue manifest,” and “establish the supreme standard.” The essential point is to take sincerity of intention as the foundation. Thus his achievements rank alongside those of heaven and earth. Those hegemons borrow virtue for so long that they never return it; their relation to the Kingly Way is like the opposition between a jade-like stone and fine jade. Why, then, be surprised that their accomplishments are so inferior? Therefore, only with heavenly virtue can one speak of the Kingly Way; only with sincerity of intention can one speak of heavenly virtue.
Memorials

translation_en:
Memorial Expressing Thanks for the Bestowal of the Six Statutes of the Tang, Composed in the Persona of Zeng Gong of the Song, in the Fifth Year of Yuanfeng [1082].
By Li Zhaolong.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: Recent memorials often let their language exceed their reasoning and their ornament exceed their substance. This piece alone is classical and well regulated, detailed and clear; it also quietly conveys loyal devotion. Surely its author has accumulated learning while awaiting his opportunity!
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: He weighs the Six Statutes against the needs of the times and deeply understands the principles of consulting antiquity to establish offices. Most commendable, most commendable!
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Appropriate to the form.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: Classical and elegant.
On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of Yuanfeng, your servant Gong, holding the duly specified office, having recently received through Your Majesty’s sage benevolence a copy of the Six Statutes, in profound awe and trepidation bows his head to the ground twice and submits these words:
I humbly consider that Yin took the age of Xia as its mirror, though fidelity and simplicity were said to be their different ideals; Zhou followed the rites of Shang, and its omissions and additions drew upon both earlier traditions. You have thus extended the munificence of your gracious bestowal and magnificently displayed the brilliance of this splendid text. The honor surpasses that of the robes of the five ranks; before receiving it reverently, I hasten to purify myself three times with incense.
I reflect that, in naming offices after dragons, clouds, birds, and fire, the sages exalted their institutions so as to honor the worthy; in assigning offices to spring, summer, autumn, and winter, enlightened kings bequeathed plans for diligent service. They ordered the offices of chief minister, the Four Peaks, regional governors, and chiefs, clearly distinguishing those who rendered illustrious service and those who discharged particular duties. Their provision extended even to the details of mountains, marshes, rivers, and forests, including officials in charge of kudzu and of bitter herbs. …the Sui system. Accordingly, men such as Jiuling were assembled, and the book Six Statutes (Liudian) was completed. It divided responsibilities and assigned tasks, establishing officials to coordinate military and agricultural affairs; it distinguished the regions and laid out the countryside, fixing rents and taxes to bring well-being to the people. It concentrated essential affairs in the Department of State Affairs, embodying the principle of leadership by the chief minister; it placed the various officials under the Six Ministries, retaining a framework of direction and supervision. It abolished such extravagant designations as “Terrace of the Phoenix” and “Pavilion of the Phoenix,” making names correct and language appropriate; it addressed [?] the abuses of officials numerous enough to be carried by cartloads and measured by bushels, so that, once the main cord was raised, the meshes of administration spread into order. Its organization entirely followed the model of the Zhou, and its institutions seemed to surpass those of earlier dynasties. Yet the great ministries and the Nine Courts were established side by side, like ten hands lifting a single pot; the Four Directorates and the Six Ministers checked one another, like two Chuis added to four Yis. The Treasury and Granaries sections did not administer money and grain, leaving their functions nearly empty; the Directorate of Waterways did not manage mountains and rivers, leaving its title almost without substance. Perhaps the intention expressed in “The Unicorn’s Hoof” was imperfectly fulfilled; but could the legacy intended to secure the welfare of descendants have been unsound?
Unexpectedly, the surviving text remained and happened to receive Your Majesty’s solitary attention during the second watch of the night. Eminent scholars corrected its textual errors, and it was carved into printing blocks as a treasure of the inner palace. These pearls and jades were brought forth from the imperial repositories and distributed to the distinguished men of the outer court.
This, we humbly recognize, is because we have encountered 〇〇〇〇, whose sagacious endowments attain the wisdom of a sage and whose mighty decisiveness equals that of the spirits.
