郡既無撫字之勞留附中書豈有對揚之
punctuated:
丕圖而遠馭，將增祖武之光。俯矜登瀧抱槧之謠，載新易轍改絃之化。謂司徒司馬政權不宜歸之樞府三司，謂太僕太常事體不應分之判院判寺。官多寄禄，文士遥領乎外班；事靡定員，舊臣始兼乎資政。固循晉周之成式，更定未遑；至來億育之建言，眞切可據。蓋屢朝欲為之先志，逮今日始發乎淵衷。取六典以摹，賜群臣可為準今酌古；集諸儒而詳定官品，方將臨制决疑。官悉罷乎空名，詔傳宣政；班遂頒於新秩，禮出明堂。載歌周雅之德音，庸踵皐謨之常吉。冠裳動色，精炫田龍；中外騰懽，聲諧岡鳳。
竊念臣資性偃蹇，弗適時宜，過誤頻仍，屢寬嚴譴。出知外郡，既無撫字之勞；留附中書，豈有對揚之
translation_en:
…governing far and wide under the grand imperial design, you will add lustre to your ancestors’ achievements. Deigning to heed the songs of those climbing the rapids and carrying writing tablets [?], you renew the work of transformation by changing course and retuning the strings. You hold that the governing powers of the Minister of Education and Minister of War should not devolve upon the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Three Fiscal Commissions, and that the business of the Court of the Imperial Stud and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices should not be divided among officials assigned to direct bureaus and courts. Many offices merely provide stipends, while literary officials nominally hold appointments outside the central court; duties have no fixed personnel, while senior ministers concurrently hold posts in the Hall of Aid to Governance [?]. The established arrangements of Jin and Zhou were indeed followed, with no opportunity to revise them; then came the proposals of Lai Yiyu [?], precise, pertinent, and fit to serve as a basis. Thus an intention cherished by successive reigns, which they had wished to carry out, has only today found expression in your profound imperial heart. You take the Six Statutes as a model and bestow it upon your ministers, enabling them to establish standards for the present while weighing ancient practice. You assemble the scholars to determine official ranks in detail, and will personally decide doubtful matters. All empty official titles are abolished; the decree is transmitted at Xuanzheng [?]. Places in the court hierarchy are accordingly assigned under the new ranking, and ritual issues from the Hall of Light. We sing anew the virtuous strains of the Elegantiae of Zhou, thereby continuing the enduring good fortune promised in the Counsels of Gao Yao. Those in official caps and robes brighten with delight, their radiance outshining the dragon in the field; rejoicing rises within and beyond the court, its sound harmonizing with the phoenix upon the ridge.
I humbly reflect that your servant is by disposition proud and unbending, ill suited to the needs of the times. My faults and errors have been frequent, yet you have repeatedly spared me severe censure. Sent out to administer a distant prefecture, I rendered no meritorious service in nurturing its people; retained in attendance upon the Secretariat, how could I have contributed to requiting and proclaiming your…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
補伏願
學典終始
心單緝熈精厲開元謹日中之戒釁萌天寶懷
城復之防旁求姚宋之材恤人言而畏天
變永杜幽燕之警子庶民以柔遠人臣無
任感
恩仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
===
謝以
聞
第叄塲
策
第一問
潘庭楠
同考試官教諭謝批〔此策事詳而覈辭典而章於〕
〔二聖合一之學推廣不遺閎深浩博乎豈凡士也耶敬羡敬羡〕
同考試官學正甯批〔此策於我〕
punctuated:
補。伏願學典終始，心單緝熈，精厲開元，謹日中之戒；釁萌天寶，懷城復之防。旁求姚宋之材，恤人言而畏天變；永杜幽燕之警，子庶民以柔遠人。臣無任感恩仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄塲
策
第一問
潘庭楠
同考試官教諭謝批〔此策事詳而覈，辭典而章，於〕〔二聖合一之學，推廣不遺，閎深浩博乎！豈凡士也耶？敬羡！敬羡！〕
同考試官學正甯批〔此策於我〕
translation_en:
… benefit. I humbly wish that Your Majesty sustain your learning from beginning to end and devote your heart to continuing illumination [?]. When striving vigorously, as in the Kaiyuan era, heed the warning implicit in the sun at midday; when seeds of trouble emerge, as in the Tianbao era, remain mindful of the danger of the city wall collapsing back into its moat. Seek widely for men of the abilities of Yao Chong and Song Jing; take heed of what people say and stand in awe of Heaven’s portents. Forever forestall alarms from You and Yan; cherish the common people as your children and thereby conciliate those afar. Your servant cannot contain his gratitude for your grace, his reverence for your sageliness, or his intense emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Pan Tingnan
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔This policy essay is detailed and exact in its treatment of affairs, classical and lucid in its language. Concerning〕〔the two sages’ learning of unity, it develops the subject fully, omitting nothing. How capacious, profound, vast, and comprehensive! Can its author be an ordinary scholar? Respect and admiration! Respect and admiration!〕

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖天子邃於心學之妙頗能言其槩末復重一敬字其亦涵濡而有得者歟
考試官教諭張批言有忠愛
考試官教授錢批典則
人君動靜合一之學天德王道之本也蓋
靜所以效天下之至動者也不虛則無以
利用動所以涵天下之至靜者也不直則
無以立本故虛則存神然後妙應物之感
也由是而畜義焉以幸群生以命百物以
則地義以象天明其何業不廣直則無我
===
然後得正己之盡也由是而敦仁焉以制
六志以慎百行以宥密于至善以緝熈于
光明其何德不崇故曰天德王道之本也
是學也先千百世而作者唐虞三代其至
乎後千百世而作者我
祖宗
皇上其盛乎執事以此策士蓋欲明
聖化之有本矣敬條陳之夫乾靜專動直是以
大生焉夫坤靜翕動闢是以廣生焉聖人
punctuated:
聖天子邃於心學之妙，頗能言其槩，末復重一敬字，其亦涵濡而有得者歟？
考試官教諭張批：言有忠愛。
考試官教授錢批：典則。
人君動靜合一之學，天德王道之本也。蓋靜所以效天下之至動者也，不虛則無以利用；動所以涵天下之至靜者也，不直則無以立本。故虛則存神，然後妙應物之感也。由是而畜義焉，以幸群生，以命百物，以則地義，以象天明，其何業不廣？直則無我，然後得正己之盡也。由是而敦仁焉，以制六志，以慎百行，以宥密于至善，以緝熈于光明，其何德不崇？故曰天德王道之本也。
是學也，先千百世而作者，唐虞三代其至乎？後千百世而作者，我祖宗皇上其盛乎？執事以此策士，蓋欲明聖化之有本矣。敬條陳之。夫乾靜專動直，是以大生焉；夫坤靜翕動闢，是以廣生焉。聖人
translation_en:
…the wondrous subtleties of our sagely Son of Heaven’s profound learning of the mind, this essay is quite able to convey their general purport. At its close, it again places emphasis on the single word “reverence.” Surely its author, too, has steeped himself in this learning and gained something from it?
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “His words express loyalty and love for the sovereign.”
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “Classical and exemplary.”
The ruler’s learning that unifies activity and stillness is the foundation of heavenly virtue and the kingly Way. Stillness is what gives effect to the utmost activity under Heaven; without inner emptiness, there is no means of making its operation beneficial. Activity is what nurtures the utmost stillness under Heaven; without uprightness, there is no means of establishing the foundation. Thus, through emptiness one preserves spiritual efficacy, and only then responds wondrously to the impulses of things. From this one accumulates righteousness, bringing blessings to all living beings, ordering the myriad things, taking Earth’s right order as a rule and Heaven’s brightness as a model. What undertaking, then, would fail to expand? Through uprightness one becomes free of self, and only then achieves complete rectification of oneself. From this one deepens benevolence, regulating the six dispositions, exercising care in every act, abiding in profound serenity within the highest good, and continually advancing in brightness. What virtue, then, would fail to be exalted? Hence it is called the foundation of heavenly virtue and the kingly Way.
As for this learning, among those who put it into practice hundreds and thousands of generations ago, did it not reach its utmost under Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties? Among those who put it into practice hundreds and thousands of generations later, does it not flourish under our imperial ancestors and our reigning Emperor? In examining candidates with this policy question, you gentlemen surely wish to make clear that the sage ruler’s transforming influence has a foundation. I respectfully set out my account point by point. Qian, the Creative, is concentrated in stillness and straight in activity; thus it brings forth life in its greatness. Kun, the Receptive, closes in stillness and opens in activity; thus it brings forth life in its breadth. The sage…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
合一之學其求端於此乎故堯曰執中舜
曰精一禹曰安止幾康湯曰以義制事以
禮制心文王曰不顯亦臨不聞亦式帝王
授受一道也皆合動靜而一之者也夫是
以日新之德配天富有之業配地令聞嘉
績垂于無窮自漢而下此學不講雜博相
高者而以涉獵記誦華靡相勝者而以割
裂裝綴願治之辟雖世相起也要皆隨世
以就功名而終不得以與乎帝王之盛其
===
或耻為卑近而思奮以師則又不免蔽於
老子浮屠之說靜則徒以虛無寂滅之樂
而不知有所謂實理之原動則徒以應緣
無礙為達而不知有所謂善惡之幾漢以
宣帝唐以太宗非不石渠詔講弘文引士
而僅以刑名慚德終焉其所學者可知矣
宋太宗建清心殿以儲經籍元文宗立奎
章閣置學士員非不好且盛矣而一則金
匱之盟不踐一則以再傳之胤不得蒙業
punctuated:
合一之學，其求端於此乎？故堯曰執中，舜曰精一，禹曰安止幾康，湯曰以義制事、以禮制心，文王曰不顯亦臨、不聞亦式。帝王授受，一道也，皆合動靜而一之者也。夫是以日新之德配天，富有之業配地，令聞嘉績垂于無窮。
自漢而下，此學不講。雜博相高者，而以涉獵記誦；華靡相勝者，而以割裂裝綴。願治之辟，雖世相起也，要皆隨世以就功名，而終不得以與乎帝王之盛。其或耻為卑近而思奮以師，則又不免蔽於老子浮屠之說。靜則徒以虛無寂滅之樂，而不知有所謂實理之原；動則徒以應緣無礙為達，而不知有所謂善惡之幾。
漢以宣帝，唐以太宗，非不石渠詔講、弘文引士，而僅以刑名慚德終焉，其所學者可知矣。宋太宗建清心殿以儲經籍，元文宗立奎章閣、置學士員，非不好且盛矣，而一則金匱之盟不踐，一則以再傳之胤不得蒙業
translation_en:
…Does the learning that unites them into one seek its beginnings here? Thus Yao spoke of holding to the mean; Shun, of refinement and singleness; Yu, of resting in one’s proper place, attending to incipient developments, and securing well-being [?]; Tang, of regulating affairs through righteousness and regulating the mind through ritual propriety; and King Wen, of being watchful even where nothing is manifest and maintaining due form even where nothing is heard. What emperors and kings transmitted and received was a single Way: all united activity and stillness into one. Thus their daily renewed virtue matched Heaven, and their richly abundant achievements matched Earth; their good repute and admirable accomplishments endured without end.
From the Han onward, this learning went unexamined. Those who sought to surpass one another in miscellaneous erudition did so through cursory reading and memorization; those who competed in ornate elegance did so by cutting passages apart and stitching them together. Although rulers who desired good government arose in successive ages, they all ultimately followed the tendencies of their times in pursuit of achievement and fame, and never attained the grandeur of the ancient emperors and kings. Some, ashamed of what was low and commonplace, sought to rouse themselves to emulate exemplary models [?], yet could not escape being blinded by the teachings of Laozi and the Buddha. In stillness, they sought only the pleasures of emptiness and quiescent extinction, unaware of what is called the source of substantial principle; in activity, they regarded responding to conditions without obstruction as full understanding, unaware of what are called the incipient stirrings of good and evil.
Emperor Xuan of the Han and Emperor Taizong of the Tang did indeed command scholarly discussions at Shiqu and draw scholars to Hongwen, respectively. Yet they ended with mere techniques of punishment and administrative control, and with shortcomings in virtue: from this one can discern what they had learned. Emperor Taizong of the Song built Qingxin Hall to store the classics and other writings; Emperor Wenzong of the Yuan established Kuizhang Pavilion and appointed academicians. Their fondness for learning and the magnificence of their undertakings were undeniable. Yet the former failed to fulfill the covenant kept in the Golden Coffer, while in the latter’s case, a descendant two successions later could not inherit the dynastic enterprise…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而安又何聖學之敢幾也夫所謂聖學者
以實也不以文也彼徒取夫帝王之所謂
文者行之以爲是足以經緯天下矣而其
實不與及其未足以華天下也又從而附
益之竊取其近似者以爲口實如假易之
變通以妄意紛更假書之柴望以甘心封
禪慕鳳凰來儀之說援刑兹無赦之文者
類相望也而當時諸臣復相與彌縫其闕
而緣飾之故唐虞三代之學遂亡而治亦
邈乎遠也洪惟我
===
太祖高皇帝聰明天授獨起而紹述之使帝王
心學之全復見于天下如觀心亭記有曰
返視却聽上契冲漠其堯之執中乎擬問
心有曰運之至精守之永久其舜之精一
乎道衡說有曰心常履道而不迂性常如
衡而不曲其禹之安止幾康乎題暮雪雙
禽圖而有曰玩物喪志其湯之以義制事
文之不聞亦式乎若我
punctuated:
而安，又何聖學之敢幾也？夫所謂聖學者，以實也，不以文也。彼徒取夫帝王之所謂文者行之，以爲是足以經緯天下矣，而其實不與。及其未足以華天下也，又從而附益之，竊取其近似者以爲口實。如假《易》之變通以妄意紛更，假《書》之柴望以甘心封禪，慕鳳凰來儀之說，援刑兹無赦之文者，類相望也。而當時諸臣復相與彌縫其闕而緣飾之，故唐虞三代之學遂亡，而治亦邈乎遠也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，聰明天授，獨起而紹述之，使帝王心學之全復見于天下。如《觀心亭記》有曰：「返視却聽，上契冲漠。」其堯之執中乎？《擬問心》有曰：「運之至精，守之永久。」其舜之精一乎？《道衡說》有曰：「心常履道而不迂，性常如衡而不曲。」其禹之安止幾康乎？題《暮雪雙禽圖》而有曰：「玩物喪志。」其湯之以義制事、文之不聞亦式乎？若我
translation_en:
…and be at ease—how, then, could he dare aspire to the learning of the sages? What is called the learning of the sages depends on substance, not outward form. Those rulers merely adopted and practised what passed for the outward forms of the ancient emperors and kings, believing these sufficient to order the world, while their substance was absent. When these proved insufficient to bring cultural splendour to the world, they added further embellishments, appropriating superficially similar precedents to justify themselves. Examples followed one another: invoking the adaptability taught in the Book of Changes to pursue arbitrary and incessant alterations; invoking the fire sacrifices and sacrifices to distant mountains and rivers in the Book of Documents to indulge their desire to perform the feng and shan sacrifices; admiring the account of phoenixes coming to dance in ordered array; and citing the passage, “Punish them without pardon.” The ministers of those times then joined together to patch over their shortcomings and adorn them. Thus the learning of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties disappeared, and good government likewise grew remote.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with intelligence, arose alone to carry on and renew this learning, allowing the full learning of the mind practised by the ancient emperors and kings to appear again in the world. For example, his Record of the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind says: “Turn sight inward and withdraw hearing; attain accord above with the undifferentiated stillness.” Is this not Yao’s holding fast to the Mean? His Draft Inquiry into the Mind says: “Exercise it with utmost refinement; preserve it forever.” Is this not Shun’s refinement and single-mindedness? His Discourse on the Way and the Balance says: “Let the mind always tread the Way without deviation, and let one’s nature always be like a balance, without crookedness.” Is this not Yu’s resting in his proper place and attending to the incipient signs of things and to peace [?]? In his inscription on Picture of Two Birds in Evening Snow, he says: “Taking pleasure in objects destroys one’s resolve.” Is this not Tang’s regulating affairs through righteousness, and King Wen’s following the rule even in things unheard of? As for our …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太宗文皇帝覽講義而有心如明鏡止水之喻
即觀心諸篇之旨也因製筆而有令人自
怠大儒積勤之規置金獅而有小事必謹
小過必改之戒即道衡諸篇之旨也嗚呼
此我
祖宗合一之學眞有以發帝王之精蘊矣
孫謀燕翼不有待於
今日之盛乎肆我
聖天子祗遹憲章厥有成𤔡其見於
===
製作如奉揚
先烈有
祖德詩勸重農桑有
穀祗贊壇賦親禮宰輔有
平臺召見集固皆有本之學旁作逢源然
奎閣未頒不可槩見所可見者惟
敬一箴惟
五箴註則巳昭揭宇內敷賁人心有年矣故
嘗陟山忘大飲海忘深而仰窺
punctuated: 太宗文皇帝覽講義而有心如明鏡止水之喻，即觀心諸篇之旨也。因製筆而有令人自怠、大儒積勤之規，置金獅而有小事必謹、小過必改之戒，即道衡諸篇之旨也。嗚呼！此我祖宗合一之學，眞有以發帝王之精蘊矣。孫謀燕翼，不有待於今日之盛乎？肆我聖天子祗遹憲章，厥有成𤔡。其見於製作，如奉揚先烈，有《祖德詩》；勸重農桑，有《穀祗贊壇賦》；親禮宰輔，有《平臺召見集》。固皆有本之學，旁作逢源。然奎閣未頒，不可槩見。所可見者，惟《敬一箴》，惟《五箴註》，則巳昭揭宇內，敷賁人心有年矣。故嘗陟山忘大，飲海忘深，而仰窺
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizong Wen, on reading the lecture expositions, offered the comparison of the mind to a bright mirror and still water: this was precisely the purport of the various writings on contemplating the mind. On the occasion of making writing brushes, he offered an admonition concerning causing people to grow indolent and great Confucian scholars’ accumulated diligence [?]; on having a golden lion set in place, he warned that one must be careful even in small matters and correct even minor faults. This was precisely the purport of the various writings on the Way and the balance. Ah! This unified learning of our imperial ancestors truly brought to light the profound essentials of sage kingship. Did not their plans for their descendants and provision for their successors await the flourishing of this very day?

Thus our sagely Son of Heaven reverently follows and takes as his model the ancestral regulations, bringing his undertakings to fruition. As manifested in his writings, his reverent celebration of his forebears’ achievements produced the Poems on Ancestral Virtue; his encouragement of agriculture and sericulture produced the Rhapsody on the Altar in Praise of the Grain Spirit [?]; and his gracious treatment of his chief ministers produced the Collection of Audiences at the Platform. These are assuredly all expressions of learning firmly rooted in its source, finding that source wherever it turns. Yet these writings have not been issued from the imperial literary repository, so they cannot be surveyed in their entirety. What can be seen are the Admonition on Reverence and Unity and the Commentary on the Five Admonitions, which have already been prominently displayed throughout the realm and have illuminated people’s hearts for years. Thus I have ventured, like one who ascends a mountain forgetting its vastness, or drinks from the sea forgetting its depth, to gaze reverently upon…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖學一二於宏綱大旨已乎以敬一之義言之
夫敬所以存其心而不忽也夫一所以純
乎理而無雜也而又以嚴
郊廟以慎閒居以孚言行以貫終始是皆素豫
乎内求利乎外者也所謂靜一動也以五
箴之義言之夫心所以統視聽言動者也
懼其為物慾所攻取也於是乎以觀邪正
以辨忠讒以謹號令以戒妄動是皆素豫
乎外致養乎内者也所謂動一靜也内外
===
交養動靜合一此
聖學之所以增光
先德駕軼百王者也請推廣而終陳之人君之
學莫非敬也而敬天為精故曰敬天之怒
無敢戲豫敬天之渝無敢馳驅而所謂欽
翼祗栗以祀天也溫恭敬遜以承親也正
恭嚴恪以臨眾也宣明端誠以享下也皆
其推者矣莫非一也而一德為要故曰德
無常師主善為師善無常主協于克一而
punctuated:
聖學一二於宏綱大旨已乎。以敬一之義言之，夫敬所以存其心而不忽也，夫一所以純乎理而無雜也。而又以嚴郊廟，以慎閒居，以孚言行，以貫終始，是皆素豫乎内、求利乎外者也，所謂靜一動也。以五箴之義言之，夫心所以統視聽言動者也，懼其為物慾所攻取也，於是乎以觀邪正，以辨忠讒，以謹號令，以戒妄動，是皆素豫乎外、致養乎内者也，所謂動一靜也。内外交養，動靜合一，此聖學之所以增光先德、駕軼百王者也。
請推廣而終陳之。人君之學莫非敬也，而敬天為精。故曰：「敬天之怒，無敢戲豫；敬天之渝，無敢馳驅。」而所謂欽翼祗栗以祀天也，溫恭敬遜以承親也，正恭嚴恪以臨眾也，宣明端誠以享下也，皆其推者矣。莫非一也，而一德為要。故曰：「德無常師，主善為師；善無常主，協于克一。」而
translation_en:
…one or two aspects of Your Majesty’s sagely learning, confined to its broad outlines and principal meaning.
As for the meaning of Reverence and Unity, reverence preserves the mind and prevents negligence; unity makes one pure in moral principle, without admixture. Moreover, it brings solemnity to sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, circumspection to private life, trustworthiness to words and actions, and consistency from beginning to end. These all involve making preparations within and seeking beneficial effects without [?]: this is what is meant by stillness unifying activity. As for the meaning of the Five Admonitions, the mind governs seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting. Fearing that material desires might assail and capture it, one therefore uses these faculties to discern the deviant and the upright, distinguish loyalty from slander, exercise care in issuing commands, and guard against rash action. These all involve making preparations without and nourishing what is within: this is what is meant by activity unifying stillness. The inner and outer nourish one another, and activity and stillness become one. This is how Your Majesty’s sagely learning adds lustre to the virtue of your forebears and surpasses the hundred kings.
Allow me to extend this discussion and bring my exposition to a close. The learning of a ruler is entirely concerned with reverence, and reverence for Heaven is its essence. Thus it is said: “Revere Heaven’s anger; dare not indulge in play and pleasure. Revere Heaven’s changing disposition; dare not gallop about.” What is called serving Heaven in sacrifice with reverence, vigilance, respect, and trembling; attending upon one’s parents with warmth, deference, reverence, and humility; presiding over the multitude with uprightness, deference, solemnity, and circumspection; and bestowing bounty upon those below with clarity, rectitude, and sincerity—all these are extensions of that reverence. The ruler’s learning is entirely concerned with unity, and unity of virtue is its essential point. Thus it is said: “Virtue has no constant teacher; take goodness as your teacher. Goodness has no constant master; accord with the capacity to remain unified.” And …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所謂祓邪除穢以致精也考中度衷以致
忠也昭明物則以致禮也制義庶孚以致
信也皆其推者矣莫非視也而知人為大
故曰知人則哲能官人以至于辨是非明
好惡察言行試政事量材能課功狀詰奸
邪禁暴亂辨貴賤立紀綱考制度慎鬼神
而皆其所自推也莫非聽也而容忍為先
故曰必有忍其乃有濟有容德乃大以至
于匿瑕疾務包涵辨妖祥考謗譽察甘言
===
省卑辭進狂戇杜讒佞詢芻蕘採葑菲問
遺訓咨故實而皆其所自推也莫非言也
而慎令為重故曰慎乃出令令出惟行弗
惟反以至于審繁簡察弛張協謀議廣覽
擇盡人情通物理善因革公廢置蠲猛暴
除苛急正沿襲聳觀聽而皆其所自推也
莫非動也而戒欲為急故曰罔咈百姓以
從己之欲以至于謹好尚慎威儀簡綴衣
命受環詔彤管錫鸞鈴置巫史奉卜筮戒
punctuated: 所謂祓邪除穢以致精也，考中度衷以致忠也，昭明物則以致禮也，制義庶孚以致信也，皆其推者矣。莫非視也，而知人為大，故曰：「知人則哲，能官人。」以至于辨是非，明好惡，察言行，試政事，量材能，課功狀，詰奸邪，禁暴亂，辨貴賤，立紀綱，考制度，慎鬼神，而皆其所自推也。莫非聽也，而容忍為先，故曰：「必有忍，其乃有濟；有容，德乃大。」以至于匿瑕，疾務，包涵，辨妖祥，考謗譽，察甘言，省卑辭，進狂戇，杜讒佞，詢芻蕘，採葑菲，問遺訓，咨故實，而皆其所自推也。莫非言也，而慎令為重，故曰：「慎乃出令，令出惟行，弗惟反。」以至于審繁簡，察弛張，協謀議，廣覽擇，盡人情，通物理，善因革，公廢置，蠲猛暴，除苛急，正沿襲，聳觀聽，而皆其所自推也。莫非動也，而戒欲為急，故曰：「罔咈百姓，以從己之欲。」以至于謹好尚，慎威儀，簡綴衣，命受環，詔彤管，錫鸞鈴，置巫史，奉卜筮，戒
translation_en:
…what is called purging evil and removing defilement to attain purity, examining the mean and measuring inner rectitude to attain wholeheartedness, clearly illuminating the principles governing things to attain ritual propriety, and establishing what is right so that all may trust it to attain trustworthiness: these are all extensions of it.

All matters involve seeing, but discerning people is paramount. Thus it is said: “To discern people is to be wise; one can then appoint people to office.” This extends to distinguishing right from wrong, making clear what should be liked and disliked, examining words and conduct, testing people in government affairs, assessing talents and abilities, evaluating achievements, investigating the treacherous and wicked, prohibiting violence and disorder, distinguishing the noble from the lowly, establishing guiding principles and discipline, examining institutions and regulations, and exercising care in matters concerning spirits. All these are extensions of that discernment.

All matters involve listening, but tolerance and forbearance come first. Thus it is said: “There must be forbearance; only then can there be accomplishment. With tolerance, virtue becomes great.” This extends to overlooking faults, attending diligently to duties, being accommodating, distinguishing ominous from auspicious signs, examining blame and praise, scrutinizing honeyed words, considering humble expressions, advancing the impetuous and blunt, shutting out slanderers and flatterers, consulting grass-cutters and wood-gatherers, gathering turnips and radishes—that is, accepting useful counsel even from humble sources—inquiring into teachings handed down, and consulting historical precedents. All these are extensions of that tolerance and forbearance.

All matters involve speech, but caution in issuing commands is most important. Thus it is said: “Be cautious in issuing your commands. Once a command is issued, it is to be carried out, not reversed.” This extends to weighing complexity against simplicity, considering relaxation and tightening, coordinating deliberations, surveying widely before choosing, fully understanding human feelings, comprehending the principles of things, handling continuity and reform well, being impartial in abolishing and establishing, eliminating brutality, removing harshness and urgency, correcting inherited practices, and stirring those who see and hear. All these are extensions of that caution.

All matters involve action, but guarding against desire is most urgent. Thus it is said: “Do not go against the common people in order to follow your own desires.” This extends to exercising care in tastes and preferences, being circumspect in dignified bearing, selecting wardrobe attendants, appointing those who receive rings [?], instructing the keepers of the vermilion writing brushes [?], bestowing carriage bells, appointing spirit mediums and scribes, respecting divination by tortoise shell and milfoil, and guarding against…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遊田斥方技恤工作重征伐而皆其所自
推也夫敬一以弘其體視聽言動以懋其
用精焉而不窒其端純焉而不匱其量則
一人之心眞有以建天地中和之極而曰
盛德配高明大業配博厚固其理也幸以
是爲芹曝
獻焉
第二問
梁以斅
===
同考試官教諭紀批周禮壞於後世之私智今于以
脩齊之道求禮聲氣之元求樂誠知旨者也古制之興有日矣
考試官教諭張批識得制作之本
考試官教授錢批精覈
至哉周禮一書之妙也窺其粗而制作之
陋矣竊其似而施行之亂矣酌其權而發
明之幾矣夫禮樂有節有音有度有數故
語粗不可不究其精也語似不可不探其
眞也語權不可不考其經也然其節可定
punctuated:
遊田，斥方技，恤工作，重征伐，而皆其所自推也。夫敬一以弘其體，視聽言動以懋其用，精焉而不窒其端，純焉而不匱其量，則一人之心眞有以建天地中和之極，而曰盛德配高明，大業配博厚，固其理也。幸以是爲芹曝獻焉。
第二問
梁以斅
同考試官教諭紀批：周禮壞於後世之私智，今于以脩齊之道求禮，聲氣之元求樂，誠知旨者也。古制之興有日矣。
考試官教諭張批：識得制作之本。
考試官教授錢批：精覈。
至哉！周禮一書之妙也。窺其粗而制作之陋矣，竊其似而施行之亂矣，酌其權而發明之幾矣。夫禮樂有節、有音、有度、有數，故語粗不可不究其精也，語似不可不探其眞也，語權不可不考其經也。然其節可定
translation_en:
…excursions and hunting; dismiss practitioners of specialized arts; show concern for construction work; and treat military campaigns with gravity—all these, too, are extensions of his own understanding. By reverently holding to unity, he enlarges the underlying substance; through seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting, he vigorously develops its operation. Refined without obstructing its sources, pure without exhausting its capacity, the sovereign’s mind can truly establish the supreme standard of centrality and harmony in Heaven and Earth. Thus it is entirely fitting to say that his abundant virtue matches their height and brightness, and his great achievements their breadth and depth. I venture to present this as a humble offering of celery and sunshine.
Second Policy Question
Liang Yixiao 梁以斅
Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: “The Rites of Zhou were corrupted by the private cleverness of later generations. Here, however, ritual is sought in the Way of cultivating oneself and regulating one’s family, and music in the primal source of sound and vital energy. This is truly someone who understands their essential meaning. The revival of the ancient institutions will have its day.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “He understands the foundation of establishing institutions.”
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: “Precise and well examined.”
How consummate are the subtleties of the Rites of Zhou! To glimpse its coarse outlines and establish institutions accordingly is to make them crude; to appropriate its outward semblance and put it into practice is to produce disorder; to draw upon its expedients and expound it accordingly is precarious [?]. Ritual and music possess articulations, tones, measures, and numbers. Thus, when discussing their coarse outlines, one must investigate their subtleties; when discussing their semblance, one must explore their truth; and when discussing their expedients, one must examine their constant principles. Yet their articulations can be fixed…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也其體難圖也其音可調也其變難曉也
其度可推也其義難準也其數可籌也其
始難察也故反而求之者考於異詳以辨
之者繹於同推而行之者恊於一會而通
之者貫於萬外是而用周禮是謂斧其根
柢采其英華塞其江河汲其溝洫舍其冠
冕服其旒綴者也而豈足以窺大聖人精
神心術之蘊哉知乎此可以答執事禮樂
之問矣夫周禮制於周公而非周公作俑
===
也夫自君臣父子六親九族各有上下親
疎之别養生送死弔恤慶賀又有進止威
儀之數唐虞以上分之爲三在周始分爲
五即宗伯所掌而太史以恊事之類是也
樂之制則自黃帝以來已有雲門大卷咸
濩韶武之樂而或施之社稷山川之屬至
周始備六代之樂即大胥以六樂之會正
舞位是也是故周禮之爲書規模宏大節
目詳悉有非大聖人不能作而何休以爲
punctuated:
也，其體難圖也；其音可調也，其變難曉也；其度可推也，其義難準也；其數可籌也，其始難察也。故反而求之者考於異，詳以辨之者繹於同，推而行之者恊於一，會而通之者貫於萬。外是而用周禮，是謂斧其根柢，采其英華；塞其江河，汲其溝洫；舍其冠冕，服其旒綴者也。而豈足以窺大聖人精神心術之蘊哉？知乎此，可以答執事禮樂之問矣。
夫周禮制於周公，而非周公作俑也。夫自君臣父子、六親九族，各有上下親疎之别；養生送死、弔恤慶賀，又有進止威儀之數。唐虞以上分之爲三，在周始分爲五，即宗伯所掌，而太史以恊事之類是也。樂之制，則自黃帝以來，已有雲門、大卷、咸、濩、韶、武之樂，而或施之社稷山川之屬。至周始備六代之樂，即大胥以六樂之會正舞位是也。是故周禮之爲書，規模宏大，節目詳悉，有非大聖人不能作，而何休以爲
translation_en:
…can be fixed, yet their underlying form is difficult to delineate; their tones can be harmonized, yet their transformations are difficult to comprehend; their measures can be worked out, yet their meaning is difficult to gauge; their numbers can be calculated, yet their origins are difficult to discern. Thus, those who turn back to seek their foundations examine their differences; those who distinguish them through detailed inquiry unravel their common features; those who extend them into practice bring them into accord with a single principle; and those who bring them together into comprehensive understanding link them through the myriad things. To employ the Rites of Zhou apart from this is to axe its roots while gathering its blossoms, to dam its rivers while drawing water from its ditches, and to discard its ceremonial caps while wearing their pendant ornaments. How could this suffice to glimpse the depths of the great sage’s spirit and workings of mind? Understanding this, one can answer your question concerning rites and music.
Now, the rites of Zhou were established by the Duke of Zhou, but he was not their first originator. Between ruler and minister, father and son, and among the six categories of kin and the nine degrees of lineage, there were distinctions of superior and inferior, close and distant. In nourishing the living and burying the dead, offering condolences and relief, and celebrating and congratulating, there were also prescribed forms for movement and deportment. In the times of Tang and Yu and earlier, rites were divided into three categories; only under the Zhou were they divided into five. These were the sorts of matters administered by the Minister of Rites and coordinated by the Grand Scribe. As for the system of music, from the time of the Yellow Emperor onward there were already the musical works Yunmen, Dajuan, Xian, Huo, Shao, and Wu [the transmitted list appears abbreviated or garbled here: ?], some of which were performed in sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain, mountains, rivers, and the like. Only under the Zhou was the music of the six dynasties fully assembled. This is what is meant by the Senior Music Instructor’s regulating the dancers’ positions at the assembly for the six musical traditions. Thus the Rites of Zhou is a book vast in scope and comprehensive in its detailed provisions, such that none but a great sage could have composed it. Yet He Xiu considered it to be…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
瀆亂不經是以鷦鷯嘲鯤鵬廢井笑海若
也亦可謂不知忌憚矣今所傳儀禮十七
篇亦周公雜著三代之禮以為本經而戴
記四十九篇漢儒纂集之以為義疏如婚
義當附婚禮冠義當附冠禮此晦菴之說
甚明可考也後世通經學古之士論禮樂
者莫不知周禮之為尊若班固謂六經之
道同歸而禮樂之用為急歐陽子謂三代
治出於一而禮樂達於天下後世治出於
===
二而禮樂為虛名謂非皆得禮樂之旨哉
然謂急於六經出於一者蓋孔子刪詩定
書贊易脩春秋而不及禮樂之制以為不
可斯須去身而莫急焉者其要本之一誠
而已矣至董仲舒劉向歸之庠序是或一
道也而豈知天子躬行以為之倡而出於
一哉及考司馬遷之律書其始不言律而
言兵之偃及謂漢文帝偃兵息民而天地
之氣始正此制作之本也永嘉陳氏謂律
punctuated: 瀆亂不經，是以鷦鷯嘲鯤鵬、廢井笑海若也，亦可謂不知忌憚矣。今所傳《儀禮》十七篇，亦周公雜著三代之禮以為本經，而《戴記》四十九篇，漢儒纂集之以為義疏。如《婚義》當附《婚禮》，《冠義》當附《冠禮》，此晦菴之說甚明可考也。後世通經學古之士論禮樂者，莫不知《周禮》之為尊。若班固謂六經之道同歸，而禮樂之用為急；歐陽子謂三代治出於一，而禮樂達於天下，後世治出於二，而禮樂為虛名，謂非皆得禮樂之旨哉？然謂急於六經、出於一者，蓋孔子刪《詩》、定《書》、贊《易》、脩《春秋》，而不及禮樂之制，以為不可斯須去身，而莫急焉者，其要本之一誠而已矣。至董仲舒、劉向歸之庠序，是或一道也，而豈知天子躬行以為之倡，而出於一哉？及考司馬遷之《律書》，其始不言律而言兵之偃，及謂漢文帝偃兵息民，而天地之氣始正，此制作之本也。永嘉陳氏謂律
translation_en:
…“disorderly and contrary to the canonical norms”—this is like a wren mocking the Kun and Peng, or an abandoned well laughing at the sea god. Such a judgment may indeed be called utterly unrestrained.

The seventeen chapters of the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) transmitted today likewise comprise the Duke of Zhou’s compilation of rites from the Three Dynasties, forming the foundational classic. The forty-nine chapters of Dai’s Record (Dai ji) were compiled by Han scholars as an explanatory commentary. Thus “The Meaning of the Marriage Ceremony” should be appended to “The Marriage Ceremony,” and “The Meaning of the Capping Ceremony” to “The Capping Ceremony.” Hui’an’s explanation of this is very clear and can be consulted.

Among later scholars versed in the classics and the study of antiquity who discussed rites and music, none failed to recognize the preeminence of the Rites of Zhou (Zhou li). Ban Gu, for example, said that the ways of the Six Classics converge upon the same end, but that the application of rites and music is most urgent. Master Ouyang said that under the Three Dynasties, government proceeded from a single source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm; in later ages, government proceeded from two sources, and rites and music became empty names. Can one say that these statements did not all grasp the essential meaning of rites and music?

Yet as for calling them the most urgent among the Six Classics and saying that government proceeded from a single source: Confucius edited the Odes, established the Documents, elucidated the Changes, and revised the Spring and Autumn Annals, but did not address the institutions of rites and music. He considered that these could not be separated from one’s person even for an instant, and that nothing was more urgent. Their essentials are rooted simply in undivided sincerity. As for Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang locating them in the schools, this may be one approach; but how could they understand that the Son of Heaven personally practices them to set the example, so that government proceeds from a single source?

When we examine Sima Qian’s “Treatise on the Pitch Pipes,” its opening discusses not pitch standards but the laying down of arms. It goes on to say that only when Emperor Wen of Han laid down arms and gave the people rest did the vital energies of Heaven and Earth become properly ordered. This is the foundation for establishing institutions. Master Chen of Yongjia said that the pitch standards…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
呂之法起於黃帝而律呂之說定於太史
公是也此其說與治出於一之言何異哉
以後世之禮樂者言之西漢之禮制於叔
通而雜秦儀此兩生之所以不至也東漢
之禮制於曹褒而取讖諱在當時張酺已
有破亂聖術之奏矣唐有顯慶禮則許敬
宗所附會而削國恤一篇以致後來山陵
之論無定見敬宗之罪大矣開元禮則徐
堅輩所撰而蕭嵩輩足成之大率不脫顯
===
慶之舊也宋有開寶禮制於劉溫叟而盧
多遜爲之撰義纂政和禮則制於鄭居中
輩而湖北漕者爲之撮要似若備矣然一
時姦邪多以私智損益反不如開元禮之
爲愈也是則謂漢唐宋之禮可也而較之
周禮吾不知孰純孰駁也哉若以樂言之
漢以制氏世職大樂不過識鏗鏘之末節
而已武帝以李延年協律作十九章之歌
尤爲可鄙此班氏謂鄭聲施於朝廷也至
punctuated: 呂之法起於黃帝，而律呂之說定於太史公，是也。此其說與治出於一之言何異哉？以後世之禮樂者言之，西漢之禮制於叔通而雜秦儀，此兩生之所以不至也。東漢之禮制於曹褒而取讖諱，在當時張酺已有破亂聖術之奏矣。唐有《顯慶禮》，則許敬宗所附會，而削國恤一篇，以致後來山陵之論無定見，敬宗之罪大矣。《開元禮》則徐堅輩所撰，而蕭嵩輩足成之，大率不脫顯慶之舊也。宋有《開寶禮》，制於劉溫叟，而盧多遜爲之撰《義纂》；《政和禮》則制於鄭居中輩，而湖北漕者爲之撮要，似若備矣。然一時姦邪多以私智損益，反不如《開元禮》之爲愈也。是則謂漢唐宋之禮可也，而較之周禮，吾不知孰純孰駁也哉？若以樂言之，漢以制氏世職大樂，不過識鏗鏘之末節而已。武帝以李延年協律，作十九章之歌，尤爲可鄙，此班氏謂鄭聲施於朝廷也。至
translation_en:
…the system of pitch standards originated with the Yellow Emperor, while their theoretical explanation was established by the Grand Astrologer, Sima Qian: this is correct. How does this account differ from the statement that government proceeds from a single source?

To speak of the rites and music of later ages: the Western Han rites were established by Shutong [Shusun Tong], but incorporated Qin ceremonial practices. This was why the two scholars refused to come. The Eastern Han rites were established by Cao Bao, but drew upon prophetic and apocryphal writings [?]. Already at the time, Zhang Pu submitted a memorial charging that they disrupted and confused the methods of the sages. Under the Tang there were the Xianqing Rites, into which Xu Jingzong introduced strained accommodations. He deleted the section on mourning for the sovereign, leaving later discussions of imperial funerals without any settled position. Jingzong’s culpability was great indeed! The Kaiyuan Rites were compiled by Xu Jian and his colleagues and completed by Xiao Song and his colleagues; in the main, they did not depart from the earlier Xianqing rites. Under the Song there were the Kaibao Rites, established by Liu Wensou, for which Lu Duoxun compiled a Compendium of Explanations. The Zhenghe Rites were established by Zheng Juzhong and his colleagues, and the Transport Commissioner of Hubei prepared an abridgment of them. They thus appeared comprehensive. Yet the wicked and treacherous men of the time repeatedly made additions and deletions according to their own conceits, leaving them inferior even to the Kaiyuan Rites. It is acceptable to call these the rites of the Han, Tang, and Song; but when comparing them with the rites of Zhou, could I fail to know which are pure and which are mixed?

As for music, under the Han the Zhi family held hereditary responsibility for court music, yet knew no more than the minor details of its ringing and clanging. Emperor Wu employed Li Yannian to harmonize the pitch standards and compose songs in nineteen sections—a particularly contemptible undertaking. This is what Ban Gu meant when he said that the sounds of Zheng were used at court. As for…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於京房以仲呂再生別名執始是徒知焦
氏卦氣之去四而爲六十而遂以三分損
益之數或棄或增其誤亦甚矣在唐則祖
孝孫製十二和自豫和以至承和是也顏
師古製七舞則長發以至光大是也然皆
襲梁武帝之舊而已在宋則和峴諸人之
辯皆無定論和峴用影表尺李照造新器
阮逸與范鎮皆以徑三分累黍胡安定遷
林鍾以下以就黃鍾而司馬君實於筆談
===
通典皆不之考究比之范公又不及矣然
則數子所定之樂謂之漢唐宋之樂可也
其視周禮之樂孰高孰下哉至於王荆公
崇信周禮而卒以取敗人曰用周禮之效
也不知荆公之立青苗設條例是變仁義
爲聚斂皆不善用之過也非周禮使之然
也故嘗合而論之後世之不如三代者豈
後世終不可治哉要之以禮樂爲虛名而
治出於二也歐子之論斷乎不可易矣至
punctuated:
於京房，以仲呂再生，別名執始，是徒知焦氏卦氣之去四而爲六十，而遂以三分損益之數或棄或增，其誤亦甚矣。在唐，則祖孝孫製十二和，自豫和以至承和是也；顏師古製七舞，則長發以至光大是也。然皆襲梁武帝之舊而已。在宋，則和峴諸人之辯皆無定論。和峴用影表尺，李照造新器，阮逸與范鎮皆以徑三分累黍，胡安定遷林鍾以下以就黃鍾，而司馬君實於《筆談》《通典》皆不之考究，比之范公又不及矣。然則數子所定之樂，謂之漢唐宋之樂可也，其視《周禮》之樂，孰高孰下哉？
至於王荆公崇信《周禮》而卒以取敗，人曰用《周禮》之效也。不知荆公之立青苗、設條例，是變仁義爲聚斂，皆不善用之過也，非《周禮》使之然也。故嘗合而論之，後世之不如三代者，豈後世終不可治哉？要之，以禮樂爲虛名，而治出於二也。歐子之論，斷乎不可易矣。至
translation_en:
…As for Jing Fang, he generated another pitch from Zhonglü and gave it the separate name Zhishi. He merely knew that Master Jiao’s scheme correlating hexagrams with seasonal qi removed four hexagrams to leave sixty, and consequently discarded or added terms in the numerical sequence for generating pitches by subtracting or adding a third. His error was indeed grave. In the Tang, Zu Xiaosun composed the Twelve Harmonies, from Yuhuo to Chenghe; Yan Shigu composed the Seven Dances, from Changfa to Guangda. Yet all these merely followed precedents established by Emperor Wu of Liang. In the Song, the debates among He Xian and the others reached no settled conclusion. He Xian used a gnomon measuring rule; Li Zhao made new instruments; Ruan Yi and Fan Zhen both used an arrangement of millet grains with a diameter of three fen [?]; Hu Anding shifted the pitches from Linzhong downward to bring them into accord with Huangzhong. Sima Junshi, meanwhile, did not investigate the relevant material in either Brush Talks or the Comprehensive Institutions, and thus fell short even of Master Fan. The music established by these men may therefore properly be called the music of the Han, Tang, and Song. But compared with the music of the Rites of Zhou, which was superior and which inferior?
As for Wang Jinggong, he revered and trusted the Rites of Zhou but ultimately met with failure. People say that this was the result of putting the Rites of Zhou into practice. They do not understand that Jinggong’s establishment of the Green Sprouts loan program and the Regulations Office turned benevolence and righteousness into revenue extraction. These were all faults arising from his failure to apply the text properly; the Rites of Zhou did not make matters turn out this way. Thus, considering these things together, I have often argued: if later ages fell short of the Three Dynasties, does that mean later ages could never be well governed? The essential problem was that rites and music became empty names, while government proceeded on a separate basis. Master Ou’s judgment is decidedly incontrovertible. As for…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於可繼周禮之缺者舍文公之家禮蔡元
定之律呂新書吾誰歸乎夫家禮畧浮文
敦本實其說多叅用司馬氏程子高氏之
說若夫明大宗小宗之法乃其大義而其
本在於謹名分崇愛敬真可謂庶幾古人
脩身齊家之道者矣至於新書所載黃鍾
圍徑之數以長九寸圍九分取淮南小史
之說正其原也變律半聲之例以為黃鍾
至仲呂相生既窮遂變而上生黃鍾之宮
===
餘八寸而缺半通其變也五聲二變之則
角與徵羽與宮相去二律故角徵之間近
徵收一聲而比徵少下羽宮之間近宮收
一聲而少高於宮諧其聲也若聲氣之元
則政善民安而天下之心和然後氣飛灰
而聲中律故於此多截竹以擬黃鍾之聲
而以氣應者用之然後以秬黍之法而叅
較焉非律生於黍也此其為書明白而淵
深縝密而通暢亦可謂善言樂者矣故以
punctuated: 於可繼周禮之缺者，舍文公之《家禮》、蔡元定之《律呂新書》，吾誰歸乎？夫《家禮》畧浮文，敦本實，其說多叅用司馬氏、程子、高氏之說。若夫明大宗小宗之法，乃其大義，而其本在於謹名分、崇愛敬，真可謂庶幾古人脩身齊家之道者矣。至於《新書》所載黃鍾圍徑之數，以長九寸、圍九分，取淮南小史之說，正其原也。變律半聲之例，以為黃鍾至仲呂相生既窮，遂變而上生黃鍾之宮，餘八寸而缺半，通其變也。五聲二變之則，角與徵、羽與宮相去二律，故角徵之間近徵收一聲而比徵少下，羽宮之間近宮收一聲而少高於宮，諧其聲也。若聲氣之元，則政善民安而天下之心和，然後氣飛灰而聲中律。故於此多截竹以擬黃鍾之聲，而以氣應者用之，然後以秬黍之法而叅較焉，非律生於黍也。此其為書，明白而淵深，縝密而通暢，亦可謂善言樂者矣。故以
translation_en:
…As for works that can supplement what is lacking in the Rites of Zhou, to what could I turn other than Master Wengong’s Family Rituals and Cai Yuanding’s New Treatise on Pitch Pipes? Family Rituals dispenses with superficial formalities and strengthens what is fundamental and substantial. Its explanations frequently draw upon those of Sima, Master Cheng, and Gao. Clarifying the rules governing the major and minor descent lines is its central purport; its foundation lies in carefully observing distinctions of status and honoring affection and respect. It may truly be said to approach the ancients’ way of cultivating oneself and ordering one’s family.

As for the measurements of the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe recorded in the New Treatise, it adopts a length of nine cun and a circumference of nine fen, drawing upon the account in Huainan xiaoshi [?] to rectify the foundation. Its rules for altered pitches and half-tones hold that, once the successive generation of pitches from Huangzhong to Zhonglü has been exhausted, a change is made and the Huangzhong gong pitch is generated by the upward procedure, leaving eight cun and falling short by half [?]. This makes the transformations work. Under the rule of five tones and two altered tones, jue and zhi, and yu and gong, each stand two pitch steps apart. Thus, between jue and zhi, an additional tone is included near zhi but slightly lower than it; between yu and gong, an additional tone is included near gong but slightly higher than it [?]. This harmonizes the sounds.

As for the source of sound and vital qi, only when government is good, the people are at peace, and the hearts of all under Heaven are harmonious does qi make the ashes fly and sound accord with the pitch standards. Accordingly, many lengths of bamboo are cut to approximate the sound of Huangzhong, and the one that responds to qi is used. Only afterward is it checked against the method employing black millet grains; the pitch standard does not originate in millet. This book is lucid yet profound, meticulous yet clear and coherent. It too may be said to discuss music well. Therefore, taking…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
二書較之周禮固安勉不同道然可以繼
往開來而功在萬世亦豈可誣耶故吾謂
後世之禮樂叔孫輩陋者也介甫輩亂者
也家禮新書幾者也後之欲用周禮者盍
於家禮新書而參考之哉敢以是爲明問
復
第三問
林時雨
同考試官教諭黃批識見精明敷暢典實子於文學
===
其深有得者乎
考試官教諭張批議論精確
考試官教授錢批辨博
文章也者聖人道德之英華乎古今人品
之槖籥乎英華也者天之紀也地之表也
民之統也槖籥也者分量有所不充地位
有所不造機軸有所不運是故破紀者陷
壞表者邪失統者詖其間亦有屹然自立
而以文華震耀天下乍而見之非不盎然
punctuated:
二書較之《周禮》，固安勉不同道，然可以繼往開來，而功在萬世，亦豈可誣耶？故吾謂後世之禮樂，叔孫輩陋者也，介甫輩亂者也，《家禮》《新書》幾者也。後之欲用《周禮》者，盍於《家禮》《新書》而參考之哉？敢以是爲明問復。
第三問
林時雨
同考試官教諭黃批：識見精明，敷暢典實，子於文學，其深有得者乎！
考試官教諭張批：議論精確。
考試官教授錢批：辨博。
文章也者，聖人道德之英華乎？古今人品之槖籥乎？英華也者，天之紀也，地之表也，民之統也。槖籥也者，分量有所不充，地位有所不造，機軸有所不運。是故破紀者陷，壞表者邪，失統者詖。其間亦有屹然自立，而以文華震耀天下，乍而見之，非不盎然
translation_en:
…when these two books are compared with the Rites of Zhou, their paths admittedly differ as effortless practice differs from strenuous endeavor. Yet they can carry forward the past and open the way for the future, benefiting ten thousand generations: how could this be denied? Thus I say that, in the ritual and music of later ages, Shusun and his kind were crude, while Jiefu and his kind wrought disorder; the Family Rituals and the New Book came close to the ideal. Should those who later wish to put the Rites of Zhou into practice not consult the Family Rituals and the New Book alongside it? I venture to offer this in reply to your discerning question.
Third Question
Lin Shiyu
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Your insight is penetrating and clear; your exposition is fluent, grounded in the classics, and substantial. Surely you have attained a profound understanding of literary learning!”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The argument is precise and sound.”
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “Broad-ranging in argument.”
Is literary writing the flowering of the sages’ moral virtue? Is it the bellows through which the character of people, ancient and modern, finds expression? This flowering is Heaven’s ordering principle, Earth’s guiding standard, and the unifying rule of the people. As for the bellows, there are capacities that are not fully realized, levels that are not attained, and mechanisms that do not operate. Thus those who break the ordering principle fall into error; those who destroy the guiding standard become deviant; those who lose the unifying rule become biased. Among them are also those who stand firmly on their own and dazzle the world with literary brilliance. At first sight, they are indeed richly…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可愛也然有不充則缺矣有不造則偏矣
有不運則滯矣是故自聖人以下邪正不
同路純駁不同色大小不同器清濁不同
流而文章亦與之俱嗚呼文章固學者之
末事也而於此可以觀心志焉可以考節
操焉可以驗智識焉可以占才能焉文其
可易言耶請因明問所及而陳之夫文章
唯孔子之六經至矣而何所昉乎煥於被
四表之堯而非堯也盡於畫八卦之包羲
===
而非羲也其始於於穆不已之天乎蓋本
為一誠列為四德散為五行而聖人得之
以為心於是乎清明純粹之實自然光輝
發越條理分明故達而在上則昌言嘉謨
足以定國是而以文章見於政窮而在下
則潜德隱行足以勵世俗而以文章筆之
書聖人何嘗有意於為文哉故夫三代無
文人非無文人也風俗渾厚有欲工而不
能之意然觀周詩田夫田婦摸寫之工何
punctuated:
可愛也。然有不充則缺矣，有不造則偏矣，有不運則滯矣。是故自聖人以下，邪正不同路，純駁不同色，大小不同器，清濁不同流，而文章亦與之俱。嗚呼！文章固學者之末事也，而於此可以觀心志焉，可以考節操焉，可以驗智識焉，可以占才能焉。文其可易言耶？請因明問所及而陳之。
夫文章唯孔子之六經至矣，而何所昉乎？煥於被四表之堯，而非堯也；盡於畫八卦之包羲，而非羲也。其始於於穆不已之天乎？蓋本為一誠，列為四德，散為五行，而聖人得之以為心。於是乎清明純粹之實，自然光輝發越，條理分明。故達而在上，則昌言嘉謨足以定國是，而以文章見於政；窮而在下，則潜德隱行足以勵世俗，而以文章筆之書。聖人何嘗有意於為文哉？故夫三代無文人，非無文人也，風俗渾厚，有欲工而不能之意。然觀周詩，田夫田婦摸寫之工，何
translation_en:
…pleasing indeed. Yet where there is insufficient fullness, there is deficiency; where attainment falls short, there is partiality; where operation fails, there is stagnation. Thus, below the sages, the deviant and the upright follow different paths, the pure and the mixed bear different colors, the great and the small have different capacities, and the clear and the turbid flow in different streams. Their literary expression accompanies these differences. Alas! Literary composition is certainly a secondary concern for the scholar, yet through it one may observe his aspirations, examine his integrity, test his understanding, and gauge his abilities. Can literature, then, be lightly discussed? Allow me to set forth my views on the matters raised in your illuminating question.
In literary expression, only the Six Classics of Confucius reach perfection. But where did it originate? It shone in Yao, whose influence extended to the four limits of the world, yet it did not originate with Yao. It was fully realized in Baoxi, who drew the eight trigrams, yet it did not originate with him. Did it begin with Heaven, august and unceasing? At its root it is a single sincerity; articulated, it becomes the four virtues; dispersed, it becomes the Five Phases. The sage receives it as his heart. Thus its clear, luminous, pure substance naturally radiates brilliance and manifests a distinct order. Hence, when successful and occupying high office, the sage offers excellent counsel and worthy plans sufficient to establish the proper course of the state, manifesting literary expression in government. When thwarted and dwelling below, his hidden virtue and unheralded conduct suffice to inspire the customs of the age, and he commits these to writing through literary expression. When did the sage ever deliberately set out to compose literature? Thus, to say that the Three Dynasties had no literary men does not mean that there were none. Their customs were simple and substantial, suggesting that even if they wished to cultivate literary artifice, they could not. Yet when we examine the poems of Zhou and the skill with which farmers and their wives depicted things, how…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文人之多也六經無文法非無文法也無
意於立法而紆徐曲折有化工自然之妙
若明問所論大誥繫辭諸篇是也後世之
論文者吾惑焉如張文潜之說則學文以
明理爲急如倪正父之說則爲文以體製
爲先二者似之而實非也夫理非文外之
物也惟平日務學明理之功既深則吾之
爲文無意於明理而理趣有不可遏矣無
意於合體而體製自有可觀矣若如二子
===
之說則爲文之時尋何理以爲通貫檢何
體以爲法程此即明問所謂以文章爲事
業汲汲乎弊精神以求見於世而不自知
其勞者也而何怪其不能追古作哉至於
文章與時高下三代之文至戰國而病涉
秦漢復起秦漢之文至三國而病唐興復
起此劉夢得之說似之而亦有未盡然者
夫文之興也以道道之興也以學而豈興
於時哉如興於時則春秋何以興六經戰
punctuated:
文人之多也！六經無文法，非無文法也，無意於立法，而紆徐曲折，有化工自然之妙，若明問所論《大誥》《繫辭》諸篇是也。後世之論文者，吾惑焉。如張文潜之說，則學文以明理爲急；如倪正父之說，則爲文以體製爲先。二者似之而實非也。夫理非文外之物也，惟平日務學明理之功既深，則吾之爲文，無意於明理，而理趣有不可遏矣；無意於合體，而體製自有可觀矣。若如二子之說，則爲文之時，尋何理以爲通貫，檢何體以爲法程？此即明問所謂以文章爲事業，汲汲乎弊精神以求見於世，而不自知其勞者也。而何怪其不能追古作哉？
至於文章與時高下，三代之文至戰國而病，涉秦漢復起；秦漢之文至三國而病，唐興復起。此劉夢得之說，似之而亦有未盡然者。夫文之興也以道，道之興也以學，而豈興於時哉？如興於時，則春秋何以興六經，戰
translation_en:
…how numerous the literary talents were! To say that the Six Classics have no rules of composition does not mean that they lack such rules. They have no deliberate intention of establishing rules, yet their leisurely unfolding and intricate turns possess the spontaneous subtlety of nature’s creative workings. Such are the chapters mentioned in your discerning question, including the Great Announcement and the Appended Statements.
I am perplexed by later generations’ discussions of writing. According to Zhang Wenqian, in studying composition one must give priority to illuminating principle; according to Ni Zhengfu, in composing one must put literary form first. Both views seem right but are in fact mistaken. Principle is not something external to writing. Only when one’s everyday efforts to pursue learning and clarify principle have become profound will the significance of principle flow irrepressibly through one’s writing, without any deliberate intention to illuminate it. Without any deliberate intention to conform to a form, the composition’s form will naturally have merits worth appreciating. If one follows these two men’s views, then, when composing, what principle is one to seek to give the piece coherence, and what form is one to examine as a prescribed model? This is precisely what your discerning question describes: making literary composition one’s lifework, anxiously exhausting one’s mental energies in pursuit of recognition in the world, without oneself realizing the toil involved. Why, then, be surprised that such writers cannot match the works of antiquity?
As for literature rising and falling with the times: the literature of the Three Dynasties declined by the Warring States period and revived during the Qin and Han; the literature of the Qin and Han declined by the Three Kingdoms period and revived with the rise of the Tang. This view of Liu Mengde’s seems right, yet it too is not entirely so. Literature flourishes through the Way, and the Way flourishes through learning. How could its flourishing depend on the times? If it depended on the times, then how could the Six Classics have arisen in the Spring and Autumn period, and the Warring…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國何以與七篇哉其說亦牽合矣就其所
論文人而品評之列禦寇之文平淡疎曠
莊周之文跌蕩開闔荀况之文敷腴宏大
皆有可觀者矣然莊列荒唐多寓言與佛
氏老子之說相表裏至漁父盜跖篇又詆
孔子之徒是叛禮背教甚矣荀子極偏駁
觀其以性爲惡以禮爲僞以子思孟軻亂
天下至於事黃歇教李斯則其爲人之卑
又可知矣而何文之足論哉漢之能爲文
===
===
者皆曰賈生董相史遷相如楊雄然賈之
文質實董之文滋潤司馬之文雄健相如
之文富麗楊雄之文奧衍是皆文人之白
眉也但表餌之策幾於疎上林之賦流於
侈法言妄擬論語史記乃後六經且卓君
之開爐新莽之執贄固立身之大玷而哭
懷王以殞命救李陵以殘軀亦不知義命
者矣董之議論多騎墻而惑於災異之說
固非醇乎其醇也然正義明道之訓漢諸
punctuated: 國何以與七篇哉？其說亦牽合矣。就其所論文人而品評之，列禦寇之文平淡疎曠，莊周之文跌蕩開闔，荀况之文敷腴宏大，皆有可觀者矣。然莊列荒唐，多寓言，與佛氏老子之說相表裏。至《漁父》《盜跖》篇，又詆孔子之徒，是叛禮背教甚矣。荀子極偏駁，觀其以性爲惡，以禮爲僞，以子思孟軻亂天下，至於事黃歇、教李斯，則其爲人之卑又可知矣，而何文之足論哉？漢之能爲文者，皆曰賈生、董相、史遷、相如、楊雄。然賈之文質實，董之文滋潤，司馬之文雄健，相如之文富麗，楊雄之文奧衍，是皆文人之白眉也。但表餌之策幾於疎，《上林》之賦流於侈，《法言》妄擬《論語》，《史記》乃後六經。且卓君之開爐、新莽之執贄，固立身之大玷；而哭懷王以殞命，救李陵以殘軀，亦不知義命者矣。董之議論多騎墻，而惑於災異之說，固非醇乎其醇也。然正義明道之訓，漢諸
translation_en:
…in the Warring States period, how could the Seven Chapters have arisen [?]? This explanation, too, strains to make things fit. If we assess the writers he discusses, Lie Yukou’s prose is plain, understated, open, and expansive; Zhuang Zhou’s is boldly undulating, opening out and drawing together; and Xun Kuang’s is ample, rich, and grand. All have qualities worth admiring. Yet Zhuang Zhou and Lie Yukou are fanciful and extravagant, making frequent use of allegories; their writings and the teachings of the Buddha and Laozi mutually reinforce one another. The chapters “The Fisherman” and “Robber Zhi” even disparage Confucius and his followers. This is an extreme betrayal of ritual propriety and the teachings of the sages. Xunzi is thoroughly one-sided and inconsistent. Consider his claims that human nature is evil, that ritual is an artificial creation, and that Zisi and Meng Ke threw the world into disorder. His service to Huang Xie and instruction of Li Si further reveal the baseness of his character. What, then, is there in his prose worth discussing?

Among accomplished Han writers, everyone names Master Jia, Minister Dong, the historian Sima Qian, Xiangru, and Yang Xiong. Jia’s prose is substantial and solid; Dong’s, rich and mellow; Sima’s, vigorous and forceful; Xiangru’s, sumptuous and splendid; and Yang Xiong’s, profound and expansive. These are all outstanding literary figures. Yet the policy of inducements and rewards was almost impracticable; the “Rhapsody on the Imperial Park” lapsed into extravagance; Model Sayings presumptuously imitated the Analects; and the Records of the Grand Historian placed the Six Classics afterward [?]. Moreover, Zhuo Jun’s tending a wine-shop stove [?] and the presentation of a gift of allegiance to Wang Mang’s Xin regime were certainly great blemishes on personal conduct. To mourn King Huai until one died, and to seek to save Li Ling only to suffer mutilation oneself, likewise showed a failure to understand righteousness and fate. Dong’s arguments often straddled opposing positions, and he was misled by theories of calamities and anomalies: he certainly was not wholly pure in his learning. Yet, as for his injunction to uphold righteousness and illuminate the Way, among the Han scholars…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
儒孰能出其右者耶漢之後曰唐吾得一
韓昌黎爲一時山斗唐之後爲宋吾得一
歐陽永叔足以追韓氏而先後爭光者也
今以二子之文論之愈之文刋落陳言酷
排釋氏其言汗漫卓踔𣺌泫閎深眞所謂
日光玉潔周情孔思者也史臣稱之曰摧
陷廓清之功比孟子而力倍之今雖不可
謂倍孟子也獨不謂孟子之徒乎蘇子稱
歐子之文也曰詩賦如李白記事如司馬
===
遷論治如陸贄至於變文體濯士氣以救
時行道其功亦不細矣以其文考之則豐
樂亭等記玉顔身累等詩一唱三嘆寄美
麗於平淡當時以爲今之韓愈夫復何愧
哉但晦菴之論有曰韓千變萬化無心而
最高歐有心而可學蓋韓之文如馭馬通
衢塵陌縱橫馳逐唯意所至何高也歐之
文如賓主相見平心易氣而雍容揖遜此
所以可學也若論其文之不能無病則讀
punctuated: 儒孰能出其右者耶？漢之後曰唐，吾得一韓昌黎，爲一時山斗。唐之後爲宋，吾得一歐陽永叔，足以追韓氏而先後爭光者也。今以二子之文論之，愈之文刋落陳言，酷排釋氏，其言汗漫卓踔，𣺌泫閎深，眞所謂日光玉潔、周情孔思者也。史臣稱之曰：「摧陷廓清之功，比孟子而力倍之。」今雖不可謂倍孟子也，獨不謂孟子之徒乎？蘇子稱歐子之文也，曰：「詩賦如李白，記事如司馬遷，論治如陸贄。」至於變文體、濯士氣，以救時行道，其功亦不細矣。以其文考之，則《豐樂亭》等記、《玉顔》《身累》等詩，一唱三嘆，寄美麗於平淡，當時以爲今之韓愈，夫復何愧哉？但晦菴之論有曰：「韓千變萬化，無心而最高；歐有心而可學。」蓋韓之文如馭馬通衢塵陌，縱橫馳逐，唯意所至，何高也！歐之文如賓主相見，平心易氣，而雍容揖遜，此所以可學也。若論其文之不能無病，則讀
translation_en:
…among the Confucian scholars of the Han, who could surpass him? After the Han came the Tang, in which I find Han Changli, a Mount Tai and Northern Dipper for his age. After the Tang came the Song, in which I find Ouyang Yongshu, worthy to follow Han and rival his brilliance across the generations. To discuss these two men’s writings: Han Yu stripped away stale expressions and vehemently rejected Buddhism. His language is boundless and soaring, vast and profound [?], truly deserving the description “radiant as the sun, pure as jade, with the feelings of the Duke of Zhou and the thoughts of Confucius.” The official historian praised him thus: “His achievement in crushing opposition and clearing the field compares with that of Mencius, but with twice the force.” Although we cannot now say that he surpassed Mencius twofold, can we not call him a follower of Mencius?

Master Su praised Master Ouyang’s writing, saying: “In poetry and rhapsodies he resembles Li Bai; in recording events, Sima Qian; in discussing government, Lu Zhi.” As for transforming literary style and cleansing the spirit of scholars, thereby remedying the ills of the age and putting the Way into practice, his achievements were considerable. Examining his writings, we find accounts such as “The Pavilion of Abundant Joy” and poems such as “Jade Countenance” and “Burdened by the Person” [?]. One singing calls forth three lingering responses: he lodges beauty within plainness. His contemporaries considered him the Han Yu of their day; what cause had he to feel unworthy of that comparison?

Yet Hui’an offered this assessment: “Han undergoes a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations; without deliberate intent, he reaches the greatest heights. Ouyang writes with deliberate intent and can be learned from.” Han’s writing is like riding a horse along broad thoroughfares and dusty roads, galloping freely in every direction, wherever the will takes it—how lofty it is! Ouyang’s writing is like host and guest meeting, calm in mind and gentle in manner, bowing and yielding with composed grace. This is why it can be learned from. If, however, we discuss how their writings cannot be free of faults, then ‘On Reading…’

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
墨篇以異端並之聖人孟簡書為太顛所
惑至以博愛為仁三品為性則見用而昧
體誠有所不免者矣歐子自稱曰我所為
文必與道俱則與道與文為二事故本論
雖正而以封建井田之禮變佛氏亦拙矣
又以琴書棊酒與老人為六是何言之放
誕不羈哉蓋平日以性非所急而以十翼
不出於孔子亦幾於叛矣是故晦菴所謂
治世之文程子所謂化工之文二子皆不
===
能造其藩籬祗皆飲酒賦詩而因文以見
道也其在剪裁之下繪畫之上乎又就二
子之文而低昂之歐晚年筆力亦衰其文
終不如韓而韓之文又不如漢漢之文又
不如先秦戰國蓋去聖有遠近而聞道有
多寡也又就二子之人品而論之韓子以
出使折藩鎮勁氣凛於氷霜以極諫貶潮
陽精忠貫乎日月而歐之犯顏直諫救時
行道君子恃而不恐小人畏而不為則皆
punctuated: 墨篇，以異端並之聖人；孟簡書，為太顛所惑。至以博愛為仁，三品為性，則見用而昧體，誠有所不免者矣。歐子自稱曰：「我所為文，必與道俱。」則與道與文為二事，故本論雖正，而以封建井田之禮變佛氏，亦拙矣。又以琴書棊酒與老人為六，是何言之放誕不羈哉！蓋平日以性非所急，而以十翼不出於孔子，亦幾於叛矣。是故晦菴所謂治世之文，程子所謂化工之文，二子皆不能造其藩籬，祗皆飲酒賦詩，而因文以見道也。其在剪裁之下、繪畫之上乎？又就二子之文而低昂之，歐晚年筆力亦衰，其文終不如韓，而韓之文又不如漢，漢之文又不如先秦戰國，蓋去聖有遠近，而聞道有多寡也。又就二子之人品而論之，韓子以出使折藩鎮，勁氣凛於氷霜；以極諫貶潮陽，精忠貫乎日月。而歐之犯顏直諫，救時行道，君子恃而不恐，小人畏而不為，則皆
translation_en:
…in his essay “Reading Mozi,” he places a heterodox thinker alongside the sages; in his letter to Meng Jian, he is beguiled by Taidian. As for identifying universal love with benevolence and dividing human nature into three grades, he perceives function but remains ignorant of substance: these are indeed failings he could not escape. Master Ou declares of himself: “The writing I produce must always accompany the Way.” Yet this makes the Way and writing two separate things. Thus, although the fundamental argument of his “On Fundamentals” is sound, his attempt to transform Buddhism through the institutions of enfeoffment and the well-field system is also clumsy. Moreover, he counts the zither, books, chess, wine, and the old man as six [?]. How extravagant and unrestrained such words are! He ordinarily regarded human nature as no urgent concern, and held that the Ten Wings did not come from Confucius: this, too, verged on repudiating the sages.

Consequently, neither of these two masters could even reach the outer bounds of what Hui’an called “the writing of a well-governed age” or what Master Cheng called “writing wrought by nature.” They merely drank wine and composed poems, using literary composition to reveal the Way. Might their writing rank below “cutting and tailoring” but above “painting”? Furthermore, if we rank their writings against each other, Ou’s literary vigor also declined in his later years, and his writing ultimately falls short of Han’s. Han’s writing, in turn, falls short of that of the Han dynasty, and Han-dynasty writing falls short of that of the pre-Qin Warring States period. This is because their distance from the sages differed, as did the extent of their acquaintance with the Way.

If we turn instead to the personal character of the two masters, Han Yu, sent on a mission, subdued a military governor, displaying a resolute spirit as austere as ice and frost. Demoted to Chaoyang for his uncompromising remonstrance, his pure loyalty shone through sun and moon. Ouyang Xiu, for his part, braved the ruler’s displeasure to remonstrate frankly, redeeming his age and putting the Way into practice. Exemplary men relied on him and felt no fear; petty men feared him and refrained from wrongdoing. Thus both were…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
俊偉光明董仲舒以後所未有也其視荀
揚之擇不精語不詳而為名敎罪人何啻
珠玉之於瓦礫耶昔吕與叔之詩有曰文
如元凱方成癖學類相如始類俳獨立孔
門無一事只輸顏子得心齋則固以君子
之學務其遠者大者而不徒事其文也愚
也讀古人之文固未嘗不策勵而欲追其
歩驟咏吕氏之詩又未嘗不猛省而欲造
乎坐忘也惟執事其濯磨之
===
第四問
饒相
同考試官訓導王 批 道統之傳在學者最當體究此
策獨能探之得非學之有得者邪良士良士
考試官敎諭張 批 深契源流
考試官敎授錢 批 明備
孔門道統之傳惟聖賢為能深以造之明
以通之夫聖人之道昭灼如火焉潤澤如
水焉蓋無一息之間斷遏佚也而何待後
punctuated:
俊偉光明，董仲舒以後所未有也。其視荀揚之擇不精、語不詳，而為名敎罪人，何啻珠玉之於瓦礫耶！昔吕與叔之詩有曰：「文如元凱方成癖，學類相如始類俳。獨立孔門無一事，只輸顏子得心齋。」則固以君子之學務其遠者大者，而不徒事其文也。愚也讀古人之文，固未嘗不策勵而欲追其歩驟；咏吕氏之詩，又未嘗不猛省而欲造乎坐忘也。惟執事其濯磨之。

第四問
饒相
同考試官訓導王批：「道統之傳，在學者最當體究。此策獨能探之，得非學之有得者邪？良士！良士！」
考試官敎諭張批：「深契源流。」
考試官敎授錢批：「明備。」

孔門道統之傳，惟聖賢為能深以造之，明以通之。夫聖人之道，昭灼如火焉，潤澤如水焉，蓋無一息之間斷遏佚也。而何待後
translation_en:
…outstanding and illustrious, such as had not been seen since Dong Zhongshu. Compared with Xun Kuang and Yang Xiong, whose judgments lacked precision and whose statements lacked thoroughness, making them offenders against the moral teaching, were they not far more superior than pearls and jade are to broken tiles and rubble? Lü Yushu once wrote in a poem: “Devotion to letters like Yuan Kai’s becomes an obsession; learning like Xiangru’s begins to resemble a jester’s art. Standing alone within Confucius’s gate, with nothing to occupy oneself, one still yields to Master Yan, who attained the fasting of the mind.” Indeed, the gentleman’s learning pursues what is far-reaching and great, rather than merely attending to literary composition. When I, in my ignorance, read the writings of the ancients, I invariably spur myself on, wishing to follow in their footsteps. When I recite Lü’s poem, I likewise invariably awaken with a start, wishing to attain the state of “sitting in forgetfulness.” I ask you, honored sir, to cleanse and polish me.

Fourth Question
Rao Xiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: “The transmission of the succession to the Way is what students should above all personally investigate and comprehend. This policy essay alone succeeds in probing it. Surely its author has gained something through learning? A worthy scholar! A worthy scholar!”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “A profound grasp of the source and its subsequent course.”

Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: “Clear and comprehensive.”

As for the transmission of the succession to the Way within the school of Confucius, only sages and worthies can attain its depths and comprehend it with clarity. The Way of the sages shines brightly like fire and moistens and nourishes like water. Never for a single instant is it interrupted or obstructed [?]. Why, then, should it await those who come after…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人傳授以為之主張哉蓋使世道而常如
唐虞可無恙也唯立異者激之好高者揚
之用邪者壅之自私者撲之激則其流橫
矣揚則其本搖矣壅則其坊壞矣撲則其
光晦矣然則主盟斯世以任繼往開來之
責在聖賢可得而辭者哉顧夫時有先後
地有淺深有不可強而同者維扶世立教
而議論不詭於聖人則皆可謂濬其流也
揚其波也助其瀾也皆可謂嘘其烟也熾
===
其膏也裂其焰也安得世世如大聖人而
後可秉吾道之旌麾哉今夫世之語道統
者曰奇偶二畫包羲為文字之祖執中一
語帝堯肇心學之源列聖相承曰精曰一
曰義曰禮曰敬曰義辭雖不同而道實相
同也孰知夫子集群聖之大成而作為六
經以詔萬世皆其所自得師哉故謂夫子
為文字之祖心學之源可也而豈可獨歸
之羲堯耶夫孔子既為萬世心學之源則
punctuated:
人傳授以為之主張哉？蓋使世道而常如唐虞，可無恙也。唯立異者激之，好高者揚之，用邪者壅之，自私者撲之。激則其流橫矣，揚則其本搖矣，壅則其坊壞矣，撲則其光晦矣。然則主盟斯世，以任繼往開來之責，在聖賢可得而辭者哉？顧夫時有先後，地有淺深，有不可強而同者。維扶世立教，而議論不詭於聖人，則皆可謂濬其流也，揚其波也，助其瀾也；皆可謂嘘其烟也，熾其膏也，裂其焰也。安得世世如大聖人，而後可秉吾道之旌麾哉？

今夫世之語道統者曰：「奇偶二畫，包羲為文字之祖；執中一語，帝堯肇心學之源。列聖相承，曰精，曰一，曰義，曰禮，曰敬，曰義，辭雖不同，而道實相同也。」孰知夫子集群聖之大成，而作為六經以詔萬世，皆其所自得師哉？故謂夫子為文字之祖、心學之源可也，而豈可獨歸之羲堯耶？夫孔子既為萬世心學之源，則
translation_en:
…for later people to transmit it and uphold it? If the way of the world always remained as it was under Tang Yao and Yu Shun, it could indeed remain unharmed. But those who insist on being different agitate it; those who aspire to lofty things toss it aloft; those who employ perversity obstruct it; and the selfish smother it. Agitated, its current runs wild; tossed aloft, its foundation is shaken; obstructed, its embankments collapse; smothered, its light grows dim. Can sages and worthies, then, decline to take the lead in this world and assume responsibility for carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future? Yet their times differ, and the ground they occupy varies in depth: these cannot forcibly be made alike. So long as they sustain the world and establish its teachings, and their arguments do not depart from those of the sages, they may all be said to deepen its current, raise its waves, and swell its billows; they may all be said to fan its smoke, kindle its oil, and make its flames flare. How could we require someone equal to the great sage in every generation before anyone could bear the banners of our Way?

Now those in the world who speak of the succession of the Way say: “Through the two kinds of lines, odd and even, Baoxi became the progenitor of writing; through the single phrase ‘hold fast to the mean,’ Emperor Yao opened the source of the learning of the mind. The successive sages handed it down, speaking of refinement, singleness, righteousness, ritual propriety, reverence, and righteousness. Although their words differed, their Way was truly the same.” Who recognizes that the Master brought together the consummate achievements of all the sages and composed the Six Classics to instruct the myriad generations, all arising from what he himself had grasped as his teacher [?]? Thus it is permissible to call the Master the progenitor of writing and the source of the learning of the mind. How could these distinctions be assigned exclusively to Baoxi and Yao? Since Kongzi is the source of the learning of the mind for the myriad generations, then…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其一脉之相傳不可不要其始而究其終
矣夫孔門高弟唯顏氏曾氏之傳得其宗
曾氏以是傳之子思子思以是傳之孟子
此黃勉齋謂孟子傳統於子思之說也抑
不曰傳孔子之統而謂傳統於子思者特
據其及門受業言之也若以其功論之孟
子蘊經綸之大業而發明性道純乎純故
謂孟子傳子思之統可也傳孔子之統亦
可也豈必見而知之爲傳道聞而知之者
===
非傳道耶顏子卒於陋巷孟子亦不見用
於齊梁是皆隱未見行未成也而朱子以
顏子優湯武程子以孟子並禹稷者蓋顏
子有若無實若虛氣象何溫淳也然以有
爲如舜而敢問爲邦則其剛大之志王佐
之材又可想見故使其見諸事業雖不及
湯而成就則渾渾無痕迹雖湯亦有所不
及也是之謂優於湯武也孟子以身任道
而息邪說拒詖行放淫詞自以爲承禹抑
punctuated:
其一脉之相傳，不可不要其始而究其終矣。夫孔門高弟，唯顏氏、曾氏之傳得其宗。曾氏以是傳之子思，子思以是傳之孟子，此黃勉齋謂孟子傳統於子思之說也。抑不曰傳孔子之統，而謂傳統於子思者，特據其及門受業言之也。若以其功論之，孟子蘊經綸之大業，而發明性道，純乎純。故謂孟子傳子思之統可也，傳孔子之統亦可也。豈必見而知之爲傳道，聞而知之者非傳道耶？

顏子卒於陋巷，孟子亦不見用於齊梁，是皆隱未見、行未成也。而朱子以顏子優湯武，程子以孟子並禹稷者，蓋顏子有若無，實若虛，氣象何溫淳也！然以有爲如舜，而敢問爲邦，則其剛大之志、王佐之材，又可想見。故使其見諸事業，雖不及湯，而成就則渾渾無痕迹，雖湯亦有所不及也。是之謂優於湯武也。孟子以身任道，而息邪說、拒詖行、放淫詞，自以爲承禹抑
translation_en:
…the transmission of its single lineage must therefore be traced to its beginning and investigated through to its end. Among Confucius’s eminent disciples, only Yan Hui and Zeng Shen grasped its essential teaching in what they transmitted. Zeng Shen passed this on to Zisi, and Zisi passed it on to Mengzi. This is the meaning of Huang Mianzhai’s statement that Mengzi received the succession from Zisi. Yet his saying that Mengzi received the succession from Zisi, rather than that he transmitted Confucius’s succession, refers solely to his having entered Zisi’s school and received instruction. If we judge by his contribution, Mengzi possessed the capacity for the great undertaking of ordering the world and elucidated human nature and the Way with the utmost purity. Thus one may say that Mengzi transmitted Zisi’s succession, or equally that he transmitted Confucius’s succession. Must only those who knew through seeing count as transmitters of the Way, while those who knew through hearing do not?

Master Yan died in a humble alley, and Mengzi likewise found no employment in Qi or Liang. In both cases their abilities remained hidden rather than manifested, and their endeavors remained unaccomplished. Yet Master Zhu ranked Master Yan above Tang and Wu, and Master Cheng placed Mengzi alongside Yu and Ji. Master Yan possessed abilities yet seemed to possess none; he was full yet seemed empty. How warm and pure was his bearing! Yet he believed that anyone who acted could become like Shun, and dared to ask how to govern a state. We can thus imagine his firm and expansive resolve and his talent for assisting a true king. Had these found expression in practical achievements, even if he had not equaled Tang, his accomplishments would have been seamless, leaving no trace of contrivance; in this respect even Tang would have fallen short. This is what is meant by ranking him above Tang and Wu. Mengzi took personal responsibility for the Way, putting an end to heterodox doctrines, opposing deviant conduct, and banishing licentious words. He considered himself to be carrying forward the work of Yu in restraining…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
洪水周公驅猛獸孔子作春秋之功不然
楊墨之禍世未止也以孟子比禹稷豈不
宜耶孟子既没聖學失傳歷世久遠其間
儒者非不知尊孔孟而談六經然不越文
義訓詁之間而止矣濂溪生千載之下獨
得微旨而發之圖書凡太極性命陰陽鬼
神綱分彪別使學者曉然知所準的此正
明問所謂濂溪傳孟子之統者也而謂受
學於希夷豈知濂溪者哉自是一傳而得
===
二程數傳而得紫陽二程之學皆以學庸
語孟爲標的而達於六經辯異端扶正道
故伊川謂明道孟子以後一人而已紫陽
之學又集諸儒之大成而粹乎洙泗伊洛
之緒故鶴山謂朱子之功不在孟子下也
然則謂紫陽傳二程之統可也謂傳孟子
之統亦可也謂程子傳濂溪之統可也謂
傳孟子之統亦可也蓋千聖一心也萬古
一道也何先後彼此之間耶當時橫渠之
punctuated: 洪水、周公驅猛獸、孔子作《春秋》之功。不然，楊墨之禍世未止也。以孟子比禹稷，豈不宜耶？孟子既没，聖學失傳，歷世久遠，其間儒者非不知尊孔孟而談六經，然不越文義訓詁之間而止矣。濂溪生千載之下，獨得微旨而發之圖書。凡太極、性命、陰陽、鬼神，綱分彪別，使學者曉然知所準的。此正明問所謂濂溪傳孟子之統者也。而謂受學於希夷，豈知濂溪者哉？自是一傳而得二程，數傳而得紫陽。二程之學，皆以《學》《庸》《語》《孟》爲標的，而達於六經，辯異端，扶正道。故伊川謂明道，孟子以後一人而已。紫陽之學，又集諸儒之大成，而粹乎洙泗伊洛之緒。故鶴山謂朱子之功不在孟子下也。然則謂紫陽傳二程之統可也，謂傳孟子之統亦可也；謂程子傳濂溪之統可也，謂傳孟子之統亦可也。蓋千聖一心也，萬古一道也，何先後彼此之間耶？當時橫渠之
translation_en: …the floods, the Duke of Zhou's driving away ferocious beasts, and Confucius's composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Otherwise, the harm that the teachings of Yang Zhu and Mo Di inflicted upon the world would not have ceased. Is it not fitting to compare Mengzi with Yu and Ji? After Mengzi died, the learning of the sages lost its transmission. Many generations passed. The scholars of that interval certainly knew to revere Confucius and Mengzi and discuss the Six Classics, but they went no further than textual meanings and philological glosses. Born a thousand years later, Lianxi (Zhou Dunyi) alone grasped the subtle purport and expressed it in diagrams and writings. Whether treating the Supreme Ultimate, human nature and destiny, yin and yang, or ghosts and spirits, he clearly distinguished their guiding principles, enabling students to understand plainly what standards to follow. This is precisely what your discerning question means by Lianxi's transmitting Mengzi's succession. Could anyone who claims that he studied under Xiyi (Chen Tuan) truly understand Lianxi? From him, transmission through one generation reached the two Cheng brothers, and through several generations reached Ziyang (Zhu Xi). The learning of both Cheng brothers took the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, the Analects, and the Mengzi as its guides and extended to the Six Classics, refuting heterodox teachings and upholding the correct Way. Thus Yichuan (Cheng Yi) said that Mingdao (Cheng Hao) was the one unique figure since Mengzi. Ziyang's learning in turn brought the achievements of the various scholars to their fullest realization and embodied in purity the traditions of the Zhu and Si rivers and of the Yi and Luo rivers. Thus Heshan (Wei Liaoweng) said that Master Zhu's achievement was not inferior to Mengzi's. Accordingly, one may say that Ziyang transmitted the succession of the two Cheng brothers, or that he transmitted Mengzi's succession. One may say that Master Cheng transmitted Lianxi's succession, or that he transmitted Mengzi's succession. For the thousand sages share one mind, and throughout all ages there is one Way. What distinction can there be between earlier and later, or between this person and that? At that time, Hengqu's (Zhang Zai's) …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
精思力踐妙契疾書堯夫之天挺人豪英
邁蓋世延平之身世兩忘精義造約東萊
備四時之和涵千古之秘敬夫擴仁義之
端謹義利之辨皆於吾道有聞焉者也而
不得與道統豈非張邵猶宗乎二程呂張
猶宗乎晦翁者耶程子之門若謝上蔡朱
子之門若蔡季通亦庶幾有聞於道矣君
子論道統而以程子傳之龜山朱子傳之
勉齋者豈二子之學能過於張邵諸賢哉
===
亦自其能傳中庸易學能成經傳通解皆
見知之眞者而許之也豈天下定論哉若
夫二程之學晦翁以爲明道比顏伊川比
孟者蓋明道之德性寬大規模廣闊伊川
氣質剛方文理密察其氣象實相當也而
一愛游定夫一愛楊中立亦豈不以二人
氣象之相類哉但明道之比顏固亦然矣
伊川檢朿之功孟子不能及而孟子雄才
又非伊川所能到也就以二程行事而觀
punctuated:
精思力踐，妙契疾書；堯夫之天挺人豪，英邁蓋世；延平之身世兩忘，精義造約；東萊備四時之和，涵千古之秘；敬夫擴仁義之端，謹義利之辨，皆於吾道有聞焉者也。而不得與道統，豈非張邵猶宗乎二程，呂張猶宗乎晦翁者耶？程子之門若謝上蔡，朱子之門若蔡季通，亦庶幾有聞於道矣。君子論道統，而以程子傳之龜山、朱子傳之勉齋者，豈二子之學能過於張邵諸賢哉？亦自其能傳中庸易學，能成經傳通解，皆見知之眞者而許之也，豈天下定論哉？
若夫二程之學，晦翁以爲明道比顏、伊川比孟者，蓋明道之德性寬大，規模廣闊；伊川氣質剛方，文理密察，其氣象實相當也。而一愛游定夫，一愛楊中立，亦豈不以二人氣象之相類哉？但明道之比顏，固亦然矣；伊川檢朿之功，孟子不能及，而孟子雄才，又非伊川所能到也。就以二程行事而觀
translation_en:
…profound reflection and vigorous practice, subtle understanding and swift writing; Yaofu’s being a naturally gifted hero among men, whose outstanding brilliance surpassed his age; Yanping’s forgetting both self and worldly circumstances, refining his understanding of principles and reaching their essentials; Donglai’s embodying the harmony of the four seasons and encompassing the hidden wisdom of all antiquity; and Jingfu’s expanding the beginnings of humaneness and righteousness and carefully distinguishing righteousness from profit—all these men had gained an understanding of our Way. Yet they were not included in the succession of the Way. Was this not because Zhang Zai and Shao Yong still took the two Cheng brothers as their masters, while Lü Zuqian and Zhang Shi still took Huiweng as theirs? Among Master Cheng’s disciples, men such as Xie Shangcai, and among Master Zhu’s disciples, men such as Cai Jitong, had also come close to understanding the Way. When gentlemen discuss its succession and hold that Master Cheng transmitted it to Guishan, and Master Zhu to Mianzhai, can it be that these two men’s learning surpassed that of Zhang, Shao, and the other worthies? They accord them this recognition simply because one could transmit the learning of the Doctrine of the Mean and the Changes, and the other could complete the Comprehensive Explanations of the Classics and Commentaries, both displaying genuine understanding. How could this be a settled judgment accepted by all under Heaven?
As for the learning of the two Cheng brothers, Huiweng considered Mingdao comparable to Yan Hui and Yichuan comparable to Mencius. This was because Mingdao’s moral nature was generous and capacious, and the scope of his learning broad, while Yichuan’s temperament was firm and upright, and his discernment of patterns and principles meticulous. Their respective bearing did indeed correspond to that of those earlier sages. That one favored You Dingfu and the other Yang Zhongli—was this not also because each disciple resembled his master in bearing? Yet, although the comparison of Mingdao to Yan Hui is certainly apt, Mencius could not match Yichuan’s achievement in self-restraint, while Mencius’s extraordinary talents were beyond Yichuan’s reach. If we examine the conduct of the two Cheng brothers…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之明道爲條例官不以爲浼而伊川作行
狀不載其事明道謂青苗猶可放過而伊
川於西監則一一較計焉是非兄弟有二
道也一則孔子之獵較爲兆一則孟子之
不見諸侯也而何害其爲同耶及以二程
之議論考之明道曰稟於天爲性感爲情
動爲心伊川曰自性之有形謂之心自性
之有動謂之情是則一以動爲心一以動
爲情若不侔矣然以近思錄所載二程體
===
用寂感之說觀之則先儒謂紀錄之誤是
矣而二程豈有異說可駭者哉若夫朱子
謂學顏子入聖人爲近而不言孟子以爲
才高無可據之地也胡文定謂立志以明
道自期待而儕之希文不論其道而論其
志也希文豈足以並明道者耶若夫顏孟
所造皆幾於聖人充之則大矣養之則粹
矣此又顏孟所以自爲深造之學也合而
言之聖賢道統之傳孟子濬其流噓其烟
punctuated: 之，明道爲條例官，不以爲浼，而伊川作行狀，不載其事；明道謂青苗猶可放過，而伊川於西監則一一較計焉。是非兄弟有二道也：一則孔子之獵較爲兆，一則孟子之不見諸侯也，而何害其爲同耶？及以二程之議論考之，明道曰：「稟於天爲性，感爲情，動爲心。」伊川曰：「自性之有形謂之心，自性之有動謂之情。」是則一以動爲心，一以動爲情，若不侔矣。然以《近思錄》所載二程體用寂感之說觀之，則先儒謂紀錄之誤，是矣。而二程豈有異說可駭者哉？若夫朱子謂學顏子入聖人爲近，而不言孟子，以爲才高，無可據之地也。胡文定謂立志以明道自期待，而儕之希文，不論其道，而論其志也。希文豈足以並明道者耶？若夫顏孟所造，皆幾於聖人，充之則大矣，養之則粹矣。此又顏孟所以自爲深造之學也。合而言之，聖賢道統之傳，孟子濬其流，噓其烟
translation_en:
…consider their conduct: Mingdao served as an official in the Regulations Office without regarding it as a defilement, yet when Yichuan wrote his biographical account, he omitted this service. Mingdao said that the Green Sprouts policy could still be let pass, whereas Yichuan scrutinized every detail at Xijian [?]. This does not mean that the brothers followed two different Ways. One resembled Confucius participating in the competitive hunt to establish a precedent; the other resembled Mengzi refusing to seek an audience with the feudal lords. How could this impair their essential agreement?

If we examine the two Cheng brothers’ statements, Mingdao said: “What is endowed by Heaven is the nature; its response to things is feeling; its activity is the mind.” Yichuan said: “The nature insofar as it has form is called the mind; the nature insofar as it has activity is called feeling.” Thus one identifies activity with the mind, the other with feeling, and they seem inconsistent. Yet, judging by the two Cheng brothers’ explanations of substance and function, stillness and response, recorded in Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsi lu), earlier scholars were right to attribute this to an error in recording. How could the two Cheng brothers have held divergent doctrines that should alarm us?

As for Zhu Xi’s statement that learning from Master Yan offers a nearer approach to sagehood, he did not mention Mengzi because he considered Mengzi’s gifts so lofty that they offered no accessible foothold. When Hu Wending said that, in setting one’s resolve, one should aspire to equal Mingdao, and placed him alongside Xiwen, he was discussing their resolve, not their attainment of the Way. How could Xiwen be worthy of standing alongside Mingdao?

As for the attainments of Yan and Mengzi, both approached sagehood: extended to the full, they became great; nourished, they became pure. This, in turn, was how Yan and Mengzi pursued profound attainment through their own learning. Taken together, in the transmission of the sages’ and worthies’ succession to the Way, Mengzi deepened its current and fanned its smoke…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎周程揚其波熾其膏乎紫陽助其瀾烈
其焰乎彼吳草廬又分為元亨利貞之說
以論道統者豈其磨研六經疏滌百氏而
寓自任之意歟是固不可得而知也愚也
識見寡陋豈能於前脩氣象想像而旁通
之哉姑舉所聞於父師者以復而亦不詳
其是否也惟進而教之幸甚
第五問
梁津
===
同考試官教諭余 批酌今古以理外急內政而歸于
得人通變之才識體之論咸可以觀矣
同考試官教諭曾 批勢也者變之所由而德與謀所
以弭變之方也子能悉之其深於經濟哉
考試官教諭張 批練達治體
考試官教授錢 批宏濟之學
天下勢而已矣通其變可施不倦之神而
識其重須為亟反之策凡勢之將變其生
有旁根也其趨有邪徑也其流有頹波也
punctuated:
乎？周程揚其波、熾其膏乎？紫陽助其瀾、烈其焰乎？彼吳草廬又分為元亨利貞之說以論道統者，豈其磨研六經、疏滌百氏而寓自任之意歟？是固不可得而知也。愚也識見寡陋，豈能於前脩氣象想像而旁通之哉？姑舉所聞於父師者以復，而亦不詳其是否也。惟進而教之，幸甚。
第五問
梁津
同考試官教諭余批：酌今古以理外急內政，而歸于得人，通變之才、識體之論，咸可以觀矣。
同考試官教諭曾批：勢也者，變之所由，而德與謀所以弭變之方也。子能悉之，其深於經濟哉！
考試官教諭張批：練達治體。
考試官教授錢批：宏濟之學。
天下勢而已矣。通其變，可施不倦之神；而識其重，須為亟反之策。凡勢之將變，其生有旁根也，其趨有邪徑也，其流有頹波也。
translation_en:
…? Did Zhou and the Cheng brothers raise its waves and kindle its oil? Did Ziyang [Zhu Xi] swell its billows and intensify its flames? As for Wu Caolu, who further discussed the succession of the Way through the categories of origination, flourishing, benefit, and firmness (yuan, heng, li, zhen), was he expressing his intention to assume this responsibility himself through his painstaking study of the Six Classics and his sifting of the hundred schools? This, indeed, cannot be known. With my scant knowledge and narrow understanding, how could I imagine the bearing of the former worthies and thereby attain a broader comprehension? I have merely offered in reply what I have heard from my father and teachers, without being certain whether it is correct. I would be most fortunate if you would further instruct me.
Fifth Question
Liang Jin
Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: He weighs past and present to address external exigencies and internal administration, ultimately grounding his argument in securing the right men. Both his ability to respond to change and his discussion showing an understanding of the essentials of government merit attention.
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: Circumstances give rise to change, while virtue and planning provide the means to quell disorder. You comprehend these fully: how profound your understanding of statecraft!
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: Practiced and discerning in the essentials of government.
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: Learning capable of bringing far-reaching benefit.
All under Heaven is simply a matter of circumstances. By comprehending their changes, one can exercise an inexhaustible capacity for effective action; recognizing their gravity, one must devise a policy to reverse them swiftly. Whenever circumstances are about to change, their emergence has lateral roots, their course has crooked paths, and their flow has collapsing waves…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其仆有敗脉也吾欲爲拯救肅清之方則
在顧乃德訏乃謨何也夫剛斷也者伐謀
之斧斤也中正也者救偏之繩墨也容忍
也者鎭浮之砥柱也惇大也者休否之靈
丹也以是四者隨時出之以爲之綱紀則
嬰盤錯而其鋒益厲矣乘叢雜而其界益
明矣施鼓撓而其風益震矣遇喧囂而其
聲益宏矣然則九州之事亦可决也八蠻
之人亦可化也而何廣東一省之事宜有
===
不可舉者耶且廣東之可患者曰黎峒曰
猺獞曰海寇曰番舶此外患之不可不備
者也曰屯田曰軍伍曰積穀曰徭役此內
政之不可不脩者也執事以是質諸生豈
以愚生長是邦而籌之必熟耶而生非桑
弧有志之人也顧甞以董子爲政如調琴
瑟晦翁論事若持權衡之說而三覆之矣
請終言之瓊州中據黎峒誠皇甫規虺蛇
入室之喻也頃者黎佛二爲妖殺虜官軍
punctuated: 其仆有敗脉也。吾欲爲拯救肅清之方，則在顧乃德、訏乃謨。何也？夫剛斷也者，伐謀之斧斤也；中正也者，救偏之繩墨也；容忍也者，鎭浮之砥柱也；惇大也者，休否之靈丹也。以是四者隨時出之，以爲之綱紀，則嬰盤錯而其鋒益厲矣，乘叢雜而其界益明矣，施鼓撓而其風益震矣，遇喧囂而其聲益宏矣。然則九州之事亦可决也，八蠻之人亦可化也，而何廣東一省之事宜有不可舉者耶？且廣東之可患者，曰黎峒，曰猺獞，曰海寇，曰番舶，此外患之不可不備者也；曰屯田，曰軍伍，曰積穀，曰徭役，此內政之不可不脩者也。執事以是質諸生，豈以愚生長是邦，而籌之必熟耶？而生非桑弧有志之人也。顧甞以董子爲政如調琴瑟、晦翁論事若持權衡之說，而三覆之矣。請終言之。瓊州中據黎峒，誠皇甫規虺蛇入室之喻也。頃者黎佛二爲妖，殺虜官軍。
translation_en:
…Its collapse has underlying veins of decay. If I wish to devise means of rescue and restoration of order, these lie in attending to one's virtue and making one's plans far-reaching. Why is this? Firm resolve is the axe that cuts down hostile schemes; balance and rectitude are the carpenter's line that corrects deviations; forbearance is the rock that steadies restless currents; generosity of spirit is the potent remedy that ends adversity. Bring forth these four qualities as circumstances require and use them as governing principles: when confronting tangled roots, the blade grows sharper; amid complexity, the distinctions become clearer; when applied amid agitation [?], their influence becomes more commanding; and amid clamour, their voice becomes more powerful. Thus even the affairs of the Nine Provinces can be settled, and even the peoples of the eight barbarian regions can be transformed. What affairs of Guangdong alone, then, could prove impossible to manage?

Moreover, among Guangdong's causes for concern are the Li settlements, the Yao and Zhuang peoples, maritime raiders, and foreign ships: these are external dangers against which preparations must be made. Military agricultural colonies, military ranks, grain reserves, and labour services: these are matters of internal administration that must be put in order. You have questioned us candidates about these matters. Is it because you suppose that, having grown up in this region, I must have considered them thoroughly? Yet I am not a man with the far-reaching ambitions symbolized by the mulberry bow. I have, however, repeatedly pondered Master Dong's saying that governing resembles tuning the qin and se zithers, and Huiweng's saying that deliberating on affairs resembles holding a balance. Allow me to conclude by setting out my views.

The interior of Qiongzhou is occupied by Li settlements—truly a case of Huangfu Gui's analogy of venomous snakes entering one's house. Recently Li Fo'er stirred up a heterodox disturbance, killing and capturing government troops.…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今雖生獲以快人心矣而黨與猶未革面
也明問謂搗穴窮巢以驅除之誠是也吾
謂生黎自昔不能為患而所患者熟黎乃
荆湘福閩之亡命雜居者也夫荒服固所
不治而地利在所必爭若得金牛通道以
内立屯帥則宅中有圖大之勢而永絕禍
根顧自古無為此說而事勢未可輕議也
則莫若於犬豕跳梁之境而决加
天討之兵若杜杞之擒破諸蠻趙禼之勦平三
===
峒以作我南方之干城其歸我聲教者若
韓璧之勞來不倦使供賦稅亦可也而豈
可拘一說哉廉州僻近交阯即馬伏波所
立銅柱表界之地也比年西山賊首恣行
劫掠今雖已勦滅以張
國威矣而餘孽猶未授首也明問謂鑿山刋
道以殄滅之誠是也吾謂猺賊不能為患
