而所患者浪賊乃本境奸宄之頑民交通
者也夫山險有所不由而地勢在所必守
punctuated:
今雖生獲以快人心矣，而黨與猶未革面也。明問謂搗穴窮巢以驅除之，誠是也。吾謂生黎自昔不能為患，而所患者熟黎，乃荆湘福閩之亡命雜居者也。夫荒服固所不治，而地利在所必爭。若得金牛通道，以内立屯帥，則宅中有圖大之勢，而永絕禍根。顧自古無為此說，而事勢未可輕議也。則莫若於犬豕跳梁之境，而决加天討之兵，若杜杞之擒破諸蠻、趙禼之勦平三峒，以作我南方之干城。其歸我聲教者，若韓璧之勞來不倦，使供賦稅亦可也，而豈可拘一說哉？
廉州僻近交阯，即馬伏波所立銅柱表界之地也。比年西山賊首恣行劫掠，今雖已勦滅以張國威矣，而餘孽猶未授首也。明問謂鑿山刋道以殄滅之，誠是也。吾謂猺賊不能為患，而所患者浪賊，乃本境奸宄之頑民交通者也。夫山險有所不由，而地勢在所必守。
translation_en:
… Although he has now been captured alive, to the satisfaction of the people, his confederates have yet to show outward submission. Your discerning question proposes striking their lairs and searching out their nests to drive them away. This is indeed right. I would say that the unassimilated Li have never themselves been capable of causing trouble; the danger lies with the assimilated Li, among whom fugitives from Jing, Xiang, Fu, and Min live intermingled. Remote territories may indeed lie beyond our administration, but advantageous ground must be contested. If a passage could be opened through Jinniu and a garrison commander established within, occupying this central position would provide the strategic advantage needed for larger undertakings and eradicate the root of disaster forever. Yet no such proposal has been advanced since antiquity, and the circumstances cannot be discussed lightly. Thus the best course is resolutely to send troops bearing Heaven’s punishment into the territory where these dogs and swine run rampant, following Du Qi’s capture and defeat of the various Man peoples and Zhao Xie’s suppression of the Three Dong, thereby creating a shield and rampart for our southern region. As for those who submit to our civilizing influence, it would also be acceptable to follow Han Bi’s tireless efforts to comfort and attract them, and have them pay taxes. How could we be bound to a single approach?
Lianzhou lies in a remote location near Jiaozhi, precisely where Ma, General Who Calms the Waves, erected bronze pillars to mark the boundary. In recent years, the Xishan bandit leaders have plundered at will. Although they have now been exterminated, displaying the dynasty’s might, their remaining followers have yet to surrender their heads. Your discerning question proposes cutting through the mountains and clearing roads to annihilate them. This is indeed right. I would say that the Yao bandits themselves cannot cause serious trouble; the danger lies with the Lang bandits [?], with whom lawless and unruly people of this locality maintain contact. Some mountain fastnesses need not be traversed, but strategic positions must be held…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
若得屯衛星羅以把截要路則先人有制
人之心而永安黎庶顧于今無可爲計而
事勢未可妄論也則莫若於魚鹽貨市之
際而嚴禁交通之人如冷應徵之擒治峒
獠林槩之選蠻籍兵以壯吾北門之鎖鑰
其服吾羈縻者若倉振之深入賊境示諭
禍福亦可也而豈可執一見哉海賊之雙
桅出没明間曰漳民糶穀麥之害是也而
議者以爲有巡捕交通之弊蓋謂軍衞貪
===
鄙而受彼漳人之賄賂以縱出匣也頃者
雙桅大船
明詔所不容已盡毀矣豈能保無不測之虞耶
所以召之必有土人爲之窩隱以分贓而
使之然也莫若督軍兵之巡瞭戢官吏之
奸貪如蔡謨之戍八所以備季龍李寳之
備火箭以拒逆亮亦可矣至於葉義問之
請立寨主方信孺之先員賊舟亦一方經
畧之策豈可棄哉番舶之連年往來明間
punctuated:
若得屯衛星羅，以把截要路，則先人有制人之心，而永安黎庶。顧于今無可爲計，而事勢未可妄論也。則莫若於魚鹽貨市之際，而嚴禁交通之人。如冷應徵之擒治峒獠、林槩之選蠻籍兵，以壯吾北門之鎖鑰；其服吾羈縻者，若倉振之深入賊境，示諭禍福，亦可也。而豈可執一見哉？
海賊之雙桅出没，明間曰漳民糶穀麥之害，是也。而議者以爲有巡捕交通之弊，蓋謂軍衞貪鄙，而受彼漳人之賄賂，以縱出匣也。頃者，雙桅大船，明詔所不容，已盡毀矣。豈能保無不測之虞耶？所以召之，必有土人爲之窩隱，以分贓而使之然也。莫若督軍兵之巡瞭，戢官吏之奸貪。如蔡謨之戍八所以備季龍、李寳之備火箭以拒逆亮，亦可矣。至於葉義問之請立寨主、方信孺之先員賊舟，亦一方經畧之策，豈可棄哉？
番舶之連年往來，明間
translation_en:
If military colonies and guards could be arrayed like stars to block the strategic routes, we could seize the initiative and bring others under control, securing lasting peace for the common people. Yet at present there is no practicable plan, and one must not discuss the circumstances rashly. Nothing would therefore be better than strictly prohibiting those who communicate with the rebels from doing so when fish, salt, and other goods are traded. We might follow Leng Yingzheng in capturing and punishing the indigenous people of the mountain settlements, or Lin Gai in selecting soldiers from the indigenous registers, thereby strengthening the defenses that secure our northern gateway. For those who accept our loose administrative control, we might also follow Cang Zhen [?], who penetrated deep into rebel territory and explained the calamities or blessings that awaited them. How could we insist upon a single approach?
As for the appearance and disappearance of the pirates’ two-masted ships, your illuminating question [?] identifies the harm caused by the people of Zhang selling grain and wheat; this is correct. Those discussing the matter, however, point to collusion by the patrol forces. They mean that the military guards are corrupt and accept bribes from those people of Zhang, allowing them to leave the enclosure [?]. Recently, the large two-masted ships, forbidden by an explicit imperial edict, have all been destroyed. But can we guarantee that no unforeseen danger remains? What draws the pirates here must be local people who shelter and conceal them in return for a share of the plunder. Nothing would be better than supervising the troops’ patrols and lookouts and curbing the dishonesty and greed of officials and clerks. We might follow Cai Mo, who garrisoned eight places to guard against Jilong, or Li Bao, who prepared fire arrows to resist the rebel Liang. As for Ye Yiwen’s request to appoint stockade commanders and Fang Xinru’s advance action concerning the rebels’ ships [?], these too were strategies for managing a region’s defenses. How could they be discarded?
As for foreign ships coming and going year after year, your illuminating question [?]…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
曰奇貨資軍餉之利是也而議者以為有
將來開釁之憂蓋恐往來頻數而覘我
中國之虛實以啓觸藩也比者交通番夷
恩詔所不赦若少警矣豈能保無意外之患耶
而所以致之則以番舶有商人為之鄉導
以圖利而使之然也莫若盛軍容以防閑
按舊法以抽稅如元佑之盡報物數而勿
疎隆興之納稅寬期以相愛亦可矣若夫
胡則之粥水貸錢馬亮之遣使招徠特一
===
時權宜之計豈可法哉今之屯政專委憲
臣以督理之每年如漕法為參究之典誠
亦嚴矣而官軍之侵欺不已明問曰武弁
恃世襲而敢於為惡是也愚則曰下愚之
性見利則乾沒矣豈獨武弁為然哉昔陳
阿木之在欽州勤政務開屯田其與仲淹
屯陝州之法吾不知其相合與否也但今
之田非昔之田矣比年管屯僉事林希元
亦將屯田事宜奏
punctuated:
曰：「奇貨資軍餉之利。」是也。而議者以為有將來開釁之憂，蓋恐往來頻數，而覘我中國之虛實，以啓觸藩也。比者交通番夷，恩詔所不赦，若少警矣，豈能保無意外之患耶？而所以致之，則以番舶有商人為之鄉導，以圖利而使之然也。莫若盛軍容以防閑，按舊法以抽稅，如元佑之盡報物數而勿疎，隆興之納稅寬期以相愛，亦可矣。若夫胡則之粥水貸錢，馬亮之遣使招徠，特一時權宜之計，豈可法哉？

今之屯政，專委憲臣以督理之，每年如漕法為參究之典，誠亦嚴矣。而官軍之侵欺不已。明問曰：「武弁恃世襲而敢於為惡。」是也。愚則曰：「下愚之性，見利則乾沒矣，豈獨武弁為然哉？」昔陳阿木之在欽州，勤政務，開屯田，其與仲淹屯陝州之法，吾不知其相合與否也。但今之田非昔之田矣。比年管屯僉事林希元亦將屯田事宜奏
translation_en:
…says: “There is the benefit of using exotic goods to help fund military provisions.” This is true. Yet those discussing the matter see a danger of provoking future hostilities: they fear that frequent voyages will enable foreigners to spy out the strengths and weaknesses of our Central Kingdom and embolden them to challenge our defenses. Recently, dealings with foreign peoples were excluded from pardon under the imperial proclamation of grace. This seems to have provided some warning, but can we guarantee that no unforeseen trouble will arise? What brings them here is that merchants serve as guides for foreign ships in pursuit of profit. It would be best to maintain an imposing military presence to guard against them and levy duties according to established regulations. We might follow the practice of the Yuanyou reign, requiring full declarations of the quantities of goods without laxity, or that of the Longxing reign, allowing generous deadlines for paying duties as a mark of mutual goodwill. As for Hu Ze’s selling water [?] and lending money, or Ma Liang’s dispatching envoys to attract traders, these were merely expedients for particular circumstances. How could they serve as enduring models?

The administration of military agricultural colonies is now entrusted specifically to censorial officials for supervision. Each year, procedures for impeachment and investigation are applied as under the grain-transport regulations. These arrangements are indeed stringent. Yet misappropriation and fraud by officers and soldiers persist. Your discerning question states: “Military officers rely on their hereditary status and therefore dare to do evil.” This is true. I would nevertheless say: “It is the nature of the most benighted to pocket whatever profit they see. Surely military officers are not alone in this?” Formerly, when Chen Amu was in Qinzhou, he diligently attended to government affairs and opened military agricultural colonies. I do not know whether his methods accorded with those used by Zhongyan in establishing colonies in Shanzhou. But today’s fields are not those of former times. In recent years, Lin Xiyuan, the Surveillance Commissioner responsible for military agricultural colonies, also submitted to the throne matters concerning these colonies…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
涯蓋酌今之宜而爲之策也以是潤澤而審處
之豈不臧乎今之軍政分委藩臬以督清
之各府又各有官以嚴清查之法誠亦備
矣而軍士之逃亡不止明問曰軍士苦輪
班而敢於在逃是也愚則曰軍衞之官惟
利是剥削雖不輪班亦豈能安其生哉昔
馮拯在端州而括隱丁其與張說因衞士
逃匿而募彍騎之法吾不知其相同與否
也但今之軍非昔之軍矣比年軍政條例
===
及清戎官建白亦已頒行遵守蓋參時之
弊而爲之處也以是恪守而力行之豈不
善乎積穀所以爲備荒之地也昔李悝立
平糴之法耿壽昌制常平之規其意皆有
可觀者矣而明問謂際留永豐等倉皆不
堪於久積則是贓罰惟取價值貯庫而何
以備荒歉也且不開貪吏囊橐之門哉愚
謂廣東地氣卑濕固不可積於彌年猶幸
連歲豐登亦不可濫於賑濟莫若以紙米
punctuated:
涯，蓋酌今之宜而爲之策也。以是潤澤而審處之，豈不臧乎？今之軍政，分委藩臬以督清之，各府又各有官以嚴清查之法，誠亦備矣，而軍士之逃亡不止。明問曰：「軍士苦輪班而敢於在逃。」是也。愚則曰：軍衞之官，惟利是剥削，雖不輪班，亦豈能安其生哉？昔馮拯在端州而括隱丁，其與張說因衞士逃匿而募彍騎之法，吾不知其相同與否也。但今之軍，非昔之軍矣。比年軍政條例及清戎官建白，亦已頒行遵守，蓋參時之弊而爲之處也。以是恪守而力行之，豈不善乎？

積穀所以爲備荒之地也。昔李悝立平糴之法，耿壽昌制常平之規，其意皆有可觀者矣。而明問謂際留、永豐等倉皆不堪於久積，則是贓罰惟取價值貯庫，而何以備荒歉也？且不開貪吏囊橐之門哉？愚謂廣東地氣卑濕，固不可積於彌年；猶幸連歲豐登，亦不可濫於賑濟。莫若以紙米
translation_en:
…[?]. Presumably, these proposals were devised with due regard for what is appropriate today. If they were refined and carefully applied, would this not be good? Military administration is now entrusted in separate assignments to the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, which supervise the scrutiny of military registers. Each prefecture also has officials charged with enforcing strict procedures for investigation. These arrangements are indeed comprehensive, yet soldiers continue to desert. Your question states: “Soldiers suffer from rotational service and therefore dare to desert.” This is true. But in my humble view, the officers of the military guards exploit them solely for profit. Even without rotational service, how could the soldiers live in security? Formerly, when Feng Zheng was in Duanzhou, he sought out unregistered adult males. I do not know whether his method resembled that of Zhang Yue, who recruited cavalry known as guoqi when the guardsmen fled and went into hiding. But today’s troops are not those of the past. In recent years, military regulations and proposals submitted by officials charged with scrutinizing military personnel have already been promulgated for observance. These measures were presumably devised in light of contemporary abuses. If they were faithfully observed and vigorously implemented, would this not be good?

Storing grain provides the means to prepare for famine. In the past, Li Kui established a system of equitable grain purchases, and Geng Shouchang instituted the ever-normal granary system. The intentions behind both deserve consideration. Yet your question says that the Jiliu [?], Yongfeng, and other granaries are all unsuitable for prolonged storage. If confiscations and fines are therefore collected only in their monetary equivalent and deposited in treasuries, how can provision be made for famine and poor harvests? Moreover, would this not open the way for corrupt officials to fill their own purses? In my humble view, Guangdong’s terrain is low-lying and its climate damp, so grain certainly cannot be stored for years on end. Yet, fortunately, there have been successive abundant harvests, and relief distributions should not be made indiscriminately either. It would be best to use the “paper rice” [?] …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
罪穀每倉爲官軍俸粮之用而小民秋粮
夏税毎年爲減價折色之徵則軍民兩便
而適其宜矣與平糴常平何異哉均徭本
以供役也司馬公則主差役王介甫則主
於助役其言皆有所據者矣而明問謂弓
兵水夫等役皆不樂於親當則是徭役惟
取價値雇募而何以惠貧難也其不中積
年包攬之欲哉愚謂徭役之願於納價以
官吏得逞貪殘之由而官吏之遂於貪謀
===
亦由徭戸不願赴訴之故莫若以廣詔之
願納價者聽其貯官而不使之自募以雷
廉之願親當者聽其應役而不強其必同
則貧富兩便而得其所矣與差役助役何
異哉抑凡愚之所言者法也而所以爲之
要在由前所言剛斷之四事而實責之在
人也夫黎峒徭獞之出沒其責在兵備海
賊番舶之往來其責在海道屯政之脩廢
其責在管屯之僉憲軍伍之虛實其責在
punctuated: 罪穀每倉爲官軍俸粮之用，而小民秋粮夏税毎年爲減價折色之徵，則軍民兩便而適其宜矣，與平糴常平何異哉？均徭本以供役也。司馬公則主差役，王介甫則主於助役，其言皆有所據者矣。而明問謂弓兵水夫等役皆不樂於親當，則是徭役惟取價値雇募，而何以惠貧難也？其不中積年包攬之欲哉？愚謂徭役之願於納價，以官吏得逞貪殘之由，而官吏之遂於貪謀，亦由徭戸不願赴訴之故。莫若以廣詔之願納價者，聽其貯官，而不使之自募；以雷廉之願親當者，聽其應役，而不強其必同，則貧富兩便而得其所矣，與差役助役何異哉？抑凡愚之所言者，法也，而所以爲之，要在由前所言剛斷之四事，而實責之在人也。夫黎峒徭獞之出沒，其責在兵備；海賊番舶之往來，其責在海道；屯政之脩廢，其責在管屯之僉憲；軍伍之虛實，其責在
translation_en:
…use the grain collected as penalties in each granary to provide the pay and rations of military officers and soldiers, while each year collecting the common people's autumn grain levy and summer tax in commuted payments at reduced rates. This would benefit both soldiers and civilians and suit their circumstances. How would it differ from the equitable grain-purchasing and ever-normal granary systems?

The equitable service levy was originally intended to supply labor services. Lord Sima advocated service by direct assignment, while Wang Jiefu advocated contributions toward hiring substitutes; both had grounds for their arguments. Your discerning question states that people are unwilling to perform such services as those of bowmen and water-service laborers in person. But if labor obligations are met solely by collecting commutation payments and hiring substitutes, how can this help those suffering poverty and hardship? Would it not satisfy the desires of entrenched contractors who monopolize these services? In my humble view, the preference for paying money in lieu of service gives officials and clerks an opportunity to indulge their greed and oppression; their success in these greedy schemes also results from the unwillingness of households liable for service to lodge complaints. It would be better to allow those in Guang and Shao [?] who wish to pay money to deposit it with the authorities, rather than have them recruit substitutes themselves; and to allow those in Lei and Lian who wish to serve personally to fulfill their obligations, without forcing everyone to follow the same practice. This would benefit rich and poor alike and accommodate their circumstances. How would it differ from direct assignment and contributions toward hired service?

Yet all that I have humbly proposed consists of administrative measures. The key to carrying them out lies in the four matters requiring firmness and decisiveness discussed above, and in placing actual responsibility upon the appropriate people. Responsibility for the incursions of the Li mountain communities and the Yao and Zhuang peoples rests with the military defense intendant; responsibility for the movements of pirates and foreign ships rests with the maritime defense intendant; responsibility for the maintenance or neglect of military agricultural colony administration rests with the Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in charge of those colonies; responsibility for whether military ranks are actually filled or merely nominal rests with…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
清戎之藩臬量積穀之出入以便官民其
責在於粮儲均徭役之重輕以通民瘼其
責在於守令而所以使之為氷蘖而不為
溪壑為保障而不為繭絲為胸中數萬甲
兵而不為棘門兒戲則又在撫按公激揚
之論
廟堂决黜陟之權此地方大計肉食者之所
知也而豈藿食者所能曉其萬一哉狂瞽
之言未知是否惟執事與其進而教之
punctuated: 清戎之藩臬。量積穀之出入以便官民，其責在於粮儲；均徭役之重輕以通民瘼，其責在於守令。而所以使之為氷蘖而不為溪壑，為保障而不為繭絲，為胸中數萬甲兵而不為棘門兒戲，則又在撫按公激揚之論，廟堂决黜陟之權。此地方大計，肉食者之所知也，而豈藿食者所能曉其萬一哉？狂瞽之言，未知是否，惟執事與其進而教之。
translation_en: …the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners charged with reviewing the military rolls. Regulating the receipt and disbursement of stored grain for the benefit of officials and commoners is the responsibility of the officials administering grain reserves; equalizing the burdens of corvée service to relieve the people’s suffering is the responsibility of prefects and magistrates. Yet ensuring that these officials embody the incorruptibility symbolized by ice and bitter bark, rather than the insatiable greed of ravines; that they protect the people, rather than extract resources from them like silk drawn from cocoons; and that they possess the strategic mastery of men with tens of thousands of armored troops in their minds, rather than make military affairs child’s play as at Jimen—this further depends upon impartial judgments of censure and commendation by the grand coordinator and regional inspector, and upon the court’s exercise of its authority to decide dismissals and promotions. These great plans for governing the region are matters understood by those who eat meat—the officeholders. How could one who eats bean leaves—a commoner—understand even a ten-thousandth part of them? I do not know whether these rash and ignorant words are right or wrong. I ask only that you, honored examiners, approve my willingness to come forward and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
昭哉我
國家以人文化成天下歲三閱
而取士其周之大比而賓興
者乎試之以文豈徒曰酌其
章哉有道存焉其關於治運
者懋乎其隆也槩嘗仰觀於
===
天俯察於地見其確然而示
人以易隤然而示人以簡迺
作而嘆曰休哉其文乎天之
精也地之英也人之粹也三
才之道一而莫之或遷也于
其易也唯其健也于其簡也
唯其順也有神焉以握其機
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

昭哉！我國家以人文化成天下，歲三閱而取士，其周之大比而賓興者乎？試之以文，豈徒曰酌其章哉？有道存焉，其關於治運者，懋乎其隆也。槩嘗仰觀於天，俯察於地，見其確然而示人以易，隤然而示人以簡，迺作而嘆曰：「休哉，其文乎！天之精也，地之英也，人之粹也。三才之道，一而莫之或遷也。于其易也，唯其健也；于其簡也，唯其順也。有神焉，以握其機」
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

How illustrious! Our dynasty transforms and perfects all under Heaven through human culture, selecting men for service once every three years. Is this not like the great triennial assessment of the Zhou, when worthy men were honored as guests and recommended for office? In testing them through writing, is the purpose merely to assess their literary embellishments? The Way resides therein; its bearing upon the fortunes of government is profound indeed.

Gai once looked upward to contemplate Heaven and downward to examine Earth, observing how Heaven, firm and steadfast, shows men ease, and Earth, yielding, shows men simplicity. Then he rose and exclaimed: “How splendid is their patterned expression! It is the essence of Heaven, the finest of Earth, and the purest of humanity. The Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—is one, and nothing can alter it. Heaven’s ease rests upon its vigor; Earth’s simplicity rests upon its compliance. There is a spiritual efficacy that holds the key to their workings …”

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雖天地而弗得與其能也而
况於人乎哉夫塞其體也帥
其性也其心固天地之心也
由是而發之言措之業皆夫
人之文也文不足以觀士乎
哉仰惟我
聖上以天縱之資而紹帝王之學
===
兢兢焉存其心純其理於敬
一焉緝之則精一執中之傳
允乎其相承而建極以風乎
士心者固自有本也而文也
者所以徵乎其心也士生於
時得非其慶幸哉槩始應束
廣聘事若隱有懼者意其地
punctuated:
雖天地而弗得與其能也，而况於人乎哉！夫塞其體也，帥其性也，其心固天地之心也。由是而發之言，措之業，皆夫人之文也。文不足以觀士乎哉！
仰惟我聖上以天縱之資而紹帝王之學，兢兢焉存其心，純其理，於敬一焉緝之，則精一執中之傳，允乎其相承，而建極以風乎士心者，固自有本也。而文也者，所以徵乎其心也。士生於時，得非其慶幸哉！槩始應束廣聘事，若隱有懼者，意其地
translation_en:
…Even Heaven and Earth cannot match its capacity, much less human beings! What fills a person's embodied being and governs his nature is his mind, which is indeed the mind of Heaven and Earth. What proceeds from this into words and is put into practice in undertakings is all that person's cultural expression. Is such expression not sufficient for judging a scholar?
Reverently I consider how our sagely sovereign, endowed by Heaven, carries forward the learning of emperors and kings. With vigilant care he preserves his mind and keeps its principles pure, continually cultivating them through reverent unity. Thus the transmitted teaching of refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the Mean is truly carried on. His establishment of the supreme standard to influence scholars' minds assuredly has its foundation in this. Writing is the means by which their minds may be assessed. Is it not a blessing and good fortune for scholars to live in this age? When I, Gai, first accepted the invitation to serve in eastern Guangdong [?], I felt a lingering apprehension, thinking that its territory…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
涉遐方士之心或未盡淑而
文弗之辨邪徐而校之則震
而弗靡其氣達也美而弗詭
其才華也雅而有倫其制典
也夫氣德之充也充則弗餒
而於理也直才德之焜也華
則弗涸而於理也澤制德之
===
準也典則弗雜而於理也純
三者集而心庶乎其亮矣槩
敬竦而嘆曰於猗哉
聖化之入人深也雖嶺海之遠猶
且翕焉而丕變則
中興之運於茲乎昭矣二三子
沐盛而起將奚以示我周行
punctuated: 涉遐方，士之心或未盡淑，而文弗之辨邪？徐而校之，則震而弗靡，其氣達也；美而弗詭，其才華也；雅而有倫，其制典也。夫氣，德之充也，充則弗餒，而於理也直；才，德之焜也，華則弗涸，而於理也澤；制，德之準也，典則弗雜，而於理也純。三者集，而心庶乎其亮矣。槩敬竦而嘆曰：「於猗哉！聖化之入人深也！雖嶺海之遠，猶且翕焉而丕變，則中興之運於茲乎昭矣。二三子沐盛而起，將奚以示我周行
translation_en:
…lay in a distant region, where the scholars’ hearts might not yet be wholly good, and their writing might fail to reveal this? Yet, on gradually examining their work, I found it vigorous without being extravagant, showing the free expression of their vital force; beautiful without being bizarre, showing the brilliance of their talent; and refined and orderly, showing the classical correctness of their form. Vital force is virtue in its fullness: when full, it does not falter and is upright in relation to principle. Talent is virtue’s radiance: when brilliant, it does not run dry and gives lustre to principle. Form is virtue’s standard: when classically correct, it is free of confusion and pure in relation to principle. When these three come together, the heart may approach true clarity.
Gai, stirred with reverence, exclaimed: “Ah, how deeply the sage sovereign’s transforming influence enters people’s hearts! Even as far away as Linghai, people respond in concord and undergo a great transformation. Here, then, the fortunes of dynastic resurgence are made manifest. You gentlemen, who have risen while bathing in this flourishing age, how will you show me the great Way…”

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以觀
國之光哉夫言之非艱行惟艱
行之非艱心唯艱薦書祗成
必實錄其文者所以識其心
而要其行於終也矧邇者
聖諭太學務在惇本尚實勿徒專
事詞章使大道明而彝倫叙
===
用贊我
國家文明之化則拳拳致望於
天下士者至重至切二三子
得無念哉亦惟曰貞其心而
已矣蓋蘊諸心者為德性則
宣諸言者為德聲徵諸行者
為德業經而緯之造化在我
punctuated: 以觀國之光哉？夫言之非艱，行惟艱；行之非艱，心唯艱。薦書祗成，必實錄其文者，所以識其心，而要其行於終也。矧邇者聖諭太學，務在惇本尚實，勿徒專事詞章，使大道明而彝倫叙，用贊我國家文明之化，則拳拳致望於天下士者，至重至切。二三子得無念哉？亦惟曰貞其心而已矣。蓋蘊諸心者為德性，則宣諸言者為德聲，徵諸行者為德業。經而緯之，造化在我
translation_en: …so as to behold the glory of the state? Speaking is not difficult; acting is difficult. Acting is not difficult; setting the heart right is difficult. As the recommendation document is reverently completed, we must faithfully record their writings, so that we may discern their hearts and hold them to their conduct to the very end. Moreover, the recent imperial admonition to the Imperial University urged the strengthening of fundamentals and the valuing of substance, rather than exclusive devotion to literary composition, so that the Great Way might be made manifest and the enduring human relationships set in order, thereby furthering our state’s civilizing transformation. The earnest expectations thus placed upon the scholars of the realm are most weighty and pressing. Can you gentlemen fail to take heed? It comes down simply to making your hearts upright. What is stored within the heart constitutes moral nature; what is expressed in words constitutes the voice of virtue; what is borne out in conduct constitutes the accomplishments of virtue. Weaving these together as warp and weft, the power of transformation lies within ourselves…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
必如是而后無愧於文也否
則而堅而辨率歸諸僞君子
耻之二三子得無念哉庶或
勉之固諸大夫主司願也遂
拜書于錄
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學敎
諭張槩謹序
punctuated:
必如是而后無愧於文也。否則，而堅而辨，率歸諸僞，君子耻之。二三子得無念哉？庶或勉之，固諸大夫主司願也。遂拜書于錄。
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學敎諭張槩謹序。
translation_en:
…Only in this way can one be free from shame in one’s writing. Otherwise, firmness and eloquence [?] alike amount to falsity, which the gentleman regards as shameful. Can you, gentlemen, fail to give this thought? That you might strive toward this is indeed the wish of the officials presiding over the examination. I therefore respectfully set these words down in the record.
Preface respectfully written by Zhang Gai, Instructor in the Confucian School of Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

text:
第壹場
四書
夫仁者己欲立而立人己欲達而達人能
近取譬可謂仁之方也已
誠者自成也而道自道也
存其心養其性所以事天也
易
觀乎天文以察時變觀乎人文以化成天
下
===
當位以節中正以通
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
精義入神以致用也
書
慎厥身脩思永惇叙九族庶明勵翼邇可
遠在兹禹拜昌言曰俞
惟天聰明惟聖時憲
凡厥庶民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

夫仁者，己欲立而立人，己欲達而達人。能近取譬，可謂仁之方也已。

誠者，自成也；而道，自道也。

存其心，養其性，所以事天也。

易

觀乎天文，以察時變；觀乎人文，以化成天下。

當位以節，中正以通。

夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

精義入神，以致用也。

書

慎厥身，脩思永，惇叙九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠在兹。禹拜昌言曰：「俞。」

惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。

凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The benevolent person, wishing to establish himself, establishes others; wishing to attain success himself, enables others to succeed. To draw an analogy from what is close at hand may be called the method of benevolence.

Sincerity is the means by which one completes oneself; the Way is the means by which one guides oneself.

Preserving one's heart and nurturing one's nature are the means by which one serves Heaven.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern changes in the seasons; observe human patterns to transform and perfect all under Heaven.

Occupying the proper position, one exercises restraint; through centrality and correctness, one achieves free passage.

The Changes is the means by which the sages exalt their virtue and extend their achievements. Understanding is lofty; ritual propriety is humble. The lofty emulates Heaven; the humble models itself on Earth.

Refining one's understanding of what is right until one penetrates the numinous is the means of bringing it into practical use.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

Be watchful over your conduct; in cultivating yourself, think of the long term. Generously maintain the proper order among the nine degrees of kinship, and let the many enlightened men strive to assist you. What begins nearby can extend far: herein lies the means. Yu bowed in acknowledgment of these excellent words and said, “Yes.”

Heaven hears and sees clearly; the sage takes this as his model.

As for all the common people, they follow and practice the teachings promulgated concerning the supreme standard, thereby drawing near to the Son of Heaven.

text:
之砥柱則鄭以挫困之邦而當帶甲百萬之雄
河決魚爛之秋也可懼也哉幸僑也幾審而慮
熟氣昌而備周爰築在外之館既有以陰折其
奸而不愛豐氏之祧又有以飽塞其欲卒之楚
人垂櫜而入會虢以還焉夫南方之國莫强於
楚而能拒之以弭患是楚之勢不足畏而吾人
之禮有足憑者吁僑之在鄭展哉邦家之基乎
夫以子產在鄭而强國終莫能屈其賢可知矣
宜春秋備書而樂道之也歟抑鄭一也鄭忽以
===
無故而失守子產以多難而興邦何也大要在
志不在力而亦由簡公推轂之功也不然魯之
有叔孫豹猶鄭之有子產也何鄭國以振而昭
不免其身哉以是知人才係國之重輕而人君
以用賢爲急
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
戚〔襄公五年〕
林時雨
punctuated:
之砥柱，則鄭以挫困之邦而當帶甲百萬之雄，河決魚爛之秋也，可懼也哉！幸僑也幾審而慮熟，氣昌而備周，爰築在外之館，既有以陰折其奸；而不愛豐氏之祧，又有以飽塞其欲。卒之楚人垂櫜而入，會虢以還焉。夫南方之國莫强於楚，而能拒之以弭患，是楚之勢不足畏，而吾人之禮有足憑者。吁！僑之在鄭，展哉邦家之基乎！夫以子產在鄭，而强國終莫能屈，其賢可知矣。宜春秋備書而樂道之也歟！抑鄭一也，鄭忽以無故而失守，子產以多難而興邦，何也？大要在志不在力，而亦由簡公推轂之功也。不然，魯之有叔孫豹，猶鄭之有子產也，何鄭國以振，而昭不免其身哉？以是知人才係國之重輕，而人君以用賢爲急。

公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚。〔襄公五年〕
林時雨
translation_en:
…a mainstay. Zheng, a battered and beleaguered state, faced a mighty power with a million armored soldiers: this was a moment when the river might burst its banks and everything rot like fish. How fearful it was! Fortunately, Qiao discerned the slightest signs and deliberated thoroughly; his spirit was vigorous and his preparations comprehensive. He therefore built guest quarters outside the city, thereby covertly thwarting their treachery; and by not begrudging the ancestral shrine of the Feng lineage, he also found a means of fully satisfying their desires. In the end, the men of Chu entered with their bow cases hanging down, then attended the meeting at Guo and returned home. Among the southern states, none was stronger than Chu; yet Zheng could resist it and avert disaster. Thus Chu’s power was insufficient to inspire fear, while our observance of ritual propriety provided something on which we could rely. Ah! Qiao in Zheng was truly a foundation of the state! With Zichan in Zheng, the powerful states could never make it submit: from this his worth is evident. Surely it was fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded his deeds fully and delighted in recounting them!

Yet it was the same Zheng: Hu of Zheng lost his hold upon it when there was no crisis, whereas Zichan revived the state amid many troubles. Why? What mattered chiefly was resolve, not strength; but this also owed something to Duke Jian’s support and advancement of him. Otherwise, Lu’s possession of Shusun Bao was like Zheng’s possession of Zichan: why did Zheng revive, while Duke Zhao could not himself escape disaster? From this we know that talented men determine a state’s standing, and that a ruler must make employing the worthy his urgent priority.

The duke met at Qi with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, and representatives of Wu and Zeng. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xiang〕
Lin Shiyu

李兆龍
同考試官教諭余批近表多辭浮於理文浮於事此
篇獨典則詳明且默寓忠愛之意其積學以待聘者與
同考試官教諭曾批斟酌六典參以時宜深知所以
稽古建官者可嘉可嘉
考試官教諭張批得體
考試官教授錢批典麗
元豐五年某月日具官臣鞏比蒙
===
聖恩頒賜六典者臣誠惶誠恐稽首稽首上言
伏以殷監夏時忠質雖稱異尚周因商禮
損益實在兼資適申
晉錫之隆丕示
華文之炳榮踰五服捧亟三薰竊惟龍雲鳥火
聖人崇制以上賢春夏秋冬明王貽謀於
勤事叙厥揆岳牧伯服休服采之聿彰纖
及山澤川林掌葛掌茶之亦備由卯金以
降多蹈襲乎秦儀至李唐之興欲變更乎
punctuated:
擬宋曾鞏謝賜唐六典表，元豐五年。
李兆龍。
同考試官教諭余批：近表多辭浮於理，文浮於事。此篇獨典則詳明，且默寓忠愛之意，其積學以待聘者與！
同考試官教諭曾批：斟酌六典，參以時宜，深知所以稽古建官者，可嘉可嘉！
考試官教諭張批：得體。
考試官教授錢批：典麗。
元豐五年某月日，具官臣鞏比蒙聖恩頒賜六典者，臣誠惶誠恐，稽首稽首，上言：
伏以殷監夏時，忠質雖稱異尚；周因商禮，損益實在兼資。適申晉錫之隆，丕示華文之炳。榮踰五服，捧亟三薰。竊惟龍雲鳥火，聖人崇制以上賢；春夏秋冬，明王貽謀於勤事。叙厥揆岳牧伯，服休服采之聿彰；纖及山澤川林，掌葛掌茶之亦備。由卯金以降，多蹈襲乎秦儀；至李唐之興，欲變更乎
translation_en:
A memorial composed in the person of Zeng Gong of the Song, thanking the emperor for bestowing the Six Statutes of the Tang; set in the fifth year of Yuanfeng (1082).
By Li Zhaolong.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: Recent memorials often have language that exceeds their reasoning and ornament that exceeds their substance. This piece alone is classically disciplined, detailed, and clear; it also quietly conveys loyalty and devotion. Surely its author is one who has accumulated learning while awaiting appointment!
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: He weighs the Six Statutes against the needs of the times and deeply understands how antiquity is consulted in establishing offices. Most commendable, most commendable!
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Appropriate to the form.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: Classical and elegant.
On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of Yuanfeng, your servant Gong, holding the requisite official title, having recently received through Your Majesty’s sacred grace a bestowed copy of the Six Statutes, in utmost awe and trepidation bows his head to the ground twice and submits this memorial:
I humbly reflect that Yin looked to the age of Xia as its model: although loyalty and simplicity were said to be their different preferences, Zhou likewise followed Shang ritual, and its omissions and additions in fact drew upon both traditions. Now Your Majesty has extended the munificence of this gracious bestowal, splendidly displaying the brilliance of this magnificent text. The honor surpasses that of the robes of the five ranks; to receive it reverently, I hasten to perfume myself three times.
I reflect that, with offices named after dragons, clouds, birds, and fire, the sages exalted institutions to honor the worthy; with offices corresponding to spring, summer, autumn, and winter, enlightened kings bequeathed plans for diligent service. They ordered the offices of chief minister, regional overseers, governors, and chiefs, making manifest their meritorious service and discharge of duties. Their provisions extended even to the details of mountains, marshes, rivers, and forests, including officials charged with kudzu and with tea [?]. From the Liu house of Han onward, administrations largely followed Qin precedents; when the Li house of Tang arose, it sought to reform …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
隋制爰集九齡之輩遂成六典之書分職
授功綜兵農而置吏辨方經野定租稅以
康民總機務於尚書蓋取端揆之義屬庶
僚於六部猶存倡率之規黜鸞臺鳳閣之
侈稱名正而言順芟車載斗量之蠹治綱
舉以目張規模皆倣乎成周制度似超乎
前代第大曹與九寺並設若十手挈乎一
壺四監與六卿相持猶二垂加乎四益金
倉弗司錢穀職近於虛都水不管山川名
===
幾於曠繄麟趾之意或缺豈燕翼之貽靡
臧不謂遺編之尚存偶厪
乙夜之獨覽刋豕魚於儒碩鏤為
中禁之珍出珠玉於
上方頒及外庭之彦茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
睿資入聖
雄斷同神襲
嘉運於重熙無廢舊章之率撫
punctuated:
隋制，爰集九齡之輩，遂成《六典》之書。分職授功，綜兵農而置吏；辨方經野，定租稅以康民。總機務於尚書，蓋取端揆之義；屬庶僚於六部，猶存倡率之規。黜鸞臺鳳閣之侈稱，名正而言順；芟車載斗量之蠹，治綱舉以目張。規模皆倣乎成周，制度似超乎前代。第大曹與九寺並設，若十手挈乎一壺；四監與六卿相持，猶二垂加乎四益。金倉弗司錢穀，職近於虛；都水不管山川，名幾於曠。繄麟趾之意或缺，豈燕翼之貽靡臧？不謂遺編之尚存，偶厪乙夜之獨覽。刋豕魚於儒碩，鏤為中禁之珍；出珠玉於上方，頒及外庭之彦。
茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，睿資入聖，雄斷同神，襲嘉運於重熙，無廢舊章之率撫
translation_en:
…the institutions of the Sui. Thereupon men such as Zhang Jiuling were assembled, and the book Six Statutes (Liudian) was completed. It apportioned offices and assigned duties, appointing officials to coordinate military and agricultural affairs; it distinguished regions and laid out the countryside, fixing rents and taxes to secure the people’s well-being. It concentrated essential affairs in the Department of State Affairs, adopting the principle of leadership by a chief minister; it placed the various officials under the Six Ministries, preserving the system of direction from above. It abolished such extravagant designations as “Phoenix Terrace” and “Phoenix Pavilion,” so that names were correct and language accorded with them; it removed the abuses of officials so numerous they could be carted by the load and measured by the bushel, so that, once the governing cord was lifted, the meshes of administration opened in order. Its overall design followed the established Zhou order, and its institutions seemed to surpass those of earlier dynasties. Yet the great bureaus [?] were established alongside the Nine Courts, like ten hands lifting a single pot; the Four Directorates and the Six Ministers checked one another, like two Chuis added to four Yis [the ancient exemplary officials; the comparison is uncertain]. The Treasury and Granaries sections did not administer money and grain, leaving their duties nearly empty; the Directorate of Waterways did not manage mountains and rivers, leaving its title almost without substance. Perhaps the intent celebrated in “The Unicorn’s Hoofs” was imperfectly realized; could the provision made for posterity really have been unsound?
Unexpectedly, this surviving work remained extant and happened to receive Your Majesty’s solitary attention during the second watch of the night. Through eminent scholars, its textual errors—the confusions of “pig” and “fish”—were corrected, and it was engraved for printing as a treasure of the inner palace. These pearls and jade were brought forth from the imperial precincts and distributed to the worthy men of the outer court.
This, we humbly acknowledge, is because we have encountered 〇〇〇〇, whose sagacious gifts attain sagehood and whose mighty decisiveness equals that of the spirits, who has inherited an auspicious destiny amid successive flourishing reigns and has neglected none of the observance and maintenance of the ancient statutes…

嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書贊易脩春秋而不及禮樂之制以為不
可斯須去身而莫急焉者其要本之一誠
而已矣至董仲舒劉向歸之庠序是或一
道也而豈知天子躬行以為之倡而出於
一哉及考司馬遷之律書其始不言律而
言兵之偃及謂漢文帝偃兵息民而天地
之氣始正此制作之本也永嘉陳氏謂律
===
呂之法起於黃帝而律呂之說定於太史
公是也此其說與治出於一之言何異哉
以後世之禮樂者言之西漢之禮制於叔
通而雜秦儀此兩生之所以不至也東漢
之禮制於曹褒而取讖緯在當時張酺已
有破亂聖術之奏矣唐有顯慶禮則許敬
宗所附會而削國恤一篇以致後來山陵
之論無定見敬宗之罪大矣開元禮則徐
堅輩所撰而蕭嵩輩足成之大率不脫顯
punctuated:
書，贊易，脩春秋，而不及禮樂之制，以為不可斯須去身而莫急焉者，其要本之一誠而已矣。至董仲舒、劉向歸之庠序，是或一道也，而豈知天子躬行以為之倡，而出於一哉？及考司馬遷之律書，其始不言律而言兵之偃，及謂漢文帝偃兵息民而天地之氣始正，此制作之本也。永嘉陳氏謂律呂之法起於黃帝，而律呂之說定於太史公，是也。此其說與治出於一之言何異哉？
以後世之禮樂者言之，西漢之禮制於叔通而雜秦儀，此兩生之所以不至也。東漢之禮制於曹褒而取讖緯，在當時張酺已有破亂聖術之奏矣。唐有顯慶禮，則許敬宗所附會，而削國恤一篇，以致後來山陵之論無定見，敬宗之罪大矣。開元禮則徐堅輩所撰，而蕭嵩輩足成之，大率不脫顯
translation_en:
…Documents, elucidated the Changes, and edited the Spring and Autumn Annals, yet did not address the institutions of ritual and music. He regarded these as things from which one could not depart even for an instant, and as matters of the greatest urgency; their essential basis lay simply in wholehearted sincerity. As for Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang, they assigned these matters to the schools. This was perhaps one approach, but how could they understand that the Son of Heaven must personally practise them to set an example, and that they issue from a single source? Examining Sima Qian’s Treatise on the Pitch Pipes, we find that it begins not with the pitch pipes but with the cessation of warfare. It further states that only when Emperor Wen of Han ceased warfare and gave the people respite did the vital forces of Heaven and Earth become properly ordered. This is the foundation for establishing institutions. Master Chen of Yongjia said that the methods of the pitch pipes originated with the Yellow Emperor, while their explanation was definitively established by the Grand Astrologer, Sima Qian. This is correct. How does this explanation differ from the statement that government issues from a single source?
Speaking of ritual and music in later ages, the ritual institutions of the Western Han were established by Shu Tong [?], but incorporated Qin ceremonial practices. This was why the two scholars declined to come. The ritual institutions of the Eastern Han were established by Cao Bao, but drew upon prophetic texts and apocryphal interpretations of the classics. Already at the time, Zhang Pu submitted a memorial charging that this subverted and disrupted the teachings of the sages. Under the Tang there was the Xianqing Ritual Code, which Xu Jingzong constructed through strained interpretations. He deleted the chapter on mourning for the sovereign, with the result that later deliberations concerning imperial funerals and tombs lacked a settled position. Jingzong’s culpability was great indeed. The Kaiyuan Ritual Code was compiled by Xu Jian and others and completed by Xiao Song and others; on the whole, it did not break free of the Xian…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於京房以仲吕再生别名執始是徒知焦
氏卦氣之去四而爲六十而遂以三分損
益之數或棄或增其誤亦甚矣在唐則祖
孝孫製十二和自豫和以至承和是也顏
師古製七舞則長發以至光大是也然皆
襲梁武帝之舊而已在宋則和峴諸人之
辨皆無定論和峴用影表尺李照造新噐
阮逸與范鎮皆以徑三分累黍胡安定遷
林鍾以下以就黃鍾而司馬君實於筆談
===
通典皆不之考究比之范公又不及矣然
則數子所定之樂謂之漢唐宋之樂可也
其視周禮之樂孰高孰下哉至於王荆公
崇信周禮而卒以取敗人曰用周禮之效
也不知荆公之立青苗設條例是變仁義
爲聚斂皆不善用之過也非周禮使之然
也故甞合而論之後世之不如三代者豈
後世終不可治哉要之以禮樂爲虛名而
治出於二也歐子之論斷乎不可易矣至
punctuated: 於京房，以仲吕再生，别名執始，是徒知焦氏卦氣之去四而爲六十，而遂以三分損益之數或棄或增，其誤亦甚矣。在唐，則祖孝孫製十二和，自豫和以至承和是也；顏師古製七舞，則長發以至光大是也。然皆襲梁武帝之舊而已。在宋，則和峴諸人之辨皆無定論。和峴用影表尺，李照造新噐，阮逸與范鎮皆以徑三分累黍，胡安定遷林鍾以下以就黃鍾，而司馬君實於《筆談》《通典》皆不之考究，比之范公又不及矣。然則數子所定之樂，謂之漢唐宋之樂可也，其視《周禮》之樂，孰高孰下哉？至於王荆公崇信《周禮》而卒以取敗，人曰用《周禮》之效也。不知荆公之立青苗、設條例，是變仁義爲聚斂，皆不善用之過也，非《周禮》使之然也。故甞合而論之：後世之不如三代者，豈後世終不可治哉？要之，以禮樂爲虛名，而治出於二也。歐子之論，斷乎不可易矣。至
translation_en:
…in the case of Jing Fang, he generated a further pitch from Zhonglü and gave it the distinct name Zhishi. He merely knew that Master Jiao’s system of correlating hexagrams with seasonal qi excluded four hexagrams to leave sixty, and consequently either discarded or added to the numbers produced by the method of subtracting or adding a third. His error was indeed grave. In the Tang, Zu Xiaosun composed the Twelve Harmonies, from Y uhe to Chenghe; Yan Shigu composed the Seven Dances, from Changfa to Guangda. Yet all these merely followed the precedents of Emperor Wu of Liang. In the Song, the debates of He Xian and others reached no settled conclusion. He Xian used the gnomon foot-rule; Li Zhao made new instruments; Ruan Yi and Fan Zhen both used a diameter of three fen and accumulated millet grains to establish measurements [?]. Hu Anding shifted the pitches from Linzhong downward to bring them into conformity with Huangzhong. Sima Junshi, however, failed to investigate either Brush Talks or the Comprehensive Institutions, and in comparison with Master Fan fell still further short.

Thus, the music established by these men may properly be called the music of the Han, Tang, and Song. But compared with the music of the Rites of Zhou, which is higher and which lower? As for Wang Jinggong, he revered and trusted the Rites of Zhou but ultimately met with failure. People say that this was the result of applying the Rites of Zhou. They do not understand that Jinggong’s establishment of the Green Sprouts loans and his institution of the Regulations Office turned benevolence and righteousness into revenue extraction. These were all faults of improper application; the Rites of Zhou did not make him act this way.

I have therefore considered these matters together: if later ages have fallen short of the Three Dynasties, does that mean that later ages can never be well governed? The essential point is that ritual and music were treated as empty names, while governance issued from two sources. Master Ou’s judgment most certainly cannot be altered. As for…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於可繼周禮之缺者舍文公之家禮蔡元
定之律呂新書吾誰歸乎夫家禮畧浮文
敦本實其說多參用司馬氏程子高氏之
說若夫明大宗小宗之法乃其大義而其
本在於謹名分崇愛敬真可謂庶幾古人
脩身齊家之道者矣至於新書所載黃鍾
圍徑之數以長九寸圍九分取淮南小史
之說正其原也變律半聲之例以為黃鍾
至仲呂相生既窮遂變而上生黃鍾之宮
===
餘八寸而缺半通其變也五聲二變之則
角與徵羽與宮相去二律故角徵之間近
徵收一聲而比徵少下羽宮之間近宮收
一聲而少高於宮諧其聲也若聲氣之元
則政善民安而天下之心和然後氣飛灰
而聲中律故於此多截竹以擬黃鍾之聲
而以氣應者用之然後以秬黍之法而參
較焉非律生於黍也此其為書明白而淵
深縝密而通暢亦可謂善言樂者矣故以
punctuated:
於可繼周禮之缺者，舍文公之家禮、蔡元定之律呂新書，吾誰歸乎？夫家禮畧浮文，敦本實，其說多參用司馬氏、程子、高氏之說。若夫明大宗、小宗之法，乃其大義，而其本在於謹名分、崇愛敬，真可謂庶幾古人脩身齊家之道者矣。
至於新書所載黃鍾圍徑之數，以長九寸、圍九分，取淮南小史之說，正其原也。變律半聲之例，以為黃鍾至仲呂相生既窮，遂變而上生黃鍾之宮，餘八寸而缺半，通其變也。五聲二變之則，角與徵、羽與宮相去二律，故角徵之間近徵收一聲而比徵少下，羽宮之間近宮收一聲而少高於宮，諧其聲也。若聲氣之元，則政善民安而天下之心和，然後氣飛灰而聲中律。故於此多截竹以擬黃鍾之聲，而以氣應者用之，然後以秬黍之法而參較焉，非律生於黍也。此其為書，明白而淵深，縝密而通暢，亦可謂善言樂者矣。故以
translation_en:
…As for works that can supplement the deficiencies of the Rites of Zhou, to whom could I turn apart from the Family Rituals of Master Wengong and Cai Yuanding’s New Treatise on the Pitch Pipes (Lülü xinshu)? The Family Rituals dispenses with superficial elaboration and gives weight to fundamentals and substance. Its explanations frequently draw on those of Sima, Master Cheng, and Gao. Clarifying the rules governing the principal and collateral lineage branches is its central purport, while its foundation lies in carefully observing distinctions of status and giving precedence to affection and respect. Truly, it may be said to approach the ancients’ way of cultivating oneself and ordering one’s household.
As for the measurements of the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe recorded in the New Treatise, it adopts a length of nine cun and a circumference of nine fen, drawing on the account in the Huainan Minor History [?], thereby rectifying the basis of the system. Its rules for altered pitches and half-length tones hold that once the successive generation of pitches from Huangzhong to Zhonglü has run its course, a modification is made to generate upward the gong note of Huangzhong, leaving eight cun less a half [?]. This makes the transformations of the system workable. Under the rules for the five notes and the two altered notes, jue and zhi, and yu and gong, are each separated by two pitch intervals. Thus, between jue and zhi, an additional note is included close to zhi but slightly lower; between yu and gong, an additional note is included close to gong but slightly higher than gong. This brings the sounds into harmony.
As for the source of sound and vital breath, only when government is good, the people are at peace, and the hearts of all under Heaven are harmonious does the vital breath make the ashes fly and the sound accord with the pitch standards. Accordingly, many lengths of bamboo are cut to approximate the sound of Huangzhong, and those that respond to the vital breath are selected for use. Only afterward are they checked against the method using black millet grains: the pitch standards do not originate in millet. This book is lucid yet profound, meticulous yet coherent and fluent. Its author, too, may be said to have discoursed well on music. Therefore, by…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
可愛也然有不充則缺矣有不造則偏矣
有不運則滯矣是故自聖人以下邪正不
同路純駁不同色大小不同器清濁不同
流而文章亦與之俱嗚呼文章固學者之
末事也而於此可以觀心志焉可以考節
操焉可以驗智識焉可以占才能焉文其
可易言耶請因明問所及而陳之夫文章
唯孔子之六經至矣而何所昉乎煥於被
四表之堯而非堯也盡於畫八卦之包羲
===
而非羲也其始於於穆不已之天乎蓋本
爲一誠列爲四德散爲五行而聖人得之
以爲心於是乎清明純粹之實自然光輝
發越條理分明故達而在上則昌言嘉謨
足以定國是而以文章見於政窮而在下
則潜德隱行足以勵世俗而以文章筆之
書聖人何嘗有意於爲文哉故夫三代無
文人非無文人也風俗渾厚有欲工而不
能之意然觀周詩田夫田婦摸寫之工何
punctuated:
可愛也，然有不充則缺矣，有不造則偏矣，有不運則滯矣。是故自聖人以下，邪正不同路，純駁不同色，大小不同器，清濁不同流，而文章亦與之俱。嗚呼！文章固學者之末事也，而於此可以觀心志焉，可以考節操焉，可以驗智識焉，可以占才能焉。文其可易言耶？請因明問所及而陳之。
夫文章唯孔子之六經至矣，而何所昉乎？煥於被四表之堯，而非堯也；盡於畫八卦之包羲，而非羲也。其始於於穆不已之天乎？蓋本爲一誠，列爲四德，散爲五行，而聖人得之以爲心。於是乎清明純粹之實，自然光輝發越，條理分明。故達而在上，則昌言嘉謨足以定國是，而以文章見於政；窮而在下，則潜德隱行足以勵世俗，而以文章筆之書。聖人何嘗有意於爲文哉？故夫三代無文人，非無文人也，風俗渾厚，有欲工而不能之意。然觀周詩田夫田婦摸寫之工，何
translation_en:
…is worthy of admiration. Yet wherever it is not fully developed, there is deficiency; wherever it does not attain its proper realization, there is one-sidedness; wherever it is not put into motion, there is stagnation. Thus, from the sages downward, the deviant and the upright follow different paths; the pure and the mixed display different colors; the great and the small have different capacities; the clear and the turbid flow in different streams. Literary expression accompanies these differences. Alas! Writing is indeed a secondary concern for the learner, yet through it one may observe a person's mind and aspirations, examine moral integrity, test understanding and discernment, and assess talent and ability. Can writing, then, be spoken of lightly? Allow me to set forth my views on the matters raised in your discerning question.
As for literary expression, only the Six Classics of Confucius attain perfection. But where did it originate? It shone brilliantly in Yao, whose influence reached the four distant bounds, yet it did not originate with Yao. It found its fullest expression in Baoxi, who drew the Eight Trigrams, yet it did not originate with Baoxi. Did it perhaps begin with Heaven, profound and unceasing? At its root it is a single sincerity; differentiated, it is the four virtues; dispersed, it is the Five Phases. The sage receives it and makes it his mind. Thus the substance of clarity and purity naturally radiates brilliance and displays distinct order. When successful and occupying high office, the sage offers worthy words and excellent counsels sufficient to settle the proper course of the state, and literary expression manifests itself in government. When constrained and remaining in a lowly position, his unrecognized virtue and hidden conduct suffice to elevate prevailing customs, and he records them in writing. When did the sage ever deliberately set out to compose literature? Thus, to say that the Three Dynasties had no literary men does not mean that they actually had none. Their customs were simple and substantial: it was as though, even had they wished to display literary craftsmanship, they could not. Yet consider the skill with which farming men and women depicted things in the Poetry of Zhou—how …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文人之多也六經無文法非無文法也無
意於立法而紆徐曲折有化工自然之妙
若明問所論大誥繫辭諸篇是也後世之
論文者吾惑焉如張文潜之說則學文以
明理爲急如倪正父之說則爲文以體製
爲先二者似之而實非也夫理非文外之
物也惟平日務學明理之功既深則吾之
爲文無意於明理而理趣有不可遏矣無
意於合體而體製自有可觀矣若如二子
===
之說則爲文之時尋何理以爲通貫檢何
體以爲法程此即明問所謂以文章爲事
業汲汲乎弊精神以求見於世而不自知
其勞者也而何怪其不能追古作哉至於
文章與時高下三代之文至戰國而病涉
秦漢復起秦漢之文至三國而病唐興復
起此劉夢得之說似之而亦有未盡然者
夫文之興也以道道之興也以學而豈興
於時哉如興於時則春秋何以興六經戰
punctuated: 文人之多也！六經無文法，非無文法也，無意於立法，而紆徐曲折，有化工自然之妙，若明問所論《大誥》《繫辭》諸篇是也。後世之論文者，吾惑焉。如張文潜之說，則學文以明理爲急；如倪正父之說，則爲文以體製爲先。二者似之而實非也。夫理非文外之物也，惟平日務學明理之功既深，則吾之爲文，無意於明理，而理趣有不可遏矣；無意於合體，而體製自有可觀矣。若如二子之說，則爲文之時，尋何理以爲通貫，檢何體以爲法程？此即明問所謂以文章爲事業，汲汲乎弊精神以求見於世，而不自知其勞者也。而何怪其不能追古作哉？至於文章與時高下，三代之文至戰國而病，涉秦漢復起；秦漢之文至三國而病，唐興復起。此劉夢得之說，似之而亦有未盡然者。夫文之興也以道，道之興也以學，而豈興於時哉？如興於時，則春秋何以興六經，戰
translation_en:
…how numerous were the men of letters! To say that the Six Classics have no rules of composition does not mean that they lack such rules. There was no intention to establish rules, yet their leisurely unfolding and intricate turns possess the spontaneous marvel of nature’s creative work. Such are the Great Announcement and the Appended Statements, among the pieces discussed in your discerning question.

I am perplexed by those of later ages who discuss writing. According to Zhang Wenqian’s view, understanding principle is the urgent priority in studying composition; according to Ni Zhengfu’s view, form and structure come first in writing. Both views seem correct but are actually mistaken. Principle is not something external to writing. Only when one’s habitual efforts at learning and understanding principle have become profound will the significance of principle flow irrepressibly through one’s writing, without any deliberate intention to elucidate it; and even without deliberately conforming to a form, the form and structure will naturally have qualities worthy of admiration. If one follows these two men’s views, then, when writing, what principle should one seek to provide a unifying thread, and what form should one consult as a standard? This is precisely what your discerning question describes: making literary composition one’s occupation, anxiously exhausting one’s mental energies in seeking recognition in the world, without oneself realizing the toil involved. Why, then, be surprised that such writers cannot rival ancient works?

As for the claim that writing rises and falls with the times—that the writing of the Three Dynasties declined in the Warring States period and revived during the Qin and Han, and that the writing of the Qin and Han declined by the Three Kingdoms period and revived with the rise of the Tang—this view of Liu Mengde’s also seems correct, but is not entirely so. Writing flourishes through the Way, and the Way flourishes through learning. How could its flourishing depend on the times? If it depended on the times, then how could the Six Classics have arisen in the Spring and Autumn period, and in the Warring…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國何以興七篇哉其說亦牽合矣就其所
論文人而品評之列禦寇之文平淡疎曠
莊周之文跌蕩開闔荀況之文敷腴宏大
皆有可觀者矣然莊列荒唐多寓言與佛
氏老子之說相表裏至漁父盜跖篇又詆
孔子之徒是叛禮背教甚矣荀子極偏駁
觀其以性為惡以禮為偽以子思孟軻亂
天下至於事黃歇教李斯則其為人之卑
又可知矣而何文之足論哉漢之能為文
===
者皆曰賈生董相史遷相如揚雄然賈之
文質實董之文滋潤司馬之文雄健相如
之文富麗揚雄之文奧衍是皆文人之白
眉也但表餌之策發於疎上林之賦流於
侈法言妄擬論語史記乃後六經且
之開爐新莽之執贊固立身之
懷王以殞命救李陵以
者矣董之議論
固非醇乎
punctuated: 國何以興七篇哉？其說亦牽合矣。就其所論文人而品評之：列禦寇之文平淡疎曠，莊周之文跌蕩開闔，荀況之文敷腴宏大，皆有可觀者矣。然莊列荒唐，多寓言，與佛氏老子之說相表裏；至《漁父》《盜跖》篇，又詆孔子之徒，是叛禮背教甚矣。荀子極偏駁，觀其以性為惡，以禮為偽，以子思孟軻亂天下，至於事黃歇、教李斯，則其為人之卑又可知矣，而何文之足論哉？漢之能為文者，皆曰賈生、董相、史遷、相如、揚雄。然賈之文質實，董之文滋潤，司馬之文雄健，相如之文富麗，揚雄之文奧衍，是皆文人之白眉也。但表餌之策發於疎，《上林》之賦流於侈，《法言》妄擬《論語》，《史記》乃後六經，且之開爐，新莽之執贊，固立身之，懷王以殞命，救李陵以，者矣。董之議論，固非醇乎
translation_en:
…why, then, did the Seven Chapters arise during the Warring States period? His explanation, too, forces things into agreement. If we assess the writers he discusses: Lie Yukou’s prose is plain, understated, expansive, and untrammeled; Zhuang Zhou’s is sweeping and freely shifts between opening out and drawing together; Xun Kuang’s is rich, ample, and grand. All have qualities worth appreciating. Yet Zhuang Zhou and Lie Yukou indulge in extravagant fancies and numerous allegories, their teachings complementing those of the Buddhists and Laozi. The chapters “The Fisherman” and “Robber Zhi” even disparage Confucius and his followers: this is an extreme betrayal of ritual propriety and the teaching. Xunzi is profoundly one-sided and inconsistent. Consider how he regards human nature as evil and ritual as artifice, and accuses Zisi and Meng Ke of throwing the world into disorder. As for his serving Huang Xie and teaching Li Si, these further reveal the baseness of his character. What, then, is there in his writing worth discussing?

Among accomplished Han writers, everyone names Master Jia [Jia Yi], Chancellor Dong [Dong Zhongshu], the historian Qian [Sima Qian], Sima Xiangru, and Yang Xiong. Jia’s prose is substantial and unadorned; Dong’s, rich and mellow; Sima Qian’s, vigorous and forceful; Xiangru’s, sumptuous and elegant; and Yang Xiong’s, profound and expansive. These are all outstanding figures among writers. Yet the policy proposal concerning outward displays and enticements arose from insufficient understanding [?]; the “Rhapsody on the Imperial Park” lapses into extravagance; Model Sayings presumptuously imitates the Analects; and Records of the Historian places the Six Classics afterward [?]. Then come references to “opening a furnace” [?] and offering praise to Wang Mang’s Xin regime—surely matters concerning one’s personal conduct [?]; to King Huai and losing one’s life [?]; and to defending Li Ling and thereby … [?]. As for Dong’s arguments, surely … pure … [?]…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
儒孰能出其右者耶漢之後曰唐吾得一
韓昌黎爲一時山斗唐之後爲宋吾得一
歐陽永叔足以追韓氏而先後爭光者也
今以二子之文論之愈之文刋落陳言酷
排釋氏其言汗漫卓踔𠖥泫閎深真所謂
日光玉潔周情孔思者也史臣稱之曰摧
陷廓清之功比孟子而力倍之今雖不可
謂倍孟子也獨不謂孟子之徒乎蘇子稱
歐子之文也曰詩賦如李白記事如司馬
===
遷論治如陸贄至於變文體濯士氣以救
時行道其功亦不細矣以其文考之則豐
樂亭等記玉顏身累等詩一唱三嘆寄美
麗於平淡當時以爲今之韓愈夫復何愧
哉但晦菴之論有曰韓千變萬化無心而
最高歐有心而可學蓋韓之文如馭馬通
衢塵陌縱橫馳逐唯意所至何高也歐之
文如賓主相見平心易氣而雍容揖遜此
所以可學也若論其文之不能無病則讀
punctuated: 儒孰能出其右者耶？漢之後曰唐，吾得一韓昌黎，爲一時山斗。唐之後爲宋，吾得一歐陽永叔，足以追韓氏而先後爭光者也。今以二子之文論之，愈之文刋落陳言，酷排釋氏，其言汗漫卓踔，𠖥泫閎深，真所謂日光玉潔、周情孔思者也。史臣稱之曰：「摧陷廓清之功，比孟子而力倍之。」今雖不可謂倍孟子也，獨不謂孟子之徒乎？蘇子稱歐子之文也，曰：「詩賦如李白，記事如司馬遷，論治如陸贄。」至於變文體、濯士氣，以救時行道，其功亦不細矣。以其文考之，則《豐樂亭》等記、《玉顏》《身累》等詩，一唱三嘆，寄美麗於平淡，當時以爲今之韓愈，夫復何愧哉？但晦菴之論有曰：「韓千變萬化，無心而最高；歐有心而可學。」蓋韓之文如馭馬通衢塵陌，縱橫馳逐，唯意所至，何高也！歐之文如賓主相見，平心易氣而雍容揖遜，此所以可學也。若論其文之不能無病，則讀
translation_en:
…among Confucian scholars, who could surpass him? After the Han came the Tang, in which I find Han Changli, a Mount Tai and Northern Dipper for his age. After the Tang came the Song, in which I find Ouyang Yongshu, who could follow Master Han and rival his brilliance across successive ages.

To discuss these two men’s writings: Han Yu’s prose strips away stale expressions and fiercely attacks Buddhism. His language is expansive and striking, [?] and profound—truly what is called “the radiance of the sun and purity of jade, the sentiments of the Duke of Zhou and the thoughts of Confucius.” The historian praised him, saying: “His achievement in breaking through and clearing away rival teachings was comparable to Mencius’s, but twice as forceful.” Even if we cannot now say that he was twice the equal of Mencius, can we deny that he was a follower of Mencius?

Master Su praised Master Ouyang’s writing, saying: “His poetry and rhapsodies resemble Li Bai’s; his recording of events, Sima Qian’s; his discussions of government, Lu Zhi’s.” As for transforming literary style and cleansing the spirit of scholars in order to remedy the troubles of the age and put the Way into practice, his achievement was also considerable. Examining his writings, we find accounts such as the Account of the Pavilion of Abundant Joy, and poems such as “Jade Countenance” and “The Burden of the Body” [?]: one singing calls forth three sighs of admiration, and beauty resides within plainness. His contemporaries regarded him as the Han Yu of their day. How could he fall short of that praise?

Yet Hui’an observed: “Han undergoes a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations; without conscious effort, he reaches the highest level. Ouyang works deliberately and can be learned from.” Han’s prose is like riding a horse through broad thoroughfares and dusty lanes, galloping freely in every direction, wherever the inclination leads. How lofty it is! Ouyang’s prose is like a meeting between host and guest: calm in mind and gentle in manner, graciously bowing and yielding precedence. This is why it can be learned from. If, however, we discuss the faults that their writings could not entirely avoid, then “Reading…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
墨篇以異端並之聖人孟簡書為太顛所
惑至以博愛為仁三品為性則見用而昧
體誠有所不免者矣歐子自稱曰我所為
文必與道俱則與道與文為二事故本論
雖正而以封建井田之禮變佛氏亦拙矣
又以琴書碁酒與老人為六是何言之放
誕不羈哉蓋平日以性非所急而以十翼
不出於孔子亦幾於叛矣是故晦菴所謂
治世之文程子所謂化工之文二子皆不
===
能造其藩籬祇皆飲酒賦詩而因文以見
道也其在剪裁之下繪畫之上乎又就二
子之文而低昂之歐晚年筆力亦衰其文
終不如韓而韓之文又不如漢漢之文又
不如先秦戰國蓋去聖有遠近而聞道有
多寡也又就二子之人品而論之韓子以
出使折藩鎮勁氣凛於氷霜以極諫貶潮
陽精忠貫乎日月而歐之犯顏直諫救時
行道君子恃而不恐小人畏而不為則皆
punctuated:
墨篇，以異端並之聖人；《孟簡書》，為太顛所惑。至以博愛為仁，三品為性，則見用而昧體，誠有所不免者矣。歐子自稱曰：「我所為文，必與道俱。」則與道與文為二事，故《本論》雖正，而以封建井田之禮變佛氏，亦拙矣。又以琴書碁酒與老人為六，是何言之放誕不羈哉！蓋平日以性非所急，而以《十翼》不出於孔子，亦幾於叛矣。是故晦菴所謂治世之文，程子所謂化工之文，二子皆不能造其藩籬，祇皆飲酒賦詩，而因文以見道也。其在剪裁之下、繪畫之上乎？

又就二子之文而低昂之，歐晚年筆力亦衰，其文終不如韓，而韓之文又不如漢，漢之文又不如先秦戰國。蓋去聖有遠近，而聞道有多寡也。

又就二子之人品而論之，韓子以出使折藩鎮，勁氣凛於氷霜；以極諫貶潮陽，精忠貫乎日月。而歐之犯顏直諫，救時行道，君子恃而不恐，小人畏而不為，則皆
translation_en:
…the essay on Mozi places a heterodox thinker alongside the sage; the Letter to Meng Jian shows that he was beguiled by Dadian. As for identifying benevolence with universal love and human nature with three grades, he perceived their functioning but failed to grasp their underlying substance: these were indeed faults he could not escape. Master Ouyang himself declared, “The writings I compose must always accompany the Way.” This makes the Way and writing two separate matters. Thus, although his Discourse on Fundamentals is sound, his proposal to transform Buddhism through the institutions of enfeoffment and the well-field system is also clumsy. Moreover, he counts the zither, books, chess, wine, and the old man as six [?]. How extravagant and unrestrained such words are! In his ordinary thinking, he regarded human nature as no urgent concern and held that the Ten Wings did not come from Confucius. This, too, approached apostasy. Thus, neither of these two masters could even reach the outer bounds of what Hui'an called “the writing of a well-governed age” or what Master Cheng called “writing wrought by nature.” Both merely drank wine and composed poetry, revealing the Way through their writing. Might they rank below cutting and tailoring, but above painting?

Further, if we compare the writings of the two masters, Ouyang’s literary powers also declined in his later years, and his writing ultimately falls short of Han Yu’s. Han’s writing, in turn, falls short of that of the Han dynasty, while Han-dynasty writing falls short of that of the pre-Qin Warring States period. This is because their distance from the sages differed, as did the extent to which they had learned of the Way.

Further, if we discuss the personal character of these two masters, Master Han, when sent on a mission, subdued a regional military governor, his indomitable spirit more chilling than ice and frost. For his utmost remonstrance he was demoted to Chaoyang, his pure loyalty reaching through sun and moon. As for Ouyang, he braved the ruler’s displeasure to remonstrate frankly, remedied the troubles of his age, and put the Way into practice. Gentlemen relied on him and felt no fear; petty men feared him and refrained from wrongdoing. Thus both were …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
俊偉光明董仲舒以後所未有也其視荀
揚之擇不精語不詳而爲名教罪人何啻
珠玉之於瓦礫耶昔吕與叔之詩有曰文
如元凱方成癖學類相如始類俳獨立孔
門無一事只輸顔子得心齋則固以君子
之學務其遠者大者而不徒事其文也愚
也讀古人之文固未嘗不策勵而欲追其
步驟咏吕氏之詩又未嘗不猛省而欲造
乎坐忘也惟執事其濯磨之
===
第四問
饒相
同考試官訓導王批〔道統之傳在學者最當體究此策獨能探之得非學之有得者邪良士良士〕
考試官教諭張批〔深契源流〕
考試官教授錢批〔明備〕
孔門道統之傳惟聖賢爲能深以造之明
以通之夫聖人之道昭灼如火焉潤澤如
水焉蓋無一息之間斷遏佚也而何待後
punctuated:
俊偉光明，董仲舒以後所未有也。其視荀揚之擇不精、語不詳，而爲名教罪人，何啻珠玉之於瓦礫耶！昔吕與叔之詩有曰：「文如元凱方成癖，學類相如始類俳。獨立孔門無一事，只輸顔子得心齋。」則固以君子之學務其遠者大者，而不徒事其文也。愚也讀古人之文，固未嘗不策勵而欲追其步驟；咏吕氏之詩，又未嘗不猛省而欲造乎坐忘也。惟執事其濯磨之。

第四問
饒相
同考試官訓導王批〔道統之傳，在學者最當體究。此策獨能探之，得非學之有得者邪？良士！良士！〕
考試官教諭張批〔深契源流。〕
考試官教授錢批〔明備。〕

孔門道統之傳，惟聖賢爲能深以造之，明以通之。夫聖人之道，昭灼如火焉，潤澤如水焉，蓋無一息之間斷遏佚也，而何待後
translation_en:
…outstanding and radiant, unmatched since Dong Zhongshu. Compared with Xun Kuang and Yang Xiong, whose judgments lacked precision and whose statements lacked thoroughness, making them offenders against the moral teachings, how much more were they than pearls and jade beside broken tiles and rubble! Lü Yushu once wrote in a poem: “Writing like Yuankai merely becomes an obsession; learning like Xiangru only makes one resemble an entertainer. Standing alone at Confucius’s gate, with nothing to occupy oneself, one still yields to Master Yan, who attained the fasting of the mind.” This surely means that the gentleman’s learning pursues what is far-reaching and great, rather than merely occupying itself with literary composition. Whenever I, in my ignorance, read the writings of the ancients, I spur myself onward, wishing to follow in their footsteps; whenever I recite Mr. Lü’s poem, I awaken sharply to self-examination, wishing to attain ‘sitting in forgetfulness.’ I ask you, honored sir, to cleanse and polish me.

Fourth Question
Rao Xiang
Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The transmission of the succession of the Way is what students should most earnestly investigate and embody. This policy essay alone succeeds in probing it. Surely its author is someone who has gained something through learning? A worthy scholar! A worthy scholar!〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Deeply comprehends the sources and subsequent development.〕
Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: 〔Clear and comprehensive.〕

As for the transmission of the succession of the Way in the school of Confucius, only sages and worthies can attain it through depth and comprehend it through clarity. The Way of the sages shines brightly like fire and moistens and nourishes like water. Indeed, there is not a single moment when it is interrupted, obstructed, or lost [?]. Why, then, should it depend upon later…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人傳授以爲之主張哉蓋使世道而常如
唐虞可無恙也唯立異者激之好高者揚
之用邪者壅之自私者撲之激則其流横
矣揚則其本搖矣壅則其坊壞矣撲則其
光晦矣然則主盟斯世以任繼往開來之
責在聖賢可得而辭者哉顧夫時有先後
地有淺深有不可强而同者維扶世立敎
而議論不詭於聖人則皆可謂濬其流也
揚其波也助其瀾也皆可謂嘘其烟也熾
===
其膏也裂其焰也安得世世如大聖人而
後可秉吾道之旌麾哉今夫世之語道統
者曰奇偶二畫包犧爲文字之祖執中一
語帝堯肇心學之源列聖相承曰精曰一
曰義曰禮曰敬曰義辭雖不同而道實相
同也孰知夫子集群聖之大成而作爲六
經以詔萬世皆其所自得師哉故謂夫子
爲文字之祖心學之源可也而豈可獨歸
之羲堯耶夫孔子既爲萬世心學之源則
punctuated:
人傳授以爲之主張哉？蓋使世道而常如唐虞，可無恙也。唯立異者激之，好高者揚之，用邪者壅之，自私者撲之。激則其流横矣，揚則其本搖矣，壅則其坊壞矣，撲則其光晦矣。然則主盟斯世，以任繼往開來之責，在聖賢可得而辭者哉？顧夫時有先後，地有淺深，有不可强而同者。維扶世立敎，而議論不詭於聖人，則皆可謂濬其流也，揚其波也，助其瀾也；皆可謂嘘其烟也，熾其膏也，裂其焰也。安得世世如大聖人，而後可秉吾道之旌麾哉？
今夫世之語道統者曰：「奇偶二畫，包犧爲文字之祖；執中一語，帝堯肇心學之源。列聖相承，曰精，曰一，曰義，曰禮，曰敬，曰義，辭雖不同，而道實相同也。」孰知夫子集群聖之大成，而作爲六經以詔萬世，皆其所自得師哉？故謂夫子爲文字之祖、心學之源可也，而豈可獨歸之羲堯耶？夫孔子既爲萬世心學之源，則
translation_en:
…people of later ages to transmit it and act as its champions? If the way of the world always remained as it was under Tang Yao and Yu Shun, it could suffer no harm. Yet those who insist on being different agitate it; those who prize lofty notions raise it up; those who employ perversity obstruct it; and those who pursue private interests beat it down. When agitated, its current runs wild; when raised up, its root is shaken; when obstructed, its embankments collapse; when beaten down, its light grows dim. Can sages and worthies therefore decline to lead this world and assume responsibility for carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future? Yet times differ in their sequence, and positions in their depth; these cannot be forcibly made alike. So long as people sustain the world and establish its teachings, and their arguments do not depart from the sages, they may all be said to deepen its current, raise its waves, and swell its billows; they may all be said to fan its smoke, kindle its oil, and send its flames bursting forth. How could we require people in every generation to equal the great sage before they may bear the banners of our Way?
Now those in this world who discuss the succession of the Way say: “Through the two kinds of line, odd and even, Baoxi became the progenitor of writing; through the phrase ‘hold fast to the mean,’ Emperor Yao opened the source of the learning of the mind. Successive sages handed it down, speaking of refinement, unity, righteousness, ritual propriety, reverence, and righteousness. Though their expressions differed, their Way was in fact the same.” Who recognizes that the Master brought together the consummate achievements of all the sages and composed the Six Classics to instruct all generations, all arising from his own understanding [?]? Thus it is fitting to call the Master the progenitor of writing and the source of the learning of the mind. How could these distinctions be attributed exclusively to Baoxi and Yao? Since Confucius is the source of the learning of the mind for all generations, then…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其一脉之相傳不可不要其始而究其終
矣夫孔門高弟唯顏氏曾氏之傳得其宗
曾氏以是傳之子思子思以是傳之孟子
此黃勉齋謂孟子傳統於子思之說也抑
不曰傳孔子之統而謂傳統於子思者特
據其及門受業言之也若以其功論之孟
子蘊經綸之大業而發明性道純乎純故
謂孟子傳子思之統可也傳孔子之統亦
可也豈必見而知之爲傳道聞而知之者
===
非傳道耶顏子卒於陋巷孟子亦不見用
於齊梁是皆隱未見行未成也而朱子以
顏子優湯武程子以孟子並禹稷者蓋顏
子有若無實若虛氣象何溫淳也然以有
爲如舜而敢問爲邦則其剛大之志王佐
之材又可想見故使其見諸事業雖不及
湯而成就則渾渾無痕迹雖湯亦有所不
及也是之謂優於湯武也孟子以身任道
而息邪說拒詖行放淫詞自以爲承禹抑
punctuated:
其一脉之相傳，不可不要其始而究其終矣。夫孔門高弟，唯顏氏、曾氏之傳得其宗。曾氏以是傳之子思，子思以是傳之孟子，此黃勉齋謂孟子傳統於子思之說也。抑不曰傳孔子之統，而謂傳統於子思者，特據其及門受業言之也。若以其功論之，孟子蘊經綸之大業，而發明性道，純乎純。故謂孟子傳子思之統可也，傳孔子之統亦可也。豈必見而知之爲傳道，聞而知之者非傳道耶？

顏子卒於陋巷，孟子亦不見用於齊梁，是皆隱未見、行未成也。而朱子以顏子優湯武，程子以孟子並禹稷者，蓋顏子有若無，實若虛，氣象何溫淳也！然以有爲如舜，而敢問爲邦，則其剛大之志、王佐之材，又可想見。故使其見諸事業，雖不及湯而成就，則渾渾無痕迹，雖湯亦有所不及也。是之謂優於湯武也。孟子以身任道，而息邪說、拒詖行、放淫詞，自以爲承禹抑
translation_en:
…one must trace this single line of transmission back to its beginning and investigate it through to its end. Among Kongzi’s outstanding disciples, only Yan Hui and Zeng Shen grasped its essential purport in what they transmitted. Zeng Shen transmitted this to Zisi, and Zisi transmitted it to Mengzi. This is what Huang Mianzhai meant when he said that Mengzi inherited the succession from Zisi. Yet his saying that Mengzi inherited the succession from Zisi, rather than that he transmitted Kongzi’s succession, refers specifically to his studying personally under Zisi. If we judge by his accomplishments, Mengzi possessed the capacity for the great work of ordering the world, and his elucidation of human nature and the Way was utterly pure. Thus, it is right to say that Mengzi transmitted Zisi’s succession, and equally right to say that he transmitted Kongzi’s. Must only those who knew through seeing count as transmitters of the Way, while those who knew through hearing do not?

Master Yan died in a humble lane, and Mengzi likewise found no employment in Qi or Liang. In both cases, their qualities remained hidden and unmanifested, and their endeavors were left unfulfilled. Yet Master Zhu considered Master Yan superior to Tang and Wu, while Master Cheng ranked Mengzi alongside Yu and Ji. This was because Master Yan possessed ability as though he had none, and was full as though empty: how gentle and sincere his bearing was! Yet, believing that one who acted could become like Shun, he ventured to ask about governing a state. From this we can also envisage his firm and lofty resolve and his capacity to assist a true king. Thus, had these qualities found expression in public achievements, even if his accomplishments had fallen short of Tang’s, they would have been whole and seamless, leaving no trace of contrivance; in this respect even Tang would have fallen short of him. This is what is meant by his superiority to Tang and Wu. Mengzi took personal responsibility for the Way, putting an end to pernicious doctrines, opposing deviant conduct, and banishing extravagant language. He regarded himself as carrying on the work of Yu in restraining…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
洪水周公驅猛獸孔子作春秋之功不然
楊墨之禍世未止也以孟子比禹稷豈不
宜耶孟子既沒聖學失傳歷世久遠其間
儒者非不知尊孔孟而談六經然不越文
義訓詁之間而止矣濂溪生千載之下獨
得微旨而發之圖書凡太極性命陰陽鬼
神綱分臚別使學者曉然知所準的此正
明問所謂濂溪傳孟子之統者也而謂受
學於希夷豈知濂溪者哉自是一傳而得
===
二程數傳而得紫陽二程之學皆以學庸
語孟為標的而達於六經辨異端扶正道
故伊川謂明道孟子以後一人而已紫陽
之學又集諸儒之大成而粹乎洙泗伊洛
之緒故鶴山謂朱子之功不在孟子下也
然則謂紫陽傳二程之統可也謂傳孟子
之統亦可也謂程子傳濂溪之統可也謂
傳孟子之統亦可也蓋千聖一心也萬古
一道也何先後彼此之間耶當時橫渠之
punctuated: 洪水、周公驅猛獸、孔子作《春秋》之功。不然，楊墨之禍世未止也。以孟子比禹稷，豈不宜耶？孟子既沒，聖學失傳，歷世久遠。其間儒者非不知尊孔孟而談六經，然不越文義訓詁之間而止矣。濂溪生千載之下，獨得微旨而發之圖書。凡太極、性命、陰陽、鬼神，綱分臚別，使學者曉然知所準的。此正明問所謂濂溪傳孟子之統者也。而謂受學於希夷，豈知濂溪者哉？自是一傳而得二程，數傳而得紫陽。二程之學，皆以《學》《庸》《語》《孟》為標的，而達於六經，辨異端，扶正道。故伊川謂明道孟子以後一人而已。紫陽之學，又集諸儒之大成，而粹乎洙泗伊洛之緒。故鶴山謂朱子之功不在孟子下也。然則謂紫陽傳二程之統可也，謂傳孟子之統亦可也；謂程子傳濂溪之統可也，謂傳孟子之統亦可也。蓋千聖一心也，萬古一道也，何先後彼此之間耶？當時橫渠之
translation_en: …the flood, the Duke of Zhou’s driving out fierce beasts, and Confucius’s composing the Spring and Autumn Annals. Otherwise, the harm that the teachings of Yang Zhu and Mo Di inflicted upon the world would not have ceased. Is it not fitting to compare Mengzi with Yu and Ji? After Mengzi died, the transmission of the sages’ learning was lost, and many generations passed. The Confucian scholars of those intervening times certainly knew to revere Confucius and Mengzi and discuss the Six Classics, yet they went no further than textual interpretation and glosses. Born a thousand years later, Lianxi (Zhou Dunyi) alone grasped the subtle meaning and expounded it in diagrams and writings. He systematically distinguished and set forth the Supreme Ultimate, human nature and destiny, yin and yang, and ghosts and spirits, enabling students to understand clearly what standards to follow. This is precisely what your illuminating question means by saying that Lianxi transmitted Mengzi’s succession. Could anyone who claims that he studied under Xiyi (Chen Tuan) truly understand Lianxi? From this point, one generation of transmission brought forth the two Cheng brothers, and several generations brought forth Ziyang (Zhu Xi). The learning of the two Cheng brothers took the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, the Analects, and the Mengzi as its standards and extended to the Six Classics, distinguishing heterodox teachings and upholding the correct Way. Thus Yichuan (Cheng Yi) said that Mingdao (Cheng Hao) was the sole such figure since Mengzi. Ziyang’s learning, in turn, brought together the achievements of the Confucian scholars into a comprehensive whole and embodied the pure tradition of the Zhu and Si rivers and the Yi and Luo rivers. Thus Heshan (Wei Liaoweng) said that Master Zhu’s contribution was no less than Mengzi’s. Accordingly, one may say that Ziyang transmitted the succession of the two Cheng brothers, or that he transmitted Mengzi’s succession. One may say that Master Cheng transmitted Lianxi’s succession, or that he transmitted Mengzi’s succession. For the thousand sages share one mind, and throughout all ages there is one Way. What distinction, then, is there between earlier and later, between this person and that? At that time, Hengqu’s…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
洪水周公驅猛獸孔子作春秋之功不然
楊墨之禍世未止也以孟子比禹稷豈不
宜耶孟子既沒聖學失傳歷世乆遠其間
儒者非不知尊孔孟而談六經然不越文
義訓詁之間而止矣濂溪生千載之下獨
得微㫖而發之圖書凡太極性命陰陽鬼
神綱分彪別使學者曉然知所準的此正
明問所謂濂溪傳孟子之統者也而謂受
學於希夷豈知濂溪者哉自是一傳而得
===
二程數傳而得紫陽二程之學皆以學庸
語孟為標的而達於六經辯異端扶正道
故伊川謂明道孟子以後一人而已紫陽
