之統亦可也謂程子傳濂溪之統可也謂
傳孟子之統亦可也蓋千聖一心也萬古
一道也何先後彼此之間耶當時橫渠之
punctuated: 洪水、周公驅猛獸、孔子作《春秋》之功。不然，楊墨之禍世未止也。以孟子比禹稷，豈不宜耶？孟子既沒，聖學失傳，歷世乆遠。其間儒者非不知尊孔孟而談六經，然不越文義訓詁之間而止矣。濂溪生千載之下，獨得微㫖而發之圖書。凡太極、性命、陰陽、鬼神，綱分彪別，使學者曉然知所準的。此正明問所謂濂溪傳孟子之統者也。而謂受學於希夷，豈知濂溪者哉？自是一傳而得二程，數傳而得紫陽。二程之學，皆以《學》《庸》《語》《孟》為標的，而達於六經，辯異端，扶正道。故伊川謂明道孟子以後一人而已。紫陽之學，又集諸儒之大成，而粹乎洙泗伊洛之緒。故鶴山謂朱子之功不在孟子下也。然則謂紫陽傳二程之統可也，謂傳孟子之統亦可也；謂程子傳濂溪之統可也，謂傳孟子之統亦可也。蓋千聖一心也，萬古一道也，何先後彼此之間耶？當時橫渠之
translation_en: …the achievement of [controlling] the flood, of the Duke of Zhou’s driving out fierce beasts, and of Confucius’s composing the Spring and Autumn Annals. Otherwise, the harm inflicted on the world by the teachings of Yang Zhu and Mo Di would not have ceased. Is it not fitting to compare Mengzi with Yu and Ji? After Mengzi died, the learning of the sages ceased to be transmitted, and many generations passed. Scholars during that interval were not unaware that they should revere Confucius and Mengzi and discuss the Six Classics, yet they went no further than textual meanings and philological glosses. Born a thousand years later, Lianxi (Zhou Dunyi) alone grasped the subtle purport and set it forth in diagrams and writings. He clearly distinguished the main divisions of such matters as the Supreme Ultimate, human nature and destiny, yin and yang, and ghosts and spirits, enabling students to understand plainly the standards they should follow. This is precisely what your illuminating question means by saying that Lianxi transmitted Mengzi’s succession. But can those who claim that he studied under Xiyi (Chen Tuan) truly understand Lianxi? From him, one transmission brought forth the two Cheng brothers, and several transmissions brought forth Ziyang (Zhu Xi). The learning of the two Cheng brothers took the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, the Analects, and the Mengzi as its standard and extended to the Six Classics, refuting heterodox teachings and upholding the correct Way. Thus Yichuan (Cheng Yi) said that Mingdao (Cheng Hao) was the one unique figure since Mengzi. Ziyang’s learning, moreover, brought together the great achievements of the various Confucian scholars and distilled the traditions of the Zhu and Si rivers and of the Yi and Luo rivers. Thus Heshan (Wei Liaoweng) said that Master Zhu’s achievement was no less than Mengzi’s. Accordingly, it is permissible to say that Ziyang transmitted the succession of the two Cheng brothers, and equally permissible to say that he transmitted Mengzi’s succession. It is permissible to say that Master Cheng transmitted Lianxi’s succession, and equally permissible to say that he transmitted Mengzi’s succession. For the thousand sages share one mind, and throughout all antiquity there is one Way: what distinction can there be between earlier and later, or between one and another? As for Hengqu (Zhang Zai) at that time, his…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
精思力疾妙契疾書堯夫之天挺人豪英
邁蓋世延平之身世兩忘精義造約東萊
備四時之和涵千古之秘敬夫擴仁義之
端謹義利之辯皆於吾道有聞焉者也而
不得與道統豈非張邵猶宗乎二程吕張
猶宗乎晦翁者耶程子之門若謝上蔡朱
子之門若蔡季通亦庶幾有聞於道矣君
子論道統而以程子傳之龜山朱子傳之
勉齋者豈二子之學能過於張邵諸賢哉
===
亦自其能傳中庸易學能成經傳通解皆
見知之真者而許之也豈天下定論哉若
夫二程之學晦翁以爲明道比顏伊川比
孟者蓋明道之德性寬大規模廣闊伊川
氣質剛方文理密察其氣象實相當也而
一愛游定夫一愛楊中立亦豈不以二人
氣象之相類哉但明道之比顏固亦然矣
伊川檢束之功孟子不能及而孟子雄才
又非伊川所能到也就以二程行事而觀
punctuated:
精思力疾，妙契疾書；堯夫之天挺人豪，英邁蓋世；延平之身世兩忘，精義造約；東萊備四時之和，涵千古之秘；敬夫擴仁義之端，謹義利之辯：皆於吾道有聞焉者也。而不得與道統，豈非張邵猶宗乎二程，吕張猶宗乎晦翁者耶？程子之門若謝上蔡，朱子之門若蔡季通，亦庶幾有聞於道矣。君子論道統，而以程子傳之龜山、朱子傳之勉齋者，豈二子之學能過於張邵諸賢哉？亦自其能傳中庸易學，能成經傳通解，皆見知之真者而許之也，豈天下定論哉？
若夫二程之學，晦翁以爲明道比顏、伊川比孟者，蓋明道之德性寬大，規模廣闊；伊川氣質剛方，文理密察，其氣象實相當也。而一愛游定夫，一愛楊中立，亦豈不以二人氣象之相類哉？但明道之比顏固亦然矣，伊川檢束之功，孟子不能及；而孟子雄才，又非伊川所能到也。就以二程行事而觀
translation_en:
…his profound reflection and exertion despite illness, his subtle apprehension and swift writing [?]; Yaofu’s heaven-endowed eminence and unsurpassed brilliance; Yanping’s forgetting both himself and the world, refining his understanding of principle and attaining its essentials; Donglai’s possessing the harmony of all four seasons and encompassing the mysteries of the ages; and Jingfu’s developing the beginnings of benevolence and righteousness and carefully distinguishing righteousness from profit: all these men had gained some understanding of our Way. Yet they were not included in the succession of the Way. Was this not because Zhang and Shao still took the two Cheng brothers as their masters, while Lü and Zhang still took Huiweng as theirs? Among Master Cheng’s disciples, men such as Xie Shangcai, and among Master Zhu’s disciples, men such as Cai Jitong, also came close to understanding the Way. When gentlemen discuss its succession and hold that Master Cheng transmitted it to Guishan and Master Zhu to Mianzhai, is it because the learning of these two surpassed that of worthies such as Zhang and Shao? They accord them this recognition simply because one could transmit the learning of the Doctrine of the Mean and the Book of Changes, and the other could complete the Comprehensive Explanation of the Classics and Commentaries, each demonstrating genuine understanding. How could this be a settled judgment accepted by all under Heaven?
As for the learning of the two Cheng brothers, Huiweng compared Mingdao to Yan Hui and Yichuan to Mengzi. This was because Mingdao’s moral nature was magnanimous and his scope broad, while Yichuan’s temperament was firm and upright and his discernment of the patterns of principle meticulous: their respective moral bearings truly corresponded to those of these earlier sages. One favored You Dingfu, the other Yang Zhongli. Was this not also because each disciple’s bearing resembled his teacher’s? Yet, although the comparison of Mingdao with Yan Hui is indeed apt, Mengzi could not match Yichuan’s achievement in self-restraint, while Mengzi’s commanding talent was beyond Yichuan’s reach. If we examine the conduct of the two Cheng brothers…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之明道爲條例官不以爲浼而伊川作行
狀不載其事明道謂青苗猶可放過而伊
川於西監則一一較計焉是非兄弟有二
道也一則孔子之獵較爲兆一則孟子之
不見諸侯也而何害其爲同耶及以二程
之議論考之明道曰稟於天爲性感爲情
動爲心伊川曰自性之有形謂之心自性
之有動謂之情是則一以動爲心一以動
爲情若不侔矣然以近思録所載二程體
===
用寂感之說觀之則先儒謂紀錄之誤是
矣而二程豈有異說可駭者哉若夫朱子
謂學顏子入聖人爲近而不言孟子以爲
才高無可據之地也胡文定謂立志以明
道自期待而儕之希文不論其道而論其
志也希文豈足以並明道者耶若夫顏孟
所造皆幾於聖人充之則大矣養之則粹
矣此又顏孟所以自爲深造之學也合而
言之聖賢道統之傳孟子濬其流嘘其烟
punctuated: 之，明道爲條例官，不以爲浼，而伊川作行狀，不載其事；明道謂青苗猶可放過，而伊川於西監則一一較計焉。是非兄弟有二道也，一則孔子之獵較爲兆，一則孟子之不見諸侯也，而何害其爲同耶？及以二程之議論考之，明道曰：「稟於天爲性，感爲情，動爲心。」伊川曰：「自性之有形謂之心，自性之有動謂之情。」是則一以動爲心，一以動爲情，若不侔矣。然以近思録所載二程體用寂感之說觀之，則先儒謂紀錄之誤是矣，而二程豈有異說可駭者哉？若夫朱子謂學顏子入聖人爲近，而不言孟子，以爲才高，無可據之地也。胡文定謂立志以明道自期待，而儕之希文，不論其道而論其志也。希文豈足以並明道者耶？若夫顏孟所造，皆幾於聖人，充之則大矣，養之則粹矣，此又顏孟所以自爲深造之學也。合而言之，聖賢道統之傳，孟子濬其流，嘘其烟
translation_en:
…their conduct, Mingdao (Cheng Hao) served as an official in the Regulations Office without considering it a defilement, yet when Yichuan (Cheng Yi) wrote his account of Mingdao’s life, he omitted this service. Mingdao said that the Green Sprouts loan policy could still be let pass, whereas Yichuan, at the Western Supervisory Office [?], scrutinized each matter individually. This does not mean that the brothers followed two different Ways. The one resembled Confucius participating in competitive hunting to initiate reform; the other resembled Mencius refusing to seek audiences with the feudal lords. How could this prevent their Ways from being the same?

If we examine the two Cheng brothers’ pronouncements, Mingdao said: “What is received from Heaven is the nature; its response to stimuli is feeling; its activity is the mind.” Yichuan said: “The nature insofar as it has form is called the mind; the nature insofar as it has activity is called feeling.” Thus, one identifies activity with the mind, and the other identifies activity with feeling: they seem inconsistent. Yet, viewed in light of the two Cheng brothers’ explanations of substance and function, stillness and response, recorded in Reflections on Things at Hand (Jinsi lu), the earlier scholars were right to attribute this to an error in recording. How could the two Cheng brothers have held divergent doctrines that should alarm us?

Master Zhu said that following Master Yan offered a nearer approach to sagehood, but did not say this of Mencius, considering his talents so lofty that they afforded no foothold to rely upon. Hu Wending said that, in setting one’s aspirations, one should expect of oneself what Mingdao achieved; in placing Xiwen (Fan Zhongyan) alongside him, he was discussing their aspirations, not their attainment of the Way. How could Xiwen be worthy of standing on a par with Mingdao?

As for the attainments of Yan Hui and Mencius, both approached sagehood. By extending these attainments fully, they became great; by nurturing them, they became pure. This, too, was how Yan Hui and Mencius pursued learning through which they themselves attained profound understanding. Taken together, in the transmission of the succession to the Way of the sages and worthies, Mencius deepened its stream and fanned its smoke…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎周程揚其波熾其膏乎紫陽助其瀾烈
其焰乎彼吳草廬又分為元亨利貞之說
以論道統者豈其磨研六經疏滌百氏而
寓自任之意歟是固不可得而知也愚也
識見寡陋豈能於前脩氣象想像而旁通
之哉姑舉所聞於父師者以復而亦不詳
其是否也惟進而教之幸甚
第五問
梁津
===
同考試官教諭余批酌今古以理外患內政而歸于
得人通變多才識體之論咸可以觀矣
同考試官教諭曾批勢也者變之所由而德與謀所
以弭變之方也子能悉之其深於經濟哉
考試官教諭張批練達治體
考試官教授錢批宏濟之學
天下勢而已矣通其變可施不倦之神而
識其重須為亟反之策凡勢之將變其生
有旁根也其趨有邪徑也其流有頹波也
punctuated:
乎？周程揚其波、熾其膏乎？紫陽助其瀾、烈其焰乎？彼吳草廬又分為元亨利貞之說以論道統者，豈其磨研六經、疏滌百氏而寓自任之意歟？是固不可得而知也。愚也識見寡陋，豈能於前脩氣象想像而旁通之哉？姑舉所聞於父師者以復，而亦不詳其是否也。惟進而教之，幸甚！

第五問
梁津

同考試官教諭余批：酌今古以理外患內政，而歸于得人通變，多才識體之論，咸可以觀矣。
同考試官教諭曾批：勢也者，變之所由，而德與謀所以弭變之方也。子能悉之，其深於經濟哉！
考試官教諭張批：練達治體。
考試官教授錢批：宏濟之學。

天下勢而已矣。通其變，可施不倦之神；而識其重，須為亟反之策。凡勢之將變，其生有旁根也，其趨有邪徑也，其流有頹波也。
translation_en:
…? Did Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers raise its waves and kindle its oil? Did Ziyang (Zhu Xi) swell its billows and intensify its flames? As for Wu Caolu (Wu Cheng), who further discussed the transmission of the Way by distinguishing the categories of origination, flourishing, benefit, and firmness: was he expressing a sense of personal responsibility through his painstaking study of the Six Classics and his critical sifting of the hundred schools? This cannot, of course, be known. With my scant and shallow understanding, how could I envision the bearing of earlier worthies and thereby extend my comprehension? I merely offer in reply what I have heard from my father and teachers, without even knowing whether it is correct. I would be most fortunate if you would offer me further instruction.

Fifth Policy Question
Liang Jin

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: He weighs past and present in addressing external threats and internal administration, ultimately emphasizing the recruitment of suitable men and adaptation to change. His arguments display considerable ability and an understanding of the essentials of government; all merit attention.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: The configuration of circumstances gives rise to change, while virtue and planning provide the means to avert upheaval. You comprehend these fully—how profound your understanding of statecraft!
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Thoroughly versed in the essentials of government.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Professor: Learning capable of bringing broad benefit to the realm.

The affairs of the realm come down to the configuration of circumstances. By comprehending its changes, one can exercise an untiring, responsive efficacy; by recognizing its gravity, one must devise measures promptly to reverse its course. Whenever circumstances are about to change, their beginnings have lateral roots, their movement follows crooked paths, and their flow carries collapsing waves. …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其仆有敗脉也吾欲爲拯救肅清之方則
在顧乃德訏乃謨何也夫剛斷也者伐謀
之斧斤也中正也者救偏之繩墨也容忍
也者鎭浮之砥柱也惇大也者休否之靈
丹也以是四者隨時出之以爲之綱紀則
嬰盤錯而其鋒益厲矣乗叢雜而其界益
明矣施鼓撓而其風益震矣遇喧囂而其
聲益宏矣然則九州之事亦可决也八蠻
之人亦可化也而何廣東一省之事宜有
===
不可舉者耶且廣東之可患者曰黎峒曰
猺獞曰海寇曰番舶此外患之不可不備
者也曰屯田曰軍伍曰積穀曰徭役此內
政之不可不脩者也執事以是質諸生豈
以愚生長是邦而籌之必熟耶而生非桑
弦有志之人也顧嘗以董子爲政如調琴
瑟晦翁論事若持權衡之說而三覆之矣
請終言之瓊州中據黎峒誠皇甫規虺蛇
入室之喻也頃者黎佛二爲妖殺虜官軍
punctuated: 其仆有敗脉也。吾欲爲拯救肅清之方，則在顧乃德、訏乃謨。何也？夫剛斷也者，伐謀之斧斤也；中正也者，救偏之繩墨也；容忍也者，鎭浮之砥柱也；惇大也者，休否之靈丹也。以是四者隨時出之，以爲之綱紀，則嬰盤錯而其鋒益厲矣，乗叢雜而其界益明矣，施鼓撓而其風益震矣，遇喧囂而其聲益宏矣。然則九州之事亦可决也，八蠻之人亦可化也，而何廣東一省之事宜有不可舉者耶？且廣東之可患者，曰黎峒，曰猺獞，曰海寇，曰番舶，此外患之不可不備者也；曰屯田，曰軍伍，曰積穀，曰徭役，此內政之不可不脩者也。執事以是質諸生，豈以愚生長是邦，而籌之必熟耶？而生非桑弦有志之人也。顧嘗以董子爲政如調琴瑟、晦翁論事若持權衡之說，而三覆之矣。請終言之。瓊州中據黎峒，誠皇甫規虺蛇入室之喻也。頃者黎佛二爲妖，殺虜官軍。
translation_en:
…its collapse has underlying veins of decay. If I would devise a means to rescue the situation and restore order, it lies in attending to your virtue and enlarging your plans. Why is this? Firm decisiveness is the axe that strikes down hostile schemes; balance and rectitude are the measuring line that corrects deviations; tolerance and forbearance are the steadfast pillar that stills instability; generosity and magnanimity are the potent medicine that ends adversity. Deploy these four as circumstances require and make them the guiding principles of government. Then, when confronting tangled roots, their edge grows sharper; amid confused complexities, their distinctions become clearer; when agitation arises [?], their influence becomes more commanding; and amid clamour, their voice becomes more resonant. Thus even the affairs of the Nine Provinces can be resolved, and even the peoples of the eight barbarian regions can be transformed. What undertaking in the single province of Guangdong, then, could prove impossible to carry out?

Moreover, Guangdong’s sources of concern include the Li settlements, the Yao and Zhuang peoples, maritime raiders, and foreign ships: these are external threats against which preparations are indispensable. Military agricultural colonies, military ranks, grain reserves, and corvée labour are matters of internal administration that must be put in order. You, sir, have questioned us students about these matters. Is it because you suppose that, having grown up in this land, this ignorant student must have considered them thoroughly? Yet I am not a man whose aspirations were set upon the mulberry bow and its string [?]. Nevertheless, I have repeatedly pondered Master Dong’s saying that governing is like tuning the qin and se zithers, and Huiweng’s saying that deliberating on affairs is like holding a weighing beam and its weight. Allow me to complete my discussion.

The Li settlements occupy the interior of Qiongzhou: this truly accords with Huangfu Gui’s analogy of venomous snakes entering a house. Recently, the Li man Fo’er stirred up a rebellion through heterodox practices, killing and capturing government troops…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今雖生獲以快人心矣而黨與猶未革面
也明問謂搗穴窮巢以驅除之誠是也吾
謂生黎自昔不能爲患而所患者熟黎乃
荆湘福閩之亡命雜居者也夫荒服固所
不治而地利在所必爭若得金牛通道以
内立屯帥則宅中有圖大之勢而永絶禍
根顧自古無爲此說而事勢未可輕議也
則莫若於犬豕跳梁之境而決加
天討之兵若杜杞之擒破諸蠻趙絳之勦平三
===
峒以作我南方之干城其歸我聲教者若
韓璧之勞來不倦使供賦稅亦可也而豈
可拘一說哉廉州僻近交阯即馬伏波所
立銅柱表界之地也比年西山賊首恣行
劫掠今雖已勦滅以張
國威矣而餘孽猶未授首也明問謂鑿山刋
道以殄滅之誠是也吾謂猺賊不能爲患
而所患者浪賊乃本境奸宄之頑民交通
者也夫山險有所不由而地勢在所必守
punctuated:
今雖生獲以快人心矣，而黨與猶未革面也。明問謂搗穴窮巢以驅除之，誠是也。吾謂生黎自昔不能爲患，而所患者熟黎，乃荆湘福閩之亡命雜居者也。夫荒服固所不治，而地利在所必爭。若得金牛通道，以内立屯帥，則宅中有圖大之勢，而永絶禍根。顧自古無爲此說，而事勢未可輕議也。則莫若於犬豕跳梁之境，而決加天討之兵，若杜杞之擒破諸蠻、趙絳之勦平三峒，以作我南方之干城。其歸我聲教者，若韓璧之勞來不倦，使供賦稅亦可也，而豈可拘一說哉！
廉州僻近交阯，即馬伏波所立銅柱表界之地也。比年西山賊首恣行劫掠，今雖已勦滅以張國威矣，而餘孽猶未授首也。明問謂鑿山刋道以殄滅之，誠是也。吾謂猺賊不能爲患，而所患者浪賊，乃本境奸宄之頑民交通者也。夫山險有所不由，而地勢在所必守。
translation_en:
…Although he has now been captured alive, to the satisfaction of the people, his adherents have yet to show outward submission. Your illuminating question proposes striking their lairs and rooting out their nests in order to drive them away. This is certainly right. I would argue that the unassimilated Li have never themselves been capable of causing serious trouble; the concern is the assimilated Li, among whom fugitives from Jing, Xiang, Fu, and Min live intermingled. Although the remote outer zone properly lies beyond direct administration, strategically advantageous ground must be contested. If a passage could be opened through Jinniu and a garrison commander established within, occupying the center would provide a position from which to undertake larger plans and eradicate the roots of disaster forever. Yet no one since antiquity has advanced this proposal, and the circumstances do not admit of casual judgment. The best course, then, would be resolutely to send troops carrying out Heaven’s punishment into the territory where these dogs and swine run riot, following Du Qi in capturing and defeating the various Man peoples, and Zhao Jiang in suppressing the Three Dong, thereby providing a shield and bulwark for our south. As for those who submit to our civilizing influence, it would also be acceptable to follow Han Bi in tirelessly comforting and attracting them, and have them pay taxes. How could we confine ourselves to a single approach?
Lianzhou lies in a remote location near Jiaozhi; it is the very place where Ma, General Who Calms the Waves, erected bronze pillars to mark the boundary. In recent years the Xishan bandit leaders have plundered without restraint. Although they have now been destroyed, displaying the might of the state, their remaining followers have yet to surrender their heads. Your illuminating question proposes cutting through the mountains and opening roads in order to annihilate them. This is certainly right. I would argue that the Yao bandits cannot themselves cause serious trouble; the concern is the Lang bandits [?], with whom the lawless and recalcitrant people of this locality maintain contact. Some perilous mountain routes ought not to be traversed, but strategically important terrain must be held…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
若得屯衞星羅以把截要路則先人有制
人之心而永安黎庶顧于今無可爲計而
事勢未可妄論也則莫若於魚鹽貨市之
際而嚴禁交通之人如冷應徵之擒冶峒
獠林槩之選蠻籍兵以壯吾北門之鎖鑰
其服吾羈縻者若倉振之深入賊境示諭
禍福亦可也而豈可執一見哉海賊之雙
桅出沒明問曰漳民糶穀麥之害是也而
議者以爲有巡捕交通之弊蓋謂軍衞貪
===
鄙而受彼漳人之賄賂以縱出匣也頃者
雙桅大船
明詔所不容已盡毀矣豈能保無不測之虞耶
所以召之必有土人爲之窩隱以分贓而
使之然也莫若督軍兵之巡瞭戢官吏之
奸貪如蔡謨之戍八所以備季龍李寶之
備火箭以拒逆亮亦可矣至於葉義問之
請立寨主方信孺之先負賊舟亦一方經
畧之策豈可棄哉番舶之連年往來明問
punctuated:
若得屯衞星羅，以把截要路，則先人有制人之心，而永安黎庶。顧于今無可爲計，而事勢未可妄論也，則莫若於魚鹽貨市之際，而嚴禁交通之人。如冷應徵之擒冶峒獠、林槩之選蠻籍兵，以壯吾北門之鎖鑰；其服吾羈縻者，若倉振之深入賊境，示諭禍福，亦可也，而豈可執一見哉？

海賊之雙桅出沒，明問曰漳民糶穀麥之害，是也。而議者以爲有巡捕交通之弊，蓋謂軍衞貪鄙，而受彼漳人之賄賂，以縱出匣也。頃者雙桅大船，明詔所不容，已盡毀矣，豈能保無不測之虞耶？所以召之，必有土人爲之窩隱，以分贓而使之然也。莫若督軍兵之巡瞭，戢官吏之奸貪，如蔡謨之戍八所以備季龍、李寶之備火箭以拒逆亮，亦可矣。至於葉義問之請立寨主、方信孺之先負賊舟，亦一方經畧之策，豈可棄哉？番舶之連年往來，明問
translation_en:
…If garrisons could be established in a constellation of posts to block the strategic routes, we could seize the initiative and overawe others, securing lasting peace for the common people. Yet at present no workable plan is available, and the circumstances cannot be discussed rashly. The best course would therefore be to prohibit strictly those who communicate with the bandits through the markets for fish, salt, and other goods. We could follow Leng Yingzheng in capturing the Lao of Yedong, or Lin Gai in selecting soldiers from the registers of the Man peoples, thereby strengthening the defenses that serve as the lock and key of our northern gateway. To bring them under our loose-rein control, we could also follow Cang Zhen in penetrating deep into bandit territory and explaining the consequences of defiance and submission. How could we insist on just one approach?

Concerning the sea pirates’ two-masted vessels appearing and disappearing, your discerning question identifies the harm caused by the people of Zhang selling grain and wheat. This is correct. Yet commentators also identify collusion by the patrols charged with apprehending pirates. They mean that the military guards are corrupt and accept bribes from those people of Zhang, allowing them to venture out [?]. Recently, the large two-masted vessels forbidden by the imperial edict have all been destroyed. But can we guarantee that no unforeseen danger remains? What draws the pirates here must be local people who shelter and conceal them in exchange for a share of the spoils. The best course would be to supervise the troops’ patrols and lookout duties and curb the officials’ dishonesty and greed. We could follow Cai Mo, who stationed troops at eight locations to guard against Jilong, or Li Bao, who prepared fire arrows to resist the rebel Liang. As for Ye Yiwen’s request to appoint stockade commanders and Fang Xinru’s first carrying the pirates’ vessels [?], these too were strategies for managing the defense of a region. How could they be discarded? Concerning foreign trading vessels coming and going year after year, your discerning question…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
曰奇貨資軍餉之利是也而議者以為有
將來開釁之憂蓋恐往來頻數而覘我
中國之虛實以啓觸藩也比者交通番夷
恩詔所不赦若少警矣豈能保無意外之患耶
而所以致之則以番舶有商人為之嚮導
以圖利而使之然也莫若盛軍容以防閑
按舊法以抽稅如元佑之盡報物數而勿
疎隆興之納稅寬期以相愛亦可矣若夫
胡則之溺水貸錢馬亮之遣使招徠特一
===
時權宜之計豈可法哉今之屯政專委憲
臣以督理之每年如漕法為叅究之典誠
亦嚴矣而官軍之侵欺不已明問曰武弁
恃世襲而敢於為惡是也愚則曰下愚之
性見利則乾沒矣豈獨武弁為然哉昔凍
阿木之在欽州勤政務開屯田其與仲淹
屯陝州之法吾不知其相合與否也但今
之田非昔之田矣比年管屯僉事林希元
亦將屯田事宜奏
punctuated:
曰：「奇貨資軍餉之利。」是也。而議者以為有將來開釁之憂，蓋恐往來頻數，而覘我中國之虛實，以啓觸藩也。比者交通番夷，恩詔所不赦，若少警矣，豈能保無意外之患耶？而所以致之，則以番舶有商人為之嚮導，以圖利而使之然也。莫若盛軍容以防閑，按舊法以抽稅，如元佑之盡報物數而勿疎，隆興之納稅寬期以相愛，亦可矣。若夫胡則之溺水貸錢、馬亮之遣使招徠，特一時權宜之計，豈可法哉？
今之屯政，專委憲臣以督理之，每年如漕法為叅究之典，誠亦嚴矣。而官軍之侵欺不已，明問曰：「武弁恃世襲而敢於為惡。」是也。愚則曰：下愚之性，見利則乾沒矣，豈獨武弁為然哉？昔凍阿木之在欽州，勤政務，開屯田，其與仲淹屯陝州之法，吾不知其相合與否也。但今之田非昔之田矣。比年管屯僉事林希元，亦將屯田事宜奏
translation_en:
…says: “Exotic goods provide the benefit of resources for military provisions.” This is so. Yet those discussing the matter worry that this may provoke conflict in the future. They fear that frequent journeys back and forth will allow foreigners to spy out the strengths and weaknesses of our Central Kingdom and embolden them to breach our defenses. Recently, dealings with foreign peoples were excluded from the imperial amnesty. This seems to have provided some warning, but can we guarantee that no unforeseen trouble will arise? What brings these ships here is that merchants act as their guides in pursuit of profit. Nothing would be better than to display our military strength to keep them in check and collect duties according to established regulations. We could follow the practice of the Yuanyou era, requiring full declarations of the quantities of goods without laxity, and that of the Longxing era, allowing generous deadlines for paying duties as a gesture of goodwill. As for Hu Ze’s remission of debts following a drowning [?], or Ma Liang’s dispatch of envoys to attract traders, these were merely expedients for particular circumstances. How could they serve as standing models?
The administration of military agricultural colonies is now entrusted specifically to censorial officials for supervision. Each year there are procedures for impeachment and investigation, as under the regulations governing grain transport. These are indeed stringent. Yet encroachment and fraud by officers and soldiers continue unabated. Your discerning question says: “Military officers rely on their hereditary status and therefore dare to do evil.” This is so. In my humble view, however, it is the nature of the most foolish to pocket whatever profit they see. How could this be true of military officers alone? Formerly, when Dong Amu [?] was in Qinzhou, he attended diligently to government affairs and established military agricultural colonies. I do not know whether his methods accorded with those used by Zhongyan in establishing colonies in Shanzhou. But the fields of today are not those of former times. In recent years, Lin Xiyuan, the Assistant Surveillance Commissioner responsible for the colonies, also submitted to the throne proposals concerning the military agricultural colonies…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
准蓋酌今之宜而爲之策也以是潤澤而審處
之豈不臧乎今之軍政分委藩臬以督清
之各府又各有官以嚴清查之法誠亦備
矣而軍士之逃亡不止明問曰軍士苦輪
班而敢於在逃是也愚則曰軍衞之官惟
利是剥削雖不輪班亦豈能安其生哉昔
馮拯在端州而括隱丁其與張說因衞士
逃匿而募彍騎之法吾不知其相同與否
也但今之軍非昔之軍矣比年軍政條例
===
及清戎官建白亦已頒行遵守蓋參時之
弊而爲之處也以是恪守而力行之豈不
善乎積穀所以爲備荒之地也昔李悝立
平糴之法耿壽昌制常平之規其意皆有
可觀者矣而明問謂際留永豐等倉皆不
堪於久積則是贓罰惟取價值貯庫而何
以備荒歉也且不開貪吏囊橐之門哉愚
謂廣東地氣卑濕固不可積於彌年猶幸
連歲豐登亦不可濫於賑濟莫若以紙米
punctuated:
准，蓋酌今之宜而爲之策也。以是潤澤而審處之，豈不臧乎？今之軍政，分委藩臬以督清之，各府又各有官以嚴清查之法，誠亦備矣。而軍士之逃亡不止，明問曰：「軍士苦輪班而敢於在逃。」是也。愚則曰：軍衞之官惟利是剥削，雖不輪班，亦豈能安其生哉？昔馮拯在端州而括隱丁，其與張說因衞士逃匿而募彍騎之法，吾不知其相同與否也。但今之軍非昔之軍矣。比年軍政條例及清戎官建白，亦已頒行遵守，蓋參時之弊而爲之處也。以是恪守而力行之，豈不善乎？

積穀所以爲備荒之地也。昔李悝立平糴之法，耿壽昌制常平之規，其意皆有可觀者矣。而明問謂際留、永豐等倉皆不堪於久積，則是贓罰惟取價值貯庫，而何以備荒歉也？且不開貪吏囊橐之門哉？愚謂廣東地氣卑濕，固不可積於彌年；猶幸連歲豐登，亦不可濫於賑濟。莫若以紙米
translation_en:
…received approval; these proposals were presumably devised with due consideration for present circumstances. Would it not be good to refine them and give careful thought to their implementation? Responsibility for present military administration is divided between the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, which supervise the scrutiny of military registers. Each prefecture also has officials charged with enforcing rigorous inspections. These arrangements are indeed comprehensive. Yet soldiers continue to desert. Your discerning question states: “Soldiers suffer from rotational service and therefore dare to abscond.” This is true. In my humble view, however, the officers of the military guards exploit their men solely for profit. Even without rotational service, how could the soldiers live in peace? Formerly, when Feng Zheng was in Duanzhou, he sought out unregistered adult males. Whether his method resembled that of Zhang Yue, who recruited Guoqi cavalry when guardsmen fled into hiding, I do not know. But today’s armies are not those of former times. In recent years, regulations for military administration and proposals submitted by officials charged with scrutinizing military registers have already been promulgated for observance. These measures were presumably devised in light of contemporary abuses. Would it not be good to observe them conscientiously and implement them vigorously?

Storing grain provides a foundation for famine preparedness. In former times, Li Kui established the system of equitable grain purchases, and Geng Shouchang devised the rules for ever-normal granaries. The intentions behind both deserve consideration. Yet your discerning question states that granaries such as Jiliu [?] and Yongfeng are all unsuitable for prolonged storage. If confiscations and fines are therefore collected only at their monetary value and deposited in treasuries, how can provision be made against famine and poor harvests? Would this not also open the way for corrupt officials to line their pockets? In my humble view, Guangdong’s terrain is low-lying and its climate humid, so grain certainly cannot be stored for years. Fortunately, harvests have been abundant for successive years, and relief must not be distributed indiscriminately either. Nothing would be better than to use the “paper rice” [?]…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
罪穀每倉爲官軍俸粮之用而小民秋粮
夏稅每年爲減價折色之徵則軍民兩便
而適其宜矣與平糶常平何異哉均徭本
以供役也司馬公則主差役王介甫則主
於助役其言皆有所據者矣而明問謂弓
兵水夫等役皆不樂於親當則是徭役惟
取價值雇募而何以惠貧難也其不中積
年包攬之欲哉愚謂徭役之願於納價以
官吏得逞貪殘之由而官吏之遂於貪謀
===
亦由徭戶不願赴訴之故莫若以廣韶之
願納價者聽其貯官而不使之自募以雷
廉之願親當者聽其應役而不強其必同
則貧富兩便而得其所矣與差役助役何
異哉抑凡愚之所言者法也而所以爲之
要在由前所言剛斷之四事而實責之在
人也夫黎峒猺獞之出沒其責在兵備海
賊番舶之往來其責在海道屯政之脩廢
其責在管屯之僉憲軍伍之虛實其責在
punctuated: 罪穀，每倉爲官軍俸粮之用，而小民秋粮夏稅，每年爲減價折色之徵，則軍民兩便而適其宜矣，與平糶、常平何異哉？均徭本以供役也。司馬公則主差役，王介甫則主於助役，其言皆有所據者矣。而明問謂弓兵、水夫等役，皆不樂於親當，則是徭役惟取價值雇募，而何以惠貧難也？其不中積年包攬之欲哉？愚謂徭役之願於納價，以官吏得逞貪殘之由，而官吏之遂於貪謀，亦由徭戶不願赴訴之故。莫若以廣、韶之願納價者，聽其貯官，而不使之自募；以雷、廉之願親當者，聽其應役，而不強其必同。則貧富兩便而得其所矣，與差役、助役何異哉？抑凡愚之所言者，法也，而所以爲之，要在由前所言剛斷之四事，而實責之在人也。夫黎峒、猺獞之出沒，其責在兵備；海賊、番舶之往來，其責在海道；屯政之脩廢，其責在管屯之僉憲；軍伍之虛實，其責在
translation_en:
…use the grain collected as penalties in each granary to provide stipendiary grain for officers and soldiers, while each year collecting the common people's autumn grain levy and summer tax in commuted payments assessed at reduced prices. This would benefit both soldiers and civilians and suit their respective circumstances. How would it differ from sales at equitable prices and the Ever-Normal Granary system?

The equitable service system was originally intended to supply labor services. Lord Sima advocated assigned service, while Wang Jiefu advocated service financed by contributions; both had grounds for their arguments. Your discerning question states that people are unwilling to perform personally such services as those of archers and boatmen. If service obligations are therefore met solely by collecting payments and hiring substitutes, how can this benefit the poor and distressed? Would it not satisfy the desires of entrenched contractors who monopolize these arrangements? In my humble view, the preference for paying money in lieu of service provides officials and clerks with an opportunity to indulge their greed and cruelty [?]; their success in these greedy schemes also results from the unwillingness of service-liable households to lodge complaints. The best course would be to allow those in Guangzhou and Shaozhou who wish to pay money to deposit it with the authorities, without making them hire substitutes themselves; and to allow those in Leizhou and Lianzhou who wish to serve personally to fulfill their obligations, without insisting that all follow the same practice. This would benefit rich and poor alike and accommodate their circumstances. How would it differ from assigned service and service financed by contributions?

Yet all that I have proposed consists of regulations. The key to implementing them lies in proceeding with the four matters previously discussed as requiring firmness and decisiveness, and in placing actual responsibility upon individuals. Responsibility for the incursions and movements of the Li of the mountain settlements and the Yao and Zhuang rests with the military defense officials; responsibility for the movements of maritime raiders and foreign ships rests with the maritime circuit officials; responsibility for the maintenance or neglect of military agricultural colony administration rests with the Assistant Surveillance Commissioner supervising those colonies; responsibility for whether military ranks are actually filled or merely nominal rests with…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
清戎之藩臬量積穀之出入以便官民其
責在於粮儲均徭役之重輕以通民瘼其
責在於守令而所以使之爲氷蘖而不爲
溪壑爲保障而不爲繭絲爲胸中數萬甲
兵而不爲棘門兒戲則又在撫按公激揚
之論
廟堂決黜陟之權此地方大計肉食者之所
知也而豈藿食者所能曉其萬一哉狂瞽
之言未知是否惟執事與其進而教之
punctuated: 清戎之藩臬。量積穀之出入，以便官民，其責在於粮儲；均徭役之重輕，以通民瘼，其責在於守令。而所以使之爲氷蘖而不爲溪壑，爲保障而不爲繭絲，爲胸中數萬甲兵而不爲棘門兒戲，則又在撫按公激揚之論，廟堂決黜陟之權。此地方大計，肉食者之所知也，而豈藿食者所能曉其萬一哉？狂瞽之言，未知是否，惟執事與其進而教之。
translation_en: …the provincial administration and surveillance officials charged with reviewing military rolls. Regulating the receipts and disbursements of stored grain for the convenience of officials and people is the responsibility of the grain administration; equalizing the burdens of labor service to relieve the people’s distress is the responsibility of prefects and magistrates. Yet ensuring that these officials practice austere integrity, rather than become insatiable ravines; that they serve as protective bulwarks, rather than reel silk from the people’s cocoons; and that they hold tens of thousands of armored soldiers in their minds, rather than make military affairs child’s play as at Jimen—this further depends on the grand coordinator and regional inspector delivering impartial judgments of censure and commendation, and on the central government exercising its authority to decide dismissals and promotions. These great plans for the region are matters understood by those who eat meat and hold office. How could one who subsists on bean leaves understand even a ten-thousandth part of them? I do not know whether these rash and unenlightened words are right or wrong. I ask only that you, honored examiner, approve my willingness to come forward and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
昭哉我
國家以人文化成天下歲三閱
而取士其周之大比而賓興
者乎試之以文豈徒曰酌其
章哉有道存焉其關於治運
者懋乎其隆也槩嘗仰觀於
===
天俯察於地見其確然而示
人以易隤然而示人以簡迺
作而嘆曰休哉其文乎天之
精也地之英也人之粹也三
才之道一而莫之或遷也于
其易也唯其健也于其簡也
唯其順也有神焉以握其機
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

昭哉！我國家以人文化成天下，歲三閱而取士，其周之大比而賓興者乎？試之以文，豈徒曰酌其章哉？有道存焉，其關於治運者，懋乎其隆也。槩嘗仰觀於天，俯察於地，見其確然而示人以易，隤然而示人以簡，迺作而嘆曰：「休哉，其文乎！天之精也，地之英也，人之粹也。三才之道，一而莫之或遷也。于其易也，唯其健也；于其簡也，唯其順也。有神焉，以握其機
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

How illustrious! Our dynasty transforms and perfects all under Heaven through cultural refinement. Every three years it selects men for service: does this not follow the Zhou dynasty’s great triennial assessment, in which worthy men were honored as guests and recommended for office? In examining them through their writing, could the purpose merely be to weigh their literary ornament? The Way resides therein, and its bearing on the fortunes of government is exceedingly great. I once looked upward to contemplate Heaven and downward to examine Earth. I saw how Heaven, firm, shows people ease, and Earth, yielding, shows people simplicity. Thereupon I rose and exclaimed: “How splendid is this pattern! It is the essence of Heaven, the finest quality of Earth, and the purest quality of humanity. The Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—is one, and nothing can alter it. Heaven’s ease lies in its vigor; Earth’s simplicity lies in its compliance. There is a spiritual power that holds the key to their workings …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雖天地而弗得與其能也而
况於人乎哉夫塞其體也帥
其性也其心固天地之心也
由是而發之言措之業皆夫
人之文也文不足以觀士乎
哉仰惟我
聖上以天縱之資而紹帝王之學
===
兢兢焉存其心純其理於敬
一焉緝之則精一執中之傳
允乎其相承而建極以風乎
士心者固自有本也而文也
者所以徵乎其心也士生於
時得非其慶幸哉粲始應東
廣聘事若隱有懼者意其地
punctuated: 雖天地而弗得與其能也，而况於人乎哉！夫塞其體也，帥其性也，其心固天地之心也。由是而發之言，措之業，皆夫人之文也。文不足以觀士乎哉？仰惟我聖上以天縱之資而紹帝王之學，兢兢焉存其心，純其理，於敬一焉緝之，則精一執中之傳，允乎其相承，而建極以風乎士心者，固自有本也。而文也者，所以徵乎其心也。士生於時，得非其慶幸哉！粲始應東廣聘事，若隱有懼者，意其地
translation_en:
…Even Heaven and Earth cannot rival its capacity; how much less can human beings! It fills the body and commands its nature [?]; this mind is indeed the mind of Heaven and Earth. What proceeds from it in speech and is put into practice in undertakings is all the outward expression of the person. Is writing, then, insufficient for judging scholars?
Looking reverently upward, I reflect that our sage sovereign, with his Heaven-endowed gifts, carries forward the learning of emperors and kings. With vigilant care he preserves his mind and keeps its principles pure, cultivating these through reverent singleness of purpose. Thus the transmitted teaching of refinement, singleness, and holding fast to the Mean is truly continued in succession. His establishment of the supreme standard to influence scholars’ minds assuredly has its foundation. Writing is the means by which their minds may be examined. Is it not a blessing and a good fortune for scholars to live in such an age?
When I, Can, first accepted the invitation to serve in eastern Guangdong, I felt a certain unspoken apprehension, thinking that its territory…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
涉遐方士之心或未盡淑而
文弗之辨邪徐而校之則震
而弗靡其氣達也美而弗詭
其才華也雅而有倫其制典
也夫氣德之充也充則弗餒
而於理也直才德之焜也華
則弗涸而於理也澤制德之
===
準也典則弗雜而於理也純
三者集而心庶乎其亮矣槩
敬竦而嘆曰於猗哉
聖化之入人深也雖嶺海之遠猶
且翕焉而丕變則
中興之運於茲乎昭矣二三子
沐盛而起將奚以示我周行
punctuated: 涉遐方，士之心或未盡淑，而文弗之辨邪？徐而校之，則震而弗靡，其氣達也；美而弗詭，其才華也；雅而有倫，其制典也。夫氣，德之充也；充則弗餒，而於理也直。才，德之焜也；華則弗涸，而於理也澤。制，德之準也；典則弗雜，而於理也純。三者集，而心庶乎其亮矣。槩敬竦而嘆曰：「於猗哉！聖化之入人深也！雖嶺海之遠，猶且翕焉而丕變，則中興之運於茲乎昭矣。二三子沐盛而起，將奚以示我周行，
translation_en:
…lay in a distant region, where the hearts of the scholars might not yet be entirely good, and their writing might fail to reveal this? Yet, as I gradually examined their work, I found it vigorous without being extravagant, showing the free expression of their vital energy; beautiful without being strange, showing the brilliance of their talent; and elegant and orderly, showing the classical propriety of their literary form. Vital energy is the fullness of virtue: when full, it does not flag, and accords with principle in its uprightness. Talent is the radiance of virtue: when brilliant, it does not run dry, and accords with principle in its enriching influence. Literary form is the measure of virtue: when classically proper, it is free of admixture, and accords with principle in its purity. When these three come together, the heart approaches true illumination.
Moved to reverence and awe, I exclaimed: “Ah, splendid indeed! How deeply the sage emperor’s transforming influence penetrates people! Even in the distant lands of the Lingnan mountains and southern seas, all respond together and undergo a great transformation. Thus the flourishing fortunes of dynastic resurgence are made manifest here. You gentlemen, nurtured by this prosperity and now coming forward, how will you show me the great Way …

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以觀
國之光哉夫言之非艱行唯艱
行之非艱心唯艱薦書祗戒
必實錄其文者所以識其心
而要其行於終也矧邇者
聖諭太學務在惇本尚實勿徒專
事詞章使大道明而彝倫叙
===
用賛我
國家文明之化則拳拳致望於
天下士者至重至切二三子
得無念哉亦惟曰貞其心而
已矣蓋蘊諸心者為德性則
宣諸言者為德聲徴諸行者
為德業經而緯之造化在我
punctuated: 以觀國之光哉！夫言之非艱，行唯艱；行之非艱，心唯艱。薦書祗戒，必實錄其文者，所以識其心，而要其行於終也。矧邇者聖諭太學，務在惇本尚實，勿徒專事詞章，使大道明而彝倫叙，用賛我國家文明之化，則拳拳致望於天下士者，至重至切，二三子得無念哉？亦惟曰貞其心而已矣。蓋蘊諸心者為德性，則宣諸言者為德聲，徴諸行者為德業，經而緯之，造化在我。
translation_en: …so as to behold the glory of the realm! Speaking is not difficult; acting is difficult. Acting is not difficult; setting the heart right is difficult. In preparing the recommendation document with reverent caution, we faithfully record their compositions so as to discern their hearts and hold them to their conduct to the very end. Moreover, His Majesty recently instructed the Imperial University to concentrate on strengthening the foundations and valuing substance, rather than devoting itself solely to literary composition, so that the Great Way might be made clear and the enduring human relationships properly ordered, thereby assisting our state's civilizing transformation. His earnest expectations of the scholars throughout the realm are thus of the greatest weight and urgency. Can you gentlemen fail to keep them in mind? All that is required is to make your hearts steadfast and upright. For what is stored in the heart constitutes moral nature; what is expressed in words constitutes the voice of virtue; and what is manifested in conduct constitutes the achievements of virtue. By weaving these together as warp and weft, the power of creation and transformation lies within ourselves…

title: 嘉靖十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
必如是而后無愧於文也否
則而堅而辨率歸諸偽君子
恥之二三子得無念哉庶或
勉之固諸大夫主司願也遂
拜書于錄
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學教
諭張瓛謹序
===
必如是而后無愧於文也否
則而堅而辨率歸諸偽君子
恥之二三子得無念哉庶或
勉之固諸大夫主司願也遂
拜書于錄
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學教
諭張瓛謹序
punctuated:
必如是而后無愧於文也。否則，而堅而辨，率歸諸偽，君子恥之。二三子得無念哉？庶或勉之，固諸大夫主司願也。遂拜書于錄。

浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學教諭張瓛謹序。

浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學教諭張瓛謹序。
translation_en:
…Only in this way can one be worthy of literary expression. Otherwise, firmness and eloquence [?] alike lapse into falsity, which the gentleman regards as shameful. Can you gentlemen fail to give this thought? That you might strive toward this is indeed the wish of the gentlemen presiding over the examination. I therefore respectfully inscribe these words in the record.

Preface respectfully composed by Zhang Huan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.
